# FrameAssembly (`frameassembly`)

> Rust compiler (v1.2.2) that turns plain-text `.fasm` packet recipes into deterministic, nanosecond-accurate `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures across 81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols, with IPv4/IPv6 flow reuse, automatic TCP SEQ/ACK and reply-port tracking, and SNMPv3 USM (RFC 3414/3826/7860) cryptography. Built for network engineers who do not program; a companion to Wireshark/`tshark` (inspection) and `tcpreplay` (wire injection).

FrameAssembly (`https://github.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly`, `https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly`, `https://docs.rs/frameassembly`) synthesizes bit-exact, reproducible `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures in userspace with zero root privileges or live sockets required. Every protocol compiles with **zero mandatory sub-keywords** (emitting RFC-compliant wire defaults and ports) and supports explicit field and payload overrides.

### Zero-Shot `.fasm` Grammar & Anti-Hallucination Reference

1. **Three-Block Program Structure & Case-Insensitivity**: Every compilable `.fasm` file declares one or more `HOST <id> { IP <ip> [MAC <mac>] }` blocks, one or more parameterized `FLOW <id>(<param1>, <param2>, ...) { <statements> }` blocks, and one `COMPILE { <flow_calls_or_loops> }` block. All keywords, protocols, modifiers, time suffixes (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), and identifiers (`HOST`, `FLOW`, parameters) are ASCII case-insensitive (`host` or `HOST`).
2. **1 Statement = 1 Wire Frame & Shared 4-Tuple State**: Each statement (`<a> -> <b> <PROTO> ...` or `<a> <- <b> <PROTO> ...`) emits 1 frame. TCP-based L7 statements emit a `PSH ACK` segment on that protocol's well-known port and share 4-tuple `SEQ`/`ACK` counters and bidirectional port inheritance with raw `TCP` statements on the same connection.
3. **Dual-Stack Endpoint Homogeneity**: A `FLOW` is polymorphic across IPv4 and IPv6 host pairs, but both endpoints in any single statement must share the same IP family (both IPv4 or both IPv6).

| Construct | ❌ NEVER WRITE (Invalid / Hallucinated) | ✅ ALWAYS WRITE (Canonical `.fasm` Syntax) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Host Block** | `HOST c = { IPV4: "10.0.0.1", MASK: 24 }` | `HOST c { IP 10.0.0.1 MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55 }` |
| **Flow Signature** | `FLOW web { FROM c TO s SEND HTTP }` | `FLOW web(c, s) { c -> s HTTP GET URI "/" }` |
| **Return Direction** | `s -> c REVERSE TCP` or `REPLY s -> c` | `c <- s TCP SYN ACK` (or `s -> c TCP SYN ACK`) |
| **Inter-Frame Delay** | `[+5ms] c -> s TCP ACK` or standalone `WAIT 5ms` | `c -> s TCP ACK WAIT 5ms` (inline modifier; `ns`,`us`,`ms`,`s`,`m`) |
| **Ports & TCP Ack** | `SPORT 1234 DPORT 80 ACK 100` | `SRCPORT 1234 DSTPORT 80 SEQ 1 ACKNUM 100` |
| **TCP Flags** | `FLAGS [SYN, ACK]` or `FLAGS="SA"` | `TCP SYN ACK` (bare space-separated tokens: `SYN ACK FIN RST PSH URG ECE CWR`) |
| **IPv4/IPv6 Hop Limit** | `HOP_LIMIT 64` or `HOPLIMIT 255` | `TTL 64` or `TTL 255` (canonical across both IPv4 and IPv6) |
| **802.1ad QinQ Tags** | `QINQ 100 200` or `SVLAN 100 CVLAN 200` | `QINQ 100 INNER_VLAN 200` |
| **HTTP Host Header** | `c -> s HTTP GET HOST "example.com"` | `c -> s HTTP GET URI "/" HOST_HDR "example.com"` |
| **SNMP Request ID** | `REQ_ID 10` or `REQUEST_ID 10` | `REQID 10` |
| **Compile Block** | Bare `COMPILE` or `COMPILE { web }` | `COMPILE { web(client, server) LOOP 3 { web(client, server) } }` |

### Complete 81 Native Protocol Keywords by OSI Layer

- **Layer 2 (`8` protocols)**: `ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, `MPLS`.
- **Layer 3 (`20` protocols)**: `ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, `OPENFLOW`.
- **Layer 4 (`3` protocols)**: `TCP`, `UDP`, `SCTP`.
- **Layer 7 SNMP (`3` protocols)**: `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, `SNMP3` (9 `VARBIND <oid> <TYPE> <val>` types: `STRING`, `INT`, `COUNTER32`, `GAUGE32`, `TIMETICKS`, `COUNTER64`, `IPVAL`, `OIDVAL`, `NULLVAL`).
- **Layer 7 Infra & Telemetry (`11` protocols)**: `DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, `SFLOW`.
- **Layer 7 Web, Security, VoIP & Access (`16` protocols)**: `HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `STUN`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `SSDP`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`.
- **Layer 7 Mail, Auth, Storage, DB & Messaging (`14` protocols)**: `SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`.
- **Layer 7 Industrial ICS / SCADA / OT (`6` protocols)**: `MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, `OPCUA`.
- **Universal Frame Modifiers**: `SRCMAC <mac>`, `DSTMAC <mac>`, `ETHERTYPE <u16>`, `VLAN <1..4094> [PCP <0..7>] [DEI <0..1>]`, `QINQ <1..4094> [INNER_VLAN <1..4094>]`, `MPLS <label> [EXP <0..7>] [BOS <0..1>] [MPLS_TTL <u8>]`, `TTL <u8>`, `DSCP <0..63>`, `ECN <0..3>`, `FLOWLABEL <u32>`, `IPID <u16>`, `DF`, `MF`, `FRAGOFFSET <u16>`, `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>`, `TRANSPORT TCP|UDP`, `SEQ <u32>`, `ACKNUM <u32>`, `WIN <u16>`, `MSS <u16>`, `WSCALE <u8>`, `SACK_PERM`, `TSVAL <u32>`, `TSECR <u32>`, `URGENT <u16>`, `PAYLOAD "<str>"`, `HEXPAYLOAD "<hex>"`, `WAIT <int><ns|us|ms|s|m>`.

### Minimal Canonical `.fasm` Template & Public Rust API

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Stateful TCP 3-way handshake, HTTP/1.1 GET/200 OK, and SNMPv3 USM SHA-256/AES trap
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, TCP, SYN, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, MSS, WAIT, ACK, HTTP, GET, URI, HOST_HDR, STATUS, REASON, BODY, SNMP3, TRAP, USER, ENGINEID, AUTH, SHA256, PRIV, AES, OID, VARBIND, STRING, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Declare IPv4 endpoints
HOST client { IP 10.0.0.10 MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
HOST server { IP 10.0.0.80 MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }

// INSTRUCTION: Define stateful web and SNMPv3 flow
FLOW demo_flow(c, s) {
    c -> s TCP SYN SRCPORT 51234 DSTPORT 80 WIN 65535 MSS 1460 WAIT 1ms
    c <- s TCP SYN ACK WIN 65535 MSS 1460 WAIT 1ms
    c -> s TCP ACK WAIT 1ms
    c -> s HTTP GET URI "/health" HOST_HDR "api.internal" WAIT 5ms
    c <- s HTTP STATUS 200 REASON "OK" BODY "{\"ok\":true}" WAIT 2ms
    s -> c SNMP3 TRAP USER "admin" ENGINEID "80001f8880112233" AUTH SHA256 "authpass123" PRIV AES "privpass123" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "srv01" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile flow for client and server
COMPILE {
    demo_flow(client, server)
}
```

- **Public Rust Library Signatures (`frameassembly` crate v1.2.2)**:
  - `frameassembly::lexer::lex(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<SpannedToken<'_>>, CompilerError>`
  - `frameassembly::parser::parse_program(source: &str) -> Result<Program<'_>, CompilerError>` (runs `validate_semantics` automatically)
  - `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics<'a>(program: &Program<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
  - `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(program: &Program<'_>) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>` (returns `(raw_ethernet_frame_bytes, timestamp_ns)`)
  - `frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program<'_>, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
  - `frameassembly::error::CompilerError::{LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, BackendError}`

## Core Documentation

- [README & 81-Protocol Default Table](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/README.md): Above-the-fold 30-second quickstart, `tshark` output, tool comparison, RFC wire defaults table, and sub-keyword reference for all 81 protocols.
- [Architecture, Compiler Pipeline & Formal Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/architecture_and_grammar.md): Six-stage compiler pipeline (`logos` -> `winnow` -> AST -> semantic validator -> 4-tuple backend -> `pcap-file`), `HOST`/`FLOW`/`COMPILE` syntax, L2–L4 modifiers, and dual-stack polymorphism.
- [Layer 2 Switching & Data-Link Protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l2_protocols.md): Complete syntax and wire framing for `ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, and `MPLS` (248 verified examples).
- [Layer 3 Control, Tunneling, VPN & Routing Protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l3_protocols.md): Complete syntax and wire framing for `ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, and `OPENFLOW` (620 verified examples).
- [Layer 4 Transport Protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l4_transports.md): Stateful 4-tuple progression, bidirectional port inheritance, RFC 7323 TCP options, UDP checksums, and SCTP multi-chunk bundling for `TCP`, `UDP`, and `SCTP` (95 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 SNMPv1, SNMPv2c & SNMPv3 USM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_snmp.md): ASN.1 BER encoding, `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, and `SNMP3` USM authentication (`MD5`, `SHA`, `SHA256`, `SHA384`, `SHA512`), privacy encryption (`DES`, `AES`), and all 9 SMI `VARBIND` types (93 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Infrastructure, Time, AAA & Flow Telemetry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md): Complete reference for `DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, and `SFLOW` (341 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Web, Cloud-Native, Transport Security, VoIP & Remote Access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md): Complete reference for `HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `STUN`, and `SSDP` (496 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Mail, Directory, Storage, Databases & Message Brokers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md): Complete reference for `SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, and `AMQP` (434 verified examples).
- [Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS) & SCADA/OT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/l7_industrial_ot.md): Complete reference for `MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, and `OPCUA` (186 verified examples).
- [Multi-Protocol Topologies & Dual-Stack Architectures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md): Leaf-Spine EVPN-VXLAN, Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC, 5G Service-Based Architecture, MPLS L3VPN, and Purdue ICS substations (104 verified topologies).
- [Instruction-Tuning Q&A Synthesis & Constrained Decoding Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/docs/qa_synthesis_guide.md): Natural-Language Prompt to `.fasm` Q&A pairs, RLVR reward evaluation, and constrained decoding setup with EBNF, GBNF, and Lark.

## Formal Grammars & Constrained Decoding

- [ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/grammar.ebnf): Formal context-free EBNF specification covering all 81 protocols and 640 uppercase terminal keywords.
- [llama.cpp & XGrammar GBNF Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/frameassembly.gbnf): Constrained decoding grammar (`root ::= ...`) for `llama.cpp`, `vLLM`, `SGLang`, and `TensorRT-LLM`.
- [Lark / Outlines / llguidance CFG Grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/frameassembly.lark): Earley/LALR Context-Free Grammar (`start: ...`) for `Outlines`, `Guidance`, and `llguidance`.
- [Full Single-Fetch LLM Context Bundle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/llms-full.txt): Consolidated single-file bundle (`< 900 KB`) containing section manifest, all 11 documentation guides, formal grammars, AST specs, and representative `.fasm` corpus scenarios.

## Rust Compiler Architecture

- [Library Crate Root (`src/lib.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/lib.rs): Public Rust API entry point, protocol matrix, and library quickstart.
- [Structured Compiler Errors (`src/error.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/error.rs): `CompilerError` (`LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `BackendError`) with `miette` diagnostic spans.
- [Zero-Copy Lexer (`src/lexer/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/lexer/mod.rs): `logos 0.14` tokenizer defining all 640 uppercase keyword tokens, time units, IP/MAC/OID literals, and source spans.
- [AST Definitions (`src/ast/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/ast/mod.rs): Strongly-typed AST nodes and `*Spec` structs across `src/ast/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/`.
- [Two-Phase Combinator Parser (`src/parser/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/parser/mod.rs): `winnow 1.0` token-slice parser with protocol-scoped field dispatch and semantic validator.
- [Stateful 4-Tuple Backend (`src/backend/mod.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/backend/mod.rs): Flow expansion, `LOOP` unrolling, bidirectional port inheritance, TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` progression, and RFC 1112/2464 multicast MAC derivation.
- [Native Packet Framing (`src/packet.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/packet.rs): Ethernet/VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/IPv4/IPv6/TCP/UDP/SCTP framing and RFC 1071 / RFC 9260 CRC32c checksums.
- [PCAPNG Serializer (`src/pcap.rs`)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/src/pcap.rs): Nanosecond-resolution PCAPNG writer (`IfTsResol(9)`) via `pcap-file 2.0`.

# Public Rust Library API & Structured Compiler Diagnostics (`src/lib.rs` & `src/error.rs`)

- `frameassembly::lexer::lex(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<SpannedToken<'_>>, CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::parser::parse_program(source: &str) -> Result<Program<'_>, CompilerError>` (automatically runs `validate_semantics`)
- `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics<'a>(program: &Program<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
- `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(program: &Program<'_>) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>` (returns `(raw_ethernet_frame_bytes, timestamp_ns)`)
- `frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program<'_>, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
- `frameassembly::error::CompilerError`:
  - `CompilerError::LexError { src: NamedSource<String>, span: SourceSpan }` (`frameassembly::lexer::unrecognized_token`)
  - `CompilerError::ParseError { src: NamedSource<String>, span: SourceSpan, message: String }` (`frameassembly::parser::syntax_error`)
  - `CompilerError::SemanticError { src: NamedSource<String>, span: SourceSpan, message: String, help: String }` (`frameassembly::semantic::validation_error`)
  - `CompilerError::BackendError { message: String }` (`frameassembly::backend::generation_error`)

# Repository Overview (`README.md`)

# FrameAssembly (`frameassembly`)

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/frameassembly.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/frameassembly)
[![Docs.rs](https://docs.rs/frameassembly/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/frameassembly)
[![Rust 1.85+](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B%20(Edition%202024)-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

[**Quickstart**](#quickstart) • [**Why FrameAssembly?**](#why-frameassembly) • [**Syntax Guide**](#syntax-guide) • [**All 81 Protocols (Defaults)**](#supported-protocols--default-wire-behavior) • [**Sub-Keyword Reference**](#exhaustive-protocol--sub-keyword-reference-all-81-protocols) • [**Documentation**](#documentation)

**FrameAssembly** (`frameassembly` v1.2.2) builds standard `.pcap` and `.pcapng` packet capture files from readable plain-text descriptions (`.fasm`) across **81 network protocols spanning Layers 2 through 7**.

You define the hosts in your scenario and list the frames exchanged between them using familiar networking terms—IPs, MACs, VLAN tags, TCP flags, routing attributes, or application fields. FrameAssembly handles the binary packet framing, byte lengths, checksums, and TCP sequence tracking automatically, producing a clean `.pcap` file ready to inspect in **Wireshark** / `tshark` or send onto a network interface with **`tcpreplay`**.

---

## Why FrameAssembly?

Tools like **Wireshark** and **`tcpdump`** record traffic that already exists on a network, and **`tcpreplay`** transmits existing `.pcap` files over a network interface—but neither helps when the packet capture you need doesn't exist yet.

Building custom `.pcap` files from scratch usually forces an awkward trade-off:
* **Writing Python scripts (`Scapy`)** and manually managing TCP sequence numbers, return ports, and nested protocol objects in code.
* **Editing raw hex dumps (`text2pcap`)** where changing a single field breaks byte offsets, header lengths, and checksums.
* **Building a physical or virtual lab** just to capture a specific protocol handshake, error condition, or alert—while filtering out background LAN chatter.

FrameAssembly gives you direct, bit-level control over packet headers through a readable text format that looks like a network diagram:

* **Test firewalls, ACLs, and IDS/IPS sensors:** Craft exact TCP flag combinations, blocked-port probes, fragmented IPv4 packets, or double-tagged VLAN/QinQ frames and replay them against an appliance with `tcpreplay`.
* **Verify monitoring, SIEM, and flow collectors:** Generate valid SNMPv1/v2c/v3 traps, Syslog alerts, or NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow exports without waiting for real hardware faults.
* **Simulate routing, overlays, VoIP, and OT/SCADA traffic:** Build BGP, OSPF, VXLAN, IPsec, WireGuard, TLS 1.3, SIP/RTP, or industrial PLC captures (Modbus, S7comm, DNP3, OPC UA) without physical lab equipment.
* **Share reproducible, zero-noise captures:** Check a 15-line `.fasm` text file into Git or attach it to a ticket instead of passing around noisy binary `.pcap` dumps.

| Capability | FrameAssembly (`.fasm`) | Python (`Scapy`) | `text2pcap` / Hex Editors | Live Lab Capture (`tcpdump`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **How Traffic Is Defined** | Plain-text host & packet lines | Python scripts | Raw hexadecimal byte dumps | Live devices or VMs |
| **Scripting / Coding Needed** | **None** — standard networking terms | Python programming required | Manual hex & byte-offset math | Full lab/device configuration |
| **Low-Level Header Control** | Any L2–L7 field (VLANs, flags, QoS, TTL, payloads) | Nested code constructors | Manual bit-by-bit hex editing | Difficult to force edge cases |
| **Unset Optional Fields** | Filled with valid RFC defaults automatically | Varies by layer | None (every byte written by hand) | OS / device dependent |
| **TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` & Return Ports** | **Tracked & swapped automatically** | Manual math per packet | Manual hex recalculation | Handled by OS kernel |
| **Checksums, Lengths & Crypto** | **Automatic** (IP, L4, CRC32c, ASN.1, SNMPv3) | Manual setup for stateful/crypto | Limited dummy headers | Handled by OS / NIC |
| **Privileges & Capture Noise** | Normal user; **zero background noise** | Root needed for raw socket send | Normal user | Root required; includes LAN chatter |

---

## Quickstart

### 1. Install `frameassembly`

**Cross-Platform Installer (Linux, macOS & BSDs):**
Checks for required build tools, sets up the Rust toolchain if missing, installs `frameassembly` from Crates.io, and installs the VS Code `.fasm` syntax extension if `code` is on `PATH`:

```bash
curl -fsSL [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh) | sh
```

**Or install directly via Cargo (Rust `>= 1.85`):**

```bash
cargo install frameassembly
```

### 2. Write a Traffic Specification (`demo.fasm`)

Every protocol works out of the box with standard RFC defaults—you only write the fields you want to customize:

```frameassembly
// Define the endpoints
host client { ip 10.0.0.10 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host server { ip 10.0.0.80 mac aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }

// List the packets exchanged between them (1 line = 1 frame)
flow web_session(c, s) {
    c -> s tcp syn srcport 51234 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack wait 1ms
    c -> s http get uri "/index.html" host_hdr "example.com" wait 5ms
    c <- s http status 200 reason "OK" body "<h1>Hello</h1>" wait 2ms
}

// Build the capture
compile {
    web_session(client, server)
}
```

### 3. Compile to `.pcap`, Inspect & Replay

```console
$ frameassembly demo.fasm -o output.pcap
Successfully parsed 2 hosts, 1 flows
Starting PCAP compilation...
Successfully generated output.pcap

$ tshark -r output.pcap
    1 0.000000000    10.0.0.10 → 10.0.0.80    TCP 58 51234 → 80 [SYN] Seq=0 Win=65535 Len=0 MSS=1460
    2 0.001000000    10.0.0.80 → 10.0.0.10    TCP 58 80 → 51234 [SYN, ACK] Seq=0 Ack=1 Win=65535 Len=0 MSS=1460
    3 0.002000000    10.0.0.10 → 10.0.0.80    TCP 54 51234 → 80 [ACK] Seq=1 Ack=1 Win=65535 Len=0
    4 0.003000000    10.0.0.10 → 10.0.0.80    HTTP 97 GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
    5 0.008000000    10.0.0.80 → 10.0.0.10    HTTP 126 HTTP/1.1 200 OK  (text/html)
```

Once verified in Wireshark or `tshark`, you can transmit the `.pcap` over a live network interface with `tcpreplay`:

```bash
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 output.pcap
```

What FrameAssembly handled behind the scenes:
* **Return Port Swapping:** `51234 -> 80` on `c -> s` automatically reversed to `80 -> 51234` on `c <- s` without retyping port numbers.
* **Automatic TCP `SEQ` & `ACK` Progression:** The `http` request and response automatically reused the established TCP session, emitted `PSH, ACK` segments, and incremented `Seq` and `Ack` counters by exact payload byte lengths.
* **Checksums & Nanosecond Timing:** Ethernet headers, IPv4/TCP checksums, HTTP `Content-Length`, and `wait` timestamp offsets (`0.001s`, `0.002s`, `0.003s`, `0.008s`) were calculated automatically.

---

## Syntax Guide

### 1. `host`, `flow` & `compile` Blocks

FrameAssembly syntax is completely **case-insensitive** across all keywords, protocol names, modifiers, time units (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), and identifiers (`host` or `HOST`, `tcp` or `TCP`). Single-line comments start with `//`.

* **`host <name> { ip <address> [mac <mac>] }`**: Binds a symbolic name to an IPv4 or IPv6 address. If `mac` is omitted, a deterministic unicast MAC—or RFC 1112 (`01:00:5e:...`) / RFC 2464 (`33:33:...`) multicast MAC for multicast IPs—is derived automatically.
* **`flow <name>(<param1>, <param2>, ...) { ... }`**: Defines a reusable sequence of packets:
  * `A -> B`: `A` is the sender (source), `B` is the receiver (destination).
  * `A <- B`: `B` is the sender (source), `A` is the receiver (destination).
* **`compile { ... }`**: Generates packets by passing concrete hosts into your flows. Because flows don't hardcode IPv4 vs. IPv6, the same flow can be run with IPv4 hosts and IPv6 hosts, and repeated inside `loop <count> { ... }`:

```frameassembly
host client_v4  { ip 192.168.1.50 }
host server_v4  { ip 192.168.1.100 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }
host client_v6  { ip 2001:db8::10 }
host server_v6  { ip 2001:db8::100 }
host mdns_mcast { ip 224.0.0.251 }

flow tcp_handshake(client, server) {
    client -> server tcp syn srcport 50100 dstport 443 win 65535
    client <- server tcp syn ack win 65535 wait 1ms
    client -> server tcp ack wait 1ms
}

flow mdns_probe(node, mcast) {
    node -> mcast mdns query qname "_http._tcp.local" qtype "PTR" wait 2ms
}

compile {
    loop 2 {
        tcp_handshake(client_v4, server_v4)
        tcp_handshake(client_v6, server_v6)
    }
    mdns_probe(client_v4, mdns_mcast)
}
```

### 2. Universal Layer 2–4 Modifiers

Any packet statement can include Layer 2, Layer 3, Layer 4, payload, and timing modifiers—allowing you to wrap upper-layer protocols inside VLAN trunks, QinQ service tags, MPLS label stacks, QoS markings, or fragmented IPv4 packets:

| Category | Modifiers | Wire Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Layer 2** | `SRCMAC <mac>`, `DSTMAC <mac>` | Override outer Ethernet source or destination MAC address |
| | `ETHERTYPE <u16>` | Override outer Ethernet Type field (e.g. `0x8100`, `0x8847`) |
| | `VLAN <1..4094> [PCP <0..7>] [DEI <0..1>]` | Add IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tag, priority (`PCP`), and drop indicator (`DEI`) |
| | `QINQ <1..4094> [INNER_VLAN <1..4094>]` | Add IEEE 802.1ad outer S-VLAN tag + inner C-VLAN tag |
| | `MPLS <label> [EXP <0..7>] [BOS <0..1>] [MPLS_TTL <u8>]` | Add MPLS shim header (`0x8847`) with label, Traffic Class, BOS, and TTL |
| **Layer 3** | `TTL <0..255>` | Set IPv4 Time-To-Live or IPv6 Hop Limit |
| | `DSCP <0..63>`, `ECN <0..3>` | Set DiffServ QoS Code Point (e.g. `46` = EF) and ECN congestion bits |
| | `FLOWLABEL <0..1048575>` | Set 20-bit IPv6 Flow Label (ignored on IPv4 statements) |
| | `IPID <u16>`, `DF`, `MF`, `FRAGOFFSET <u16>` | Set IPv4 Identification, Don't Fragment, More Fragments, and 8-byte offset |
| **Layer 4** | `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>` | Override TCP, UDP, or SCTP source and destination port numbers |
| | `TRANSPORT TCP \| UDP` | Force TCP or UDP for dual-mode protocols (`DNS`, `SIP`, `NFS`, `SYSLOG`) |
| | `SEQ <u32>`, `ACKNUM <u32>`, `WIN <u16>` | Override TCP sequence number, ack number, and window size |
| | `MSS <u16>`, `WSCALE <u8>`, `SACK_PERM` | Add TCP Maximum Segment Size, Window Scale, and SACK Permitted options |
| | `TSVAL <u32>`, `TSECR <u32>`, `URGENT <u16>` | Set TCP Timestamps and Urgent Pointer |
| **Payload** | `PAYLOAD "<string>"` | Append text payload (supports `\r`, `\n`, `\t`, `\xHH` escapes) |
| | `HEXPAYLOAD "<hex>"` | Append raw hexadecimal bytes (e.g. `"deadbeef"`) |
| **Timing** | `WAIT <duration>` | Advance `.pcap` capture timestamp after emitting frame (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`) |

### 3. Combining Cross-Layer Encapsulation & Application Protocols

```frameassembly
host branch_cpe { ip 10.220.1.10  mac 00:50:56:c0:01:10 }
host hq_gateway { ip 10.220.1.200 mac 00:50:56:c0:01:c8 }

// TLS 1.3 handshake carried over QinQ (2000/150) + MPLS (Label 40960) + DSCP EF (46)
flow metro_backhaul_tls(cpe, hq) {
    cpe -> hq qinq 2000 inner_vlan 150 pcp 6 mpls 40960 exp 6 bos 1 mpls_ttl 64 dscp 46 ttl 64 tls client_hello sni "vault.hq.example.com" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 5ms
    cpe <- hq qinq 2000 inner_vlan 150 pcp 6 mpls 40960 exp 6 bos 1 mpls_ttl 63 dscp 46 ttl 63 tls server_hello ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 5ms
}

compile {
    metro_backhaul_tls(branch_cpe, hq_gateway)
}
```

### 4. CLI & Editor Options

```bash
# Default output is output.pcap, or specify a path with -o / --output
frameassembly demo.fasm -o output.pcap

# Install only the VS Code .vsix syntax highlighting extension without cloning:
curl -fsSLo /tmp/frameassembly.vsix [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/frameassembly-vscode/frameassembly-vscode-1.2.2.vsix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/frameassembly-vscode/frameassembly-vscode-1.2.2.vsix) && code --install-extension /tmp/frameassembly.vsix && rm -f /tmp/frameassembly.vsix
```

## Supported Protocols & Default Wire Behavior

Every protocol can be used with **zero mandatory sub-keywords**, emitting RFC-compliant default wire headers when optional fields are omitted:

| Protocol | Layer | Transport | Default Port | Default Wire Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ARP` | L2 | Ethernet (`0x0806`) | N/A | Request, Hardware `1` (Ethernet), Protocol `0x0800` (IPv4); uses ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation on IPv6. |
| `VLAN` | L2 | Ethernet (`0x8100`) | N/A | IEEE 802.1Q tag, default VLAN ID `100`, `PCP 0`, `DEI 0`. |
| `QINQ` | L2 | Ethernet (`0x88A8`) | N/A | IEEE 802.1ad outer tag (`VLAN 100`) + 802.1Q inner tag (`VLAN 200`). |
| `LLDP` | L2 | Ethernet (`0x88CC`) | N/A | Multicast `01:80:c2:00:00:0e`, Chassis ID & Port ID TLVs, `TTL 120s`, End TLV. |
| `STP` | L2 | LLC/SNAP (`0x4242`) | N/A | Multicast `01:80:c2:00:00:00`, Configuration BPDU, Root ID, Bridge ID, `Cost 0`. |
| `LACP` | L2 | Ethernet (`0x8809`) | N/A | Multicast `01:80:c2:00:00:02`, Actor Info & Partner Info TLVs, Collector TLV. |
| `EAPOL` | L2 | Ethernet (`0x888E`) | N/A | IEEE 802.1X Version `1`, EAP-Packet Identity request/response. |
| `MPLS` | L2.5 | Ethernet (`0x8847`) | N/A | Label `16`, `EXP 0`, `BOS 1`, `TTL 64` unicast shim header. |
| `ICMP` | L3 | IP proto `1` / `58` | N/A | Echo Request (Type `8` for IPv4, Type `128` for IPv6), `ID 1`, `Seq 1`. |
| `NDP` | L3 | IPv6 ICMPv6 (`58`) | N/A | Neighbor Solicitation (Type `135`), Hop Limit `255`. |
| `IGMP` | L3 | IPv4 proto `2` | N/A | Membership Query to `224.0.0.1` (All Hosts), Max Resp Time `10.0s`. |
| `MLD` | L3 | IPv6 ICMPv6 (`58`) | N/A | Multicast Listener Query (Type `130`) to `ff02::1`. |
| `GRE` | L3 | IP proto `47` | N/A | GRE Version `0`, Protocol Type `0x0800` (IPv4) / `0x86DD` (IPv6). |
| `VXLAN` | L3 | UDP | `4789` | Flags `0x08` (`I` flag), 24-bit `VNI 1000`, 8-byte VXLAN header + inner frame. |
| `GENEVE` | L3 | UDP | `6081` | Version `0`, 24-bit `VNI 1000`, Protocol Type `0x6558` (Ethernet). |
| `IPSEC` | L3 | IP proto `50` | N/A | `SPI 0x1000`, `Sequence 1`, default ESP wire header. |
| `ESP` | L3 | IP proto `50` | N/A | Encapsulating Security Payload, `SPI 0x1000`, `Sequence 1`. |
| `AH` | L3 | IP proto `51` | N/A | Authentication Header, `SPI 0x1000`, `Sequence 1`, 96-bit ICV. |
| `IKEV2` | L3 | UDP | `500` | `SA_INIT` exchange (Type `34`), Initiator SPI set, Responder SPI `0`. |
| `WIREGUARD` | L3 | UDP | `51820` | Handshake Initiation message (Type `1`), Sender index `1`. |
| `OSPF` | L3 | IP proto `89` | N/A | OSPFv2 (IPv4) or OSPFv3 (IPv6) Hello packet, Area `0.0.0.0`, to `224.0.0.5` / `ff02::5`. |
| `BGP` | L3 | TCP | `179` | BGP-4 16-byte marker, `OPEN` message, `ASN 65001`, Hold Time `180s`. |
| `RIP` | L3 | UDP | `520` | RIPv2 Response (Command `2`), Version `2`, Route AFI `2` (IP), Metric `1`. |
| `VRRP` | L3 | IP proto `112` | N/A | VRRPv3 Advertisement, `VRID 1`, `Priority 100`, `TTL 255`. |
| `HSRP` | L3 | UDP | `1985` | Cisco HSRP Hello, State Active, `Group 1` to `224.0.0.2`. |
| `PIM` | L3 | IP proto `103` | N/A | PIM-SM Hello message, `DR Priority 1` to `224.0.0.13` / `ff02::d`. |
| `BFD` | L3 | UDP | `3784` | Single-hop Control packet, State `Up`, Detect Mult `3`, Min TX/RX `1000ms`. |
| `OPENFLOW` | L3 | TCP | `6653` | OpenFlow 1.3 (`0x04`) Hello / Features Request, `XID 1`. |
| `TCP` | L4 | IP proto `6` | `80` | Sequence numbers auto-incremented, `ACK` numbers tracked across reverse arrows. |
| `UDP` | L4 | IP proto `17` | `80` | Stateless UDP datagram with computed RFC 768 checksum. |
| `SCTP` | L4 | IP proto `132` | `80` | Verification Tag `0`, `DATA` chunk, `TSN 1`, `Stream 0`, CRC32c checksum. |
| `SNMP1` | L7 | UDP | `162` / `161` | Community `"public"`, `sysUpTime 0`, Trap/Poll PDU, RFC 1157 BER encoding. |
| `SNMP2` | L7 | UDP | `162` / `161` | Community `"public"`, `sysUpTime 0`, Trap/Poll PDU, RFC 3416 BER encoding. |
| `SNMP3` | L7 | UDP | `161` / `162` | USM security model, RFC 3414 / 3826 / 7860 authentication & privacy engine. |
| `DNS` | L7 | UDP / TCP | `53` | Standard Query, `TXID 0x1234`, `QNAME "example.com"`, `QTYPE A` / `AAAA`. |
| `MDNS` | L7 | UDP | `5353` | Multicast DNS Query (`TXID 0`) to `224.0.0.251` / `ff02::fb`. |
| `DHCP` | L7 | UDP | `67`/`68` (`546`/`547` v6) | `DHCPDISCOVER` (IPv4) or `Solicit` (IPv6) with client MAC. |
| `NTP` | L7 | UDP | `123` | Mode `3` (Client), Version `4`, Stratum `0`, Poll `4`. |
| `PTP` | L7 | UDP | `319` / `320` | IEEE 1588-2008 Version `2` `Sync` message, Domain `0`. |
| `RADIUS` | L7 | UDP | `1812` / `1813` | `Access-Request` (Code `1`, port `1812`; Accounting on `1813`), `Identifier 1`. |
| `TACACS` | L7 | TCP | `49` | TACACS+ Authentication Start, `Session ID 0x12345678`. |
| `SYSLOG` | L7 | UDP / TCP | `514` | RFC 5424 PRI `<14>` (Facility `1` User, Severity `6` Info), `APP "frameassembly"`. |
| `NETFLOW` | L7 | UDP | `2055` | Cisco NetFlow v5 Flow Record export packet. |
| `IPFIX` | L7 | UDP | `4739` | RFC 7011 IPFIX Observation Domain & Data Record packet. |
| `SFLOW` | L7 | UDP | `6343` | sFlow v5 Flow Sample datagram. |
| `TFTP` | L7 | UDP | `69` | Read Request (`RRQ`), `Filename "file.bin"`, `Mode "octet"`. |
| `FTP` | L7 | TCP | `21` | Greeting banner `"220 FTP Server Ready\r\n"` or control command. |
| `SSH` | L7 | TCP | `22` | Identification banner `"SSH-2.0-FrameAssembly_1.0\r\n"`. |
| `TELNET` | L7 | TCP | `23` | IAC `WILL`/`DO` negotiation bytes (`\xff\xfb...`). |
| `HTTP` | L7 | TCP | `80` | `GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: <host>\r\n\r\n`. |
| `HTTP2` | L7 | TCP | `443` | 24-byte client connection preface (`PRI * HTTP/2.0...`) + `SETTINGS` frame. |
| `GRPC` | L7 | TCP | `50051` | Length-prefixed gRPC frame over HTTP/2 (`application/grpc`). |
| `WEBSOCKET`| L7 | TCP | `80` | RFC 6455 WebSocket frame with optional client masking. |
| `TLS` | L7 | TCP | `443` | TLS 1.3 `ClientHello` with `SNI` and `supported_versions` extensions. |
| `QUIC` | L7 | UDP | `443` | QUIC v1 `Initial` packet or 1-RTT `Short` packet. |
| `STUN` | L7 | UDP | `3478` | Binding Request, RFC 8489 Magic Cookie `0x2112A442`. |
| `SIP` | L7 | UDP / TCP | `5060` | `INVITE sip:bob@domain SIP/2.0\r\n...`. |
| `RTP` | L7 | UDP | `5004` | RTP Version `2`, Payload Type `0` (PCMU), `Seq 1`, `Timestamp 0`. |
| `RTSP` | L7 | TCP | `554` | `DESCRIBE rtsp://server/media RTSP/1.0\r\n...`. |
| `SMTP` | L7 | TCP | `25` | `EHLO mail.example.com\r\n`. |
| `IMAP` | L7 | TCP | `143` | `A001 CAPABILITY\r\n`. |
| `POP3` | L7 | TCP | `110` | `+OK POP3 server ready\r\n` or `USER`/`PASS` command. |
| `KERBEROS` | L7 | UDP / TCP | `88` | Kerberos v5 `AS-REQ` for `krbtgt` ticket. |
| `LDAP` | L7 | TCP | `389` | LDAPv3 `BindRequest` (Simple) or `SearchRequest` message. |
| `SMB` | L7 | TCP | `445` | SMB2/3 `Negotiate Protocol Request`. |
| `NFS` | L7 | TCP / UDP | `2049` | ONC-RPC NFSv4 `NULL` / `COMPOUND` call. |
| `REDIS` | L7 | TCP

# Repository Agent Guide (`AGENTS.md`)

# AGENTS.md — FrameAssembly AI Agent & LLM Onboarding Guide

**FrameAssembly** (`frameassembly` v1.2.2) is a Rust 2024 Domain-Specific Language (DSL) and optimizing compiler that compiles declarative `.fasm` network traffic specifications into deterministic, nanosecond-precision `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet captures across **81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols** (`2,611` verified `.fasm` corpus scenarios).

---

## 1. Quick Build, Test & Verification Commands

```bash
# Cross-platform bootstrap install (curl + C linker + rustup >= 1.85 + cargo install)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh | sh

# Build compiler and CLI binary
cargo build --release

# Run all unit, integration, and corpus verification tests
cargo test

# Run the corpus verification suite (validates all 2,611 examples/**/*.fasm headers, AST parsing & PCAP output)
cargo test --test corpus_verification_tests

# Compile a single .fasm specification to a .pcap file
cargo run -- demo.fasm -o output.pcap
```

---

## 2. Unified `<layer>/<protocol>` Repository Architecture

FrameAssembly enforces strict structural symmetry across `src/`, `examples/`, and `docs/`:

- **`src/lexer/mod.rs`**: Zero-copy `logos 0.14` tokenizer defining `Token<'a>` for all 81 protocols, L2–L4 modifiers, SNMP USM parameters, time units (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), IPv4/IPv6, MAC, and OID literals.
- **`src/ast/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Strongly-typed AST node and `*Spec` definitions. Every AST type includes a `/// Syntax mapping: \`...\`` docstring binding the Rust type to its `.fasm` grammar.
- **`src/parser/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Two-phase `winnow 1.0` token-slice (`Stream<'i, 'a>`) combinator parsers and semantic validator (`validate_semantics` in `src/parser/mod.rs`).
- **`src/builders/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/<protocol>.rs`**: Zero-heap wire payload encoders and `src/builders/l7/snmp/` (`builder.rs`, `crypto.rs`) for RFC 1157 / 3416 / 3414 / 3826 / 7860 BER and USM encryption.
- **`src/backend/mod.rs` & `src/packet.rs` & `src/pcap.rs`**: 4-tuple TCP sequence/acknowledgment progression, bidirectional port inheritance across `->` and `<-`, multicast MAC derivation (RFC 2464 `33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx` and RFC 1112 `01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`), and `pcap-file 2.0` PCAPNG serialization.
- **`examples/{l2,l3,l4,l7,topologies}/`**: Verified `.fasm` corpus (`2,611` files) organized by `<layer>/<protocol>/<protocol>_<scenario>.fasm`.
- **`docs/*.md`**: Chunked (`< 50 KB` each) Markdown protocol reference and instruction-tuning guides:
  - [`docs/architecture_and_grammar.md`](docs/architecture_and_grammar.md) — Five-stage compiler pipeline, `HOST`/`FLOW`/`COMPILE` syntax, L2–L4 modifiers, dual-stack polymorphism, and formal grammar overview.
  - [`docs/l2_protocols.md`](docs/l2_protocols.md) — Layer 2 switching & data-link protocols (`ARP`, `VLAN`, `QINQ`, `LLDP`, `STP`, `LACP`, `EAPOL`, `MPLS`).
  - [`docs/l3_protocols.md`](docs/l3_protocols.md) — Layer 3 control, tunneling, VPN, and routing protocols (`ICMP`, `NDP`, `IGMP`, `MLD`, `GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `IKEV2`, `WIREGUARD`, `OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `VRRP`, `HSRP`, `PIM`, `BFD`, `OPENFLOW`).
  - [`docs/l4_transports.md`](docs/l4_transports.md) — Layer 4 transports (`TCP`, `UDP`, `SCTP`), 4-tuple state tracking, RFC 7323 TCP options, and SCTP multi-chunk signaling.
  - [`docs/l7_snmp.md`](docs/l7_snmp.md) — Layer 7 `SNMP1`, `SNMP2`, and `SNMP3` USM authentication (`MD5`/`SHA`/`SHA256`/`SHA384`/`SHA512`), encryption (`DES`/`AES`), and all 9 ASN.1 SMI `VARBIND` types.
  - [`docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`](docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md) — Layer 7 infrastructure, time, AAA, and flow telemetry (`DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`, `NTP`, `PTP`, `RADIUS`, `TACACS`, `SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, `SFLOW`).
  - [`docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`](docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md) — Layer 7 web, cloud-native, transport security, VoIP, and remote access (`HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`, `TLS`, `QUIC`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`, `STUN`, `SSDP`).
  - [`docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`](docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md) — Layer 7 mail, directory, storage, databases, caches, and message brokers (`SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `SMB`, `NFS`, `REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`, `MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`).
  - [`docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`](docs/l7_industrial_ot.md) — Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS) & SCADA/OT (`MODBUS`, `BACNET`, `DNP3`, `S7COMM`, `ETHERNETIP`, `OPCUA`).
  - [`docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`](docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md) — Multi-host enterprise, data center EVPN-VXLAN, and campus Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC topologies.
  - [`docs/qa_synthesis_guide.md`](docs/qa_synthesis_guide.md) — Natural-Language Prompt to `.fasm` instruction-tuning Q&A pairs and GBNF constrained decoding guide.
- **Formal Grammars**:
  - [`grammar.ebnf`](grammar.ebnf): Formal ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF grammar.
  - [`frameassembly.gbnf`](frameassembly.gbnf): `llama.cpp` & MLC `XGrammar` GBNF grammar for constrained decoding (`--grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf`).
  - [`frameassembly.lark`](frameassembly.lark): Earley/LALR Lark grammar for `vLLM`, `Outlines`, `Guidance`, `XGrammar`, and `llguidance`.
- **AI Routing Maps & Metadata**:
  - [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) & [`.github/copilot-instructions.md`](.github/copilot-instructions.md): Agent & IDE instructions.
  - [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) & [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt): Concise index map and single-fetch full context bundle.
  - [`context7.json`](context7.json), [`codemeta.json`](codemeta.json) & [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff): Structured AI/SEO and academic citation metadata.

---

## 3. Core FrameAssembly DSL Rules & Invariants

1. **Program Structure & Case-Insensitivity**: Every `.fasm` file declares `HOST <id> { IP <ip> [MAC <mac>] }`, `FLOW <id>(<params>) { <statements> }`, and exactly one `COMPILE { <invocations_or_loops> }` block. All keywords, protocols, modifiers, time units (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`), and identifiers (`HOST`, `FLOW`, parameters) are case-insensitive (`host` / `HOST`).
2. **Polymorphic Dual-Stack Flows**: A `FLOW` works identically over IPv4 and IPv6 host pairs. Mixing IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints in the same statement is a semantic error.
3. **Zero-Keyword RFC Defaults**: Every one of the 81 protocols compiles with zero mandatory sub-keywords (emitting RFC-compliant default headers and ports) and supports explicit field overrides.
4. **1 Statement = 1 Frame & Shared 4-Tuple State**: Each statement emits 1 frame. TCP-based L7 statements emit a `PSH ACK` frame on that protocol's well-known port and share 4-tuple sequence/ack counters with raw `TCP` statements on the same connection.
5. **Corpus, AI Discovery & Documentation Hygiene**:
   - Every `.fasm` file in `examples/` must start with `// PROMPT: ...` on line 1, `// TOKENS: ...` on line 2 (matching real `src/lexer/mod.rs` tokens), and include `// INSTRUCTION: ...` before every `HOST`, `FLOW`, and `COMPILE` block (`avg_line_length <= 85`, `max_line_length <= 200`, `words >= 50`).
   - **Canonical Syntax Only (Anti-Hallucination Guardrail)**:
     - Never use `=`, colons, commas, `IPV4`, `IPV6`, or `MASK` in `HOST` blocks (only `HOST <id> { IP <ip> [MAC <mac>] }`).
     - Never declare parameterless `FLOW <id> { ... }` or use `FROM`, `TO`, `REVERSE`, `SEND`, standalone `WAIT` lines, or `+5ms` / `[+delay]` prefixes (always `FLOW <id>(<params>) { <a> -> <b> <PROTO> ... [WAIT <int><ns|us|ms|s|m>] }`).
     - Never use `SPORT`, `DPORT`, `ACK <n>`, or `FLAGS [...]` (always `SRCPORT`, `DSTPORT`, `ACKNUM <n>`, and bare flag tokens `SYN ACK`).
     - Never write bare `COMPILE` or argumentless flow calls inside `COMPILE { <flow>(<hosts>) }`.
   - **Five-Way Grammar & Parser Lockstep**: Every keyword in `src/lexer/mod.rs`, `grammar.ebnf`, `frameassembly.gbnf`, `frameassembly.lark`, and `frameassembly.tmLanguage.json` must be wired into `src/parser/` (with protocol-scoped field dispatch so `cut_err` or 0-arg flags never shadow other protocols) and included in `parse_spanned_ident`.
   - **100% Compilable Documentation & Examples**: Every `.fasm` file in `examples/` (`2,611` files) and every ````frameassembly` / ````fasm` code block in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `docs/*.md`, `src/**/*.rs`, and `.agents/skills/**/*.md` must compile with zero errors.
   - **Rustdoc & `docs.rs` SEO Hygiene**: Every `src/**/*.rs` file must start with `//!` (`< 50 KB` per file, `>= 50` words). Never place outer `///` comments on `pub mod` declarations that have inner `//!` docs. Keep internal parser submodules `pub(crate) mod` so `docs.rs` never generates empty module pages, use `#[doc(inline)]` on layer re-exports, and annotate all 81 AST `*Spec` structs with `/// Syntax mapping:` and `#[doc(alias = "...")]`.
   - Never write literal NUL bytes (`0x00`) into any `.md` or `.txt` file.
   - Keep `docs/*.md` and `src/**/*.rs` files strictly `< 50 KB` (`50,000` bytes) with zero broken links or orphan `.md` files.
   - Never bump `version` in `Cargo.toml` or run `git commit`, `git push`, or `git tag` unless explicitly instructed by the user.

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/getting_started.md`

# Getting Started with FrameAssembly

FrameAssembly builds standard `.pcap` / `.pcapng` packet capture files from plain-text `.fasm` files. You define the hosts in your scenario and list the frames exchanged between them—FrameAssembly handles Ethernet framing, protocol headers, byte lengths, checksums, and TCP sequence numbers automatically.

---

## 1. Installation

### One-Line Installer (Linux, macOS & BSDs)
Checks for basic build prerequisites, installs the Rust toolchain if missing, installs the `frameassembly` binary, and adds `.fasm` syntax highlighting if VS Code (`code`) is on your `PATH`:

```bash
curl -fsSL [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SteveWinschel/FrameAssembly/main/install.sh) | sh
```

### Install via Cargo
If you already have Rust `>= 1.85` installed:

```bash
cargo install frameassembly
```

Verify the installation:

```bash
frameassembly --help
```

---

## 2. Structure of a `.fasm` File

Every `.fasm` file has three sections: **`host`**, **`flow`**, and **`compile`**.
* **Case-insensitive:** `host`, `Host`, and `HOST` (or `tcp` and `TCP`) work identically.
* **Comments:** Start single-line comments with `//`.
* **One line = one packet:** Each statement inside a `flow` block produces one frame in your `.pcap` file.

```frameassembly
// 1. Declare the endpoints
host workstation {
    ip 192.168.10.50
    mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:50
}

host gateway {
    ip 192.168.10.1
    mac 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:01
}

// 2. Define the packet sequence
flow ping_gateway(client, gw) {
    client -> gw icmp echo_request id 100 seq 1 payload "ping-check" wait 2ms
    client <- gw icmp echo_reply id 100 seq 1 payload "ping-check" wait 2ms
}

// 3. Build the capture
compile {
    ping_gateway(workstation, gateway)
}
```

### Defaults vs. Custom Overrides
Every protocol works with **zero mandatory sub-keywords**. Writing just `client -> gw icmp` emits a valid ICMP Echo Request with standard defaults (`TTL 64`, `ID 1`, `SEQ 1`). Whenever you want control over specific header fields—custom ports, flags, VLAN IDs, TTLs, payloads, or inter-packet delays—append those modifiers to the same line in any order.

---

## 3. Directional Arrows & Automatic TCP Tracking

Inside a `flow` block, keep the initiating host on the left and use arrows to show packet direction—matching how sequence diagrams are drawn:
* `c -> s` sends a frame from `c` (source) to `s` (destination).
* `c <- s` sends a frame from `s` (source) back to `c` (destination).

### Automatic Port Swapping & TCP `SEQ` / `ACK` Math
When you open a connection, FrameAssembly tracks its state automatically across both raw `TCP` packets and TCP-based Layer 7 protocols (`HTTP`, `TLS`, `SSH`, `BGP`, `SMB`, `POSTGRES`, etc.):
1. **Port inheritance:** Set `srcport` and `dstport` on the first packet, and subsequent forward (`->`) and return (`<-`) lines automatically reuse and swap those ports.
2. **Sequence progression:** `SYN` and `FIN` flags advance the sequence number by `1`, and payload segments advance `SEQ` and `ACKNUM` by the exact byte length of the payload.

```frameassembly
host client { ip 10.10.1.50 }
host server { ip 10.10.1.80 }

flow http_health_check(c, s) {
    // Specify ports once on the opening SYN
    c -> s tcp syn srcport 52100 dstport 80 win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp syn ack win 65535 mss 1460 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack wait 1ms

    // HTTP automatically reuses 52100 <-> 80 and updates TCP SEQ/ACK counters
    c -> s http get uri "/healthz" host_hdr "service.internal" wait 5ms
    c <- s http status 200 reason "OK" content_type "application/json" body "{\"ok\":true}" wait 2ms

    // Graceful TCP FIN close
    c -> s tcp fin ack wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp fin ack wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack
}

compile {
    http_health_check(client, server)
}
```

*(Need to test how a firewall or stack handles out-of-window packets or a zero receive window? Explicitly adding `seq`, `acknum`, or `win 0` on any line overrides the automatic counter for that packet.)*

---

## 4. VLANs, QoS Tags, IPv4/IPv6 Reuse & Loops

### Cross-Layer Modifiers
You can attach Layer 2 (`vlan`, `qinq`, `mpls`, `srcmac`, `dstmac`), Layer 3 (`ttl`, `dscp`, `ecn`, `flowlabel`, `df`, `mf`, `fragoffset`), and timing (`wait`) modifiers to **any** protocol line.

### Dual-Stack Reuse & `loop` Blocks
Because `flow` blocks accept host parameters rather than hardcoded IP addresses, the same flow can be compiled with IPv4 hosts and IPv6 hosts, and repeated inside `loop <count> { ... }`:

```frameassembly
host probe_v4  { ip 172.16.20.10 }
host target_v4 { ip 172.16.20.1 }

host probe_v6  { ip 2001:db8:20::10 }
host target_v6 { ip 2001:db8:20::1 }

flow tagged_sla_probe(src, dst) {
    src -> dst vlan 200 pcp 5 dscp 46 udp srcport 60000 dstport 9000 payload "SLA_PING" wait 5ms
    src <- dst vlan 200 pcp 5 dscp 46 udp payload "SLA_PONG" wait 5ms
}

compile {
    loop 3 {
        tagged_sla_probe(probe_v4, target_v4)
        tagged_sla_probe(probe_v6, target_v6)
    }
}
```

> **Endpoint Rule:** Both hosts in a single packet statement must use the same IP version (both IPv4 or both IPv6). Mixing an IPv4 host and an IPv6 host in one `->` statement raises a compile-time error pointing to the conflicting hosts.

---

## 5. Compiling, Inspecting & Replaying

### 1. Compile `.fasm` to `.pcap`
```bash
frameassembly my_scenario.fasm -o my_scenario.pcap
```
If your file contains a typo or invalid value, `frameassembly` prints the exact line and column of the mistake so you can fix it immediately.

### 2. Inspect in Wireshark or `tshark`
```bash
# Packet summary list
tshark -r my_scenario.pcap

# Full protocol tree decode
tshark -r my_scenario.pcap -V
```

### 3. Replay Over a Network Interface with `tcpreplay`
To send your generated capture onto a physical NIC, VLAN interface, or virtual bridge:

```bash
# Replay honoring the exact WAIT intervals defined in your .fasm file
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 my_scenario.pcap

# Replay at maximum rate or loop multiple times
sudo tcpreplay -i eth0 --topspeed --loop=50 my_scenario.pcap
```

---

## 6. Quick Syntax Cheat Sheet

| Element | Correct `.fasm` Syntax | Common Mistake to Avoid |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Host block** | `host web { ip 10.0.0.1 mac 00:11:22:33:44:55 }` | Using `=`, `:`, commas, `ipv4`, or subnet masks |
| **Flow header** | `flow check(c, s) { ... }` | Omitting host parameters `(...)` |
| **Return packet** | `c <- s tcp syn ack` | Writing `reply` or `reverse` keywords |
| **Packet delay** | `c -> s tcp ack wait 5ms` | Putting `wait 5ms` on its own line |
| **Ports & TCP Ack** | `srcport 1234 dstport 80 acknum 100` | Writing `sport`, `dport`, or `ack 100` |
| **TCP flags** | `tcp syn ack` | Writing `flags [syn, ack]` or `flags="SA"` |
| **Hop limit** | `ttl 64` (works for both IPv4 and IPv6) | Writing `hop_limit 64` |
| **Double VLAN** | `qinq 100 inner_vlan 200` | Combining `qinq` and `vlan` on one line |
| **HTTP Host header**| `http get uri "/" host_hdr "example.com"` | Using `host "example.com"` inside an `http` line |
| **Loops** | `compile { loop 5 { check(a, b) } }` | Placing `loop` inside a `flow` block |

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/use_cases.md`

# Practical Use Cases & Scenarios

Each recipe below is a complete, compilable `.fasm` file solving a common packet-crafting task. Save any snippet to a `.fasm` file, compile it with `frameassembly <file>.fasm -o out.pcap`, and open `out.pcap` in Wireshark or inject it onto a test interface with `tcpreplay`.

---

## 1. Testing Firewall Rules, ACLs & Stateful Inspection

Standard tools like `ping` and `curl` only test normal OS-initiated connections. When validating firewall rulesets, DMZ segmentation, or stateless ACLs, you often need specific source ports, rejected port probes, out-of-state TCP flags, or `DF` MTU probes in a single repeatable capture:

```frameassembly
host external_client {
    ip 198.51.100.42
    mac 00:0c:29:11:22:33
}

host dmz_gateway {
    ip 203.0.113.10
    mac 00:1b:21:aa:bb:cc
}

flow firewall_policy_audit(ext, gw) {
    // 1. Permitted HTTPS 3-way handshake
    ext -> gw tcp syn srcport 51001 dstport 443 wait 1ms
    ext <- gw tcp syn ack wait 1ms
    ext -> gw tcp ack wait 5ms

    // 2. Blocked database port 3306 SYN and immediate RST+ACK rejection
    ext -> gw tcp syn srcport 51002 dstport 3306 wait 1ms
    ext <- gw tcp rst ack wait 5ms

    // 3. Out-of-state ACK probe on SSH port 22 (verifies stateful table drops)
    ext -> gw tcp ack srcport 51003 dstport 22 seq 8000 acknum 8000 wait 5ms

    // 4. Unusual flag combination (FIN + PSH + URG) for intrusion prevention checks
    ext -> gw tcp fin psh urg srcport 51004 dstport 445 wait 5ms

    // 5. Blocked ping answered with ICMP Administratively Prohibited (Code 13)
    ext -> gw df ttl 64 icmp echo_request id 99 seq 1 payload "ACL_PING_TEST" wait 1ms
    ext <- gw icmp dest_unreach code 13
}

compile {
    firewall_policy_audit(external_client, dmz_gateway)
}
```

---

## 2. Simulating SNMPv1, SNMPv2c & Encrypted SNMPv3 Traps

Testing monitoring alert rules (Zabbix, Checkmk, LibreNMS, PRTG, `snmptrapd`) normally means waiting for real device faults or wrestling with MIB dependencies and SNMPv3 key-localization flags. This scenario emits legacy `SNMPv1`, `SNMPv2c`, and encrypted `SNMPv3` (`SHA-256` + `AES-128`) traps directly:

```frameassembly
host core_switch {
    ip 10.100.0.254
    mac 00:1c:73:a0:00:fe
}

host nms_collector {
    ip 10.100.0.10
    mac 00:50:56:a0:00:10
}

flow snmp_alert_simulation(sw, nms) {
    // SNMPv1 linkDown generic trap (gentrap 2) on interface index 5
    sw -> nms snmp1 trap community "public" enterprise 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.1 agentip 10.100.0.254 gentrap 2 spectrap 0 sysuptime 125000 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.5 int 5 wait 10ms

    // SNMPv2c linkUp trap (1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4) with interface description
    sw -> nms snmp2 trap community "noc_traps" reqid 201 sysuptime 125500 oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.1.5 string "TenGigabitEthernet1/1/5" wait 10ms

    // Encrypted SNMPv3 USM authPriv trap (HMAC-SHA256 + AES-128) for high chassis temperature
    sw -> nms snmp3 trap user "nms_v3_ops" engineid "80001f8880001c73a000fe" engineboots 4 enginetime 86400 auth sha256 "TrapAuthSecret2026!" priv aes "TrapPrivSecret2026!" reqid 301 oid 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.13.3.0.1 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "core-sw-01" varbind 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.13.1.3.1.3.1 gauge32 84
}

compile {
    snmp_alert_simulation(core_switch, nms_collector)
}
```

---

## 3. Verifying VLAN Trunks, Carrier QinQ & DiffServ QoS Policies

Desktop operating systems often strip 802.1Q VLAN tags or restrict unprivileged DSCP markings. FrameAssembly stamps exact Layer 2 `VLAN` / `PCP`, 802.1ad `QINQ`, `MPLS` `EXP`, and Layer 3 `DSCP` values onto frames for switch trunk and WAN shaper verification:

```frameassembly
host branch_cpe { ip 10.20.0.10 mac 00:1c:73:20:00:10 }
host hq_concentrator { ip 10.20.0.1 mac 00:1c:73:20:00:01 }

flow qos_and_trunk_check(branch, hq) {
    // Voice VLAN 110: CoS 5 + DSCP 46 (Expedited Forwarding)
    branch -> hq vlan 110 pcp 5 dscp 46 rtp pt 0 seq 1 timestamp 160 ssrc 0x11223344 payload "G711_VOICE_20MS" wait 20ms

    // Video VLAN 120: CoS 4 + DSCP 34 (AF41)
    branch -> hq vlan 120 pcp 4 dscp 34 rtp pt 96 seq 1 timestamp 3600 ssrc 0x55667788 marker 1 payload "H264_KEYFRAME" wait 10ms

    // Double-tagged 802.1ad QinQ service trunk (S-VLAN 2500, C-VLAN 300, Drop-Eligible)
    branch -> hq qinq 2500 inner_vlan 300 pcp 1 dei 1 dscp 8 udp srcport 49100 dstport 873 payload "BULK_RSYNC_BLOCK"
}

compile {
    qos_and_trunk_check(branch_cpe, hq_concentrator)
}
```

---

## 4. Validating IDS/IPS Rules, TLS SNI Filtering & DNS Policies

Generate deterministic, noise-free `.pcap` inputs (`suricata -r test.pcap` or `zeek -r test.pcap`) to verify signature detection, TLS `SNI` inspection, HTTP header matching, and DNS sinkhole responses:

```frameassembly
host endpoint { ip 10.40.5.25 mac 00:50:56:40:05:25 }
host gateway  { ip 10.40.5.1  mac 00:1c:73:40:05:01 }

flow ids_and_sni_validation(client, gw) {
    // DNS lookup blocked by policy (RCODE 5 = REFUSED)
    client -> gw dns query txid 0x4401 qname "c2-beacon.bad-domain.test" qtype "A" wait 1ms
    client <- gw dns response txid 0x4401 qname "c2-beacon.bad-domain.test" qtype "A" rcode 5 wait 5ms

    // TLS 1.3 ClientHello carrying a specific SNI and ALPN for DPI inspection
    client -> gw tcp syn srcport 53443 dstport 443 wait 1ms
    client <- gw tcp syn ack wait 1ms
    client -> gw tcp ack wait 1ms
    client -> gw tls client_hello sni "unapproved-saas.example.net" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    client <- gw tls alert payload "ACCESS_DENIED_SNI_POLICY"
}

compile {
    ids_and_sni_validation(endpoint, gateway)
}
```

---

## 5. Testing SIEM Syslog & Flow Telemetry Collectors

Verify that your log and flow ingestion pipeline parses RFC 5424 Syslog, Cisco NetFlow v5, IPFIX (NetFlow v10), and sFlow v5 datagrams accurately:

```frameassembly
host border_router  { ip 10.250.0.1   mac 00:1c:73:fa:00:01 }
host telemetry_node { ip 10.250.0.100 mac 00:50:56:fa:00:64 }

flow noc_telemetry_ingest(rtr, col) {
    rtr -> col syslog facility 16 severity 2 hostname "border-rtr-01" app "bgpd" procid "1842" msg "BGP-3-NOTIFICATION: peer 198.51.100.1 Hold Timer Expired" wait 2ms
    rtr -> col netflow srcip 198.51.100.25 dstip 203.0.113.80 srcport 52400 dstport 443 proto 6 packets 15400 octets 21560000 wait 2ms
    rtr -> col ipfix domain_id 4001 srcip 198.51.100.25 dstip 203.0.113.80 srcport 52400 dstport 443 proto 6 packets 15400 octets 21560000 wait 2ms
    rtr -> col sflow agent_ip 10.250.0.1 sub_agent_id 1 uptime 86400000 samples 8
}

compile {
    noc_telemetry_ingest(border_router, telemetry_node)
}
```

---

## 6. Routing, BFD & Gateway Failover Simulation

Build control-plane captures combining sub-second BFD liveness, OSPF/BGP peering, and VRRP + Gratuitous ARP virtual IP takeover:

```frameassembly
host core_a { ip 10.0.0.1 mac 00:00:5e:00:01:0a }
host core_b { ip 10.0.0.2 mac 00:1c:73:00:00:02 }
host lan_bc { ip 10.0.0.255 mac ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff }

flow control_plane_convergence(a, b, bcast) {
    a -> b bfd state 3 my_disc 101 your_disc 202 min_tx 50000 min_rx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 1ms
    a -> b ospf hello router_id 1.1.1.1 area_id 0 hello_interval 10 dead_interval 40 ttl 1 wait 2ms
    a -> b bgp open asn 65001 holdtime 90 bgpid 1.1.1.1 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    a <- b bgp open asn 65002 holdtime 90 bgpid 2.2.2.2 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    a -> b bgp update asn 65001 prefix "172.16.0.0/16" nexthop 10.0.0.1 ttl 255 wait 5ms

    // VRRPv3 Master advertisement + Gratuitous ARP claiming VIP 10.0.0.254
    a -> b vrrp version 3 vrid 10 priority 200 adv_int 1 vip 10.0.0.254 ttl 255 wait 1ms
    a -> bcast arp reply gratuitous sendermac 00:00:5e:00:01:0a senderip 10.0.0.254 targetmac ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff targetip 10.0.0.254
}

compile {
    control_plane_convergence(core_a, core_b, lan_bc)
}
```

---

## 7. Industrial / OT Firewall & Dissector Testing

Validate IEC 62443 industrial firewall rules and OT security sensors across Modbus TCP, Siemens S7comm, DNP3, and OPC UA without physical PLCs:

```frameassembly
host scada_hmi { ip 192.168.100.10 mac 00:1b:21:a0:00:10 }
host plant_plc { ip 192.168.100.50 mac 00:0e:8c:a0:00:50 }

flow ot_conduit_polling(hmi, plc) {
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus func "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS" txid 1 unitid 1 addr 40001 count 4 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus func "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS" txid 1 unitid 1 count 4 is_response wait 5ms
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 s7comm rosctr "JOB" func "READ_VAR" pdu_ref 10 area 0x84 db_num 1 offset 0 count 8 wait 5ms
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 opcua msg_type "HEL" chunk_type "F" endpoint_url "opc.tcp://192.168.100.50:4840"
}

compile {
    ot_conduit_polling(scada_hmi, plant_plc)
}
```
