# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l2_protocols.md`

# Layer 2 Data Link Protocols & Encapsulation Reference

FrameAssembly supports **8 Layer 2 and Layer 2.5 protocols** natively—generating valid Ethernet II / IEEE 802.3 LLC framing, multicast MACs, and protocol TLVs automatically when optional fields are omitted.

| Protocol | Keyword | Standard | EtherType / Multicast MAC | Primary Use Cases |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ARP** | `ARP` | RFC 826 / 5227 | `0x0806` / `ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff` | Gateway MAC lookup, Gratuitous ARP (`GARP`) VIP failover, IP conflict probes |
| **VLAN** | `VLAN` | IEEE 802.1Q / 802.1p | `0x8100` | 12-bit VLAN ID (`1..4094`), 3-bit CoS priority (`PCP`), 1-bit drop bit (`DEI`) |
| **QinQ** | `QINQ` | IEEE 802.1ad | `0x88A8` (S-Tag) + `0x8100` (C-Tag) | Carrier Metro Ethernet double-tagging (`QINQ <s_vid> INNER_VLAN <c_vid>`) |
| **LLDP** | `LLDP` | IEEE 802.1AB | `0x88CC` / `01:80:c2:00:00:0e` | Chassis ID, Port ID, TTL, System Name, and System Description TLVs |
| **STP / RSTP**| `STP` | IEEE 802.1D / 802.1w | 802.3 LLC / `01:80:c2:00:00:00` | Root Bridge elections, RSTP Proposal/Agreement BPDUs, BPDU Guard tests |
| **LACP** | `LACP` | IEEE 802.3ad / 802.1AX| `0x8809` / `01:80:c2:00:00:02` | Port-Channel / LAG Actor & Partner state synchronization |
| **EAPOL** | `EAPOL` | IEEE 802.1X | `0x888E` / `01:80:c2:00:00:03` | Port NAC (`START`, `EAP_PACKET` Identity/MD5/TLS, WPA `KEY`, `LOGOFF`) |
| **MPLS** | `MPLS` | RFC 3031 / 3032 | `0x8847` | 20-bit label switching (`MPLS` / `LABEL`), Traffic Class (`EXP`), `BOS`, `MPLS_TTL` |

### Universal Ethernet II Header Overrides
Any statement in FrameAssembly also accepts outer Ethernet header overrides:
* `SRCMAC <mac>`: Overrides the 48-bit source MAC address.
* `DSTMAC <mac>`: Overrides the 48-bit destination MAC address.
* `ETHERTYPE <u16>`: Overrides the 16-bit EtherType field.

---

## 1. Address Resolution Protocol (`ARP` — RFC 826)

Maps IPv4 addresses (`0x0800`) to 48-bit Ethernet MAC addresses. *(If an `ARP` flow is run with IPv6 hosts in `compile`, FrameAssembly automatically emits an RFC 4861 ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation / Advertisement packet with Hop Limit `255`.)*

| Modifier | Syntax | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Operation** | `REQUEST` / `REPLY` | ARP Opcode (`1` = Request, `2` = Reply) | `REQUEST` (`1`) |
| **Gratuitous Mode**| `GRATUITOUS` or `GARP` | Sets Sender IP = Target IP for VIP failover or duplicate address detection | Disabled |
| **Sender MAC** | `SHA <mac>` or `SENDERMAC <mac>` | 48-bit Sender Hardware Address | Source host MAC |
| **Sender IP** | `SPA <ipv4>` or `SENDERIP <ipv4>` | 32-bit Sender Protocol Address | Source host IP |
| **Target MAC** | `THA <mac>` or `TARGETMAC <mac>` | 48-bit Target Hardware Address (`00:00:00:00:00:00` on Request) | Dest host MAC |
| **Target IP** | `TPA <ipv4>` or `TARGETIP <ipv4>` | 32-bit Target Protocol Address | Dest host IP |

```frameassembly
host workstation { ip 192.168.1.105 mac 00:50:56:a1:00:20 }
host gateway     { ip 192.168.1.1   mac 00:50:56:fe:00:01 }
host broadcast   { ip 192.168.1.255 mac ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff }

flow arp_and_failover_garp(client, gw, bcast) {
    // Standard broadcast ARP Request and unicast Reply
    client -> gw arp request dstmac ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff tha 00:00:00:00:00:00 wait 1ms
    client <- gw arp reply wait 5ms

    // RFC 5227 ARP Probe (senderip 0.0.0.0) followed by Gratuitous ARP VIP announcement
    gw -> bcast arp request sendermac 00:50:56:fe:00:01 senderip 0.0.0.0 targetmac 00:00:00:00:00:00 targetip 192.168.1.1 wait 5ms
    gw -> bcast arp reply gratuitous sendermac 00:50:56:fe:00:01 senderip 192.168.1.1 targetmac ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff targetip 192.168.1.1
}

compile {
    arp_and_failover_garp(workstation, gateway, broadcast)
}
```

---

## 2. Virtual LAN (`VLAN` — 802.1Q) & Provider Bridging (`QINQ` — 802.1ad)

Both `VLAN` and `QINQ` can be used as standalone Layer 2 frames or attached as modifiers to any upper-layer protocol (`TCP`, `UDP`, `HTTP`, `OSPF`, `SIP`, `MODBUS`, etc.).

| Modifier | Syntax | Range | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **802.1Q VLAN ID** | `VLAN <u16>` | `0..4095` | Inserts an 802.1Q tag (`0x8100`) with 12-bit VLAN ID |
| **Priority (CoS)** | `PCP <u8>` | `0..7` | 3-bit IEEE 802.1p priority (`5` = Voice, `6` = Control, `7` = Network) |
| **Drop Eligible** | `DEI <u8>` | `0..1` | 1-bit Drop Eligible Indicator for congestion policing |
| **Outer S-VLAN** | `QINQ <u16>` | `0..4095` | Inserts outer IEEE 802.1ad Service VLAN tag (`0x88A8`) |
| **Inner C-VLAN** | `INNER_VLAN <u16>` | `0..4095` | Sets inner Customer VLAN tag (`0x8100`) paired with `QINQ` |

> **Syntax Rule:** For double-tagged 802.1ad frames, always write `QINQ <outer_svid> INNER_VLAN <inner_cvid>`. Do not combine `QINQ` and `VLAN` on the same statement.

```frameassembly
host site_a { ip 172.20.10.1 mac 00:50:56:ce:0a:01 }
host site_b { ip 172.20.10.2 mac 00:50:56:ce:0b:02 }

flow trunk_and_qinq(a, b) {
    // Single-tagged 802.1Q voice and bulk frames
    a -> b vlan 100 pcp 5 dei 0 udp srcport 16384 dstport 16384 payload "VOICE_RTP" wait 1ms
    a -> b vlan 300 pcp 1 dei 1 udp srcport 49200 dstport 873 payload "BULK_BACKUP" wait 2ms

    // Double-tagged 802.1ad Metro Ethernet L2VPN carrying BGP
    a -> b qinq 2500 inner_vlan 40 pcp 6 tcp syn srcport 52000 dstport 179 wait 1ms
    a <- b qinq 2500 inner_vlan 40 pcp 6 tcp syn ack
}

compile {
    trunk_and_qinq(site_a, site_b)
}
```

---

## 3. Link Layer Discovery Protocol (`LLDP` — IEEE 802.1AB)

Advertises switch/server identity, interface names, and software versions to directly connected neighbors (`01:80:c2:00:00:0e`, EtherType `0x88CC`).

| Modifier | Syntax | TLV & Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chassis ID** | `CHASSIS_ID "<str>"` | TLV Type `1` (Mandatory): Chassis MAC or identifier string |
| **Port ID** | `PORT_ID "<str>"` or `<u16>` | TLV Type `2` (Mandatory): Interface name (e.g. `"Ethernet1/1"`) or index |
| **Hold Time** | `TTL <u8>` | TLV Type `3` (Mandatory): Neighbor hold time in seconds (default `120`) |
| **System Name** | `SYSNAME "<str>"` | TLV Type `5` (Optional): Device FQDN / hostname |
| **System Desc** | `SYSDESC "<str>"` | TLV Type `6` (Optional): OS version and hardware platform string |

```frameassembly
host spine_sw { ip 10.255.0.1  mac 00:1c:73:a0:01:01 }
host leaf_sw  { ip 10.255.0.11 mac 00:1c:73:b0:11:49 }

flow lldp_neighbor_exchange(spine, leaf) {
    spine -> leaf lldp chassis_id "00:1c:73:a0:01:01" port_id "Ethernet1/1" ttl 120 sysname "spine-01.dc1" sysdesc "SONiC 202511 400G" wait 5ms
    spine <- leaf lldp chassis_id "00:1c:73:b0:11:49" port_id "Ethernet49/1" ttl 120 sysname "leaf-01.dc1" sysdesc "SONiC 202511 ToR"
}

compile {
    lldp_neighbor_exchange(spine_sw, leaf_sw)
}
```

---

## 4. Spanning Tree Protocol (`STP` / `RSTP` — IEEE 802.1D / 802.1w)

Emits classic STP Configuration BPDUs or 36-byte Rapid Spanning Tree (`RSTP`) BPDUs to `01:80:c2:00:00:00`.

| Modifier | Syntax | Description & Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Rapid STP** | `RSTP` | Emits IEEE 802.1w Version `2` Rapid Spanning Tree BPDU |
| **BPDU Flags** | `FLAGS <u8>` | Topology Change (`0x01`), Proposal (`0x02`), Role/State bits, TCA (`0x80`) |
| **Root Bridge ID**| `ROOT_ID "<prio>/<mac>"` | Root priority and MAC (e.g. `"4096/00:05:73:a0:00:01"`) |
| **Sender Bridge**| `BRIDGE_ID "<prio>/<mac>"` | Transmitting bridge priority and MAC |
| **Path Cost** | `COST <u32>` | Root path cost (`0` on root bridge, `2000` for 10GbE) |
| **Port & Timers** | `PORT_ID <u16>`, `MAX_AGE <u16>`, `HELLO_TIME <u16>`, `FORWARD_DELAY <u16>` | Port ID (`0x8001`) and timers (defaults: Max Age `20`s, Hello `2`s, Fwd Delay `15`s) |

```frameassembly
host root_sw   { ip 10.0.1.1 mac 00:05:73:a0:00:01 }
host access_sw { ip 10.0.1.2 mac 00:05:73:a0:00:02 }

flow rstp_proposal_agreement(root, acc) {
    root -> acc stp rstp root_id "4096/00:05:73:a0:00:01" bridge_id "4096/00:05:73:a0:00:01" cost 0 max_age 20 hello_time 2 forward_delay 15 flags 0x0e wait 2ms
    root <- acc stp rstp root_id "4096/00:05:73:a0:00:01" bridge_id "32768/00:05:73:a0:00:02" cost 2000 max_age 20 hello_time 2 forward_delay 15 flags 0x7c
}

compile {
    rstp_proposal_agreement(root_sw, access_sw)
}
```

---

## 5. Link Aggregation Control Protocol (`LACP` — IEEE 802.3ad)

Negotiates dynamic LAG / Port-Channel bundles (`01:80:c2:00:00:02`, EtherType `0x8809`).

| Modifier | Syntax | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Actor Fields** | `ACTOR_SYS <mac>`, `ACTOR_KEY <u16>`, `ACTOR_PORT <u16>`, `ACTOR_STATE <u8>` | Local switch system MAC, admin key, port number, and state bitmask (`0x3f` = Active/Short/Agg/Sync/Col/Dist) |
| **Partner Fields**| `PARTNER_SYS <mac>`, `PARTNER_KEY <u16>`, `PARTNER_PORT <u16>`, `PARTNER_STATE <u8>` | Remote peer's system MAC, key, port, and state bitmask |

```frameassembly
host sw_a { ip 10.0.2.1 mac 00:e0:f7:01:02:03 }
host sw_b { ip 10.0.2.2 mac 00:e0:f7:04:05:06 }

flow lacp_port_channel_sync(a, b) {
    a -> b lacp actor_sys 00:e0:f7:01:02:03 actor_key 100 actor_port 1 actor_state 0x47 partner_sys 00:00:00:00:00:00 partner_key 0 partner_port 0 partner_state 0x00 wait 5ms
    a <- b lacp actor_sys 00:e0:f7:04:05:06 actor_key 100 actor_port 1 actor_state 0x3f partner_sys 00:e0:f7:01:02:03 partner_key 100 partner_port 1 partner_state 0x3f wait 5ms
    a -> b lacp actor_sys 00:e0:f7:01:02:03 actor_key 100 actor_port 1 actor_state 0x3f partner_sys 00:e0:f7:04:05:06 partner_key 100 partner_port 1 partner_state 0x3f
}

compile {
    lacp_port_channel_sync(sw_a, sw_b)
}
```

---

## 6. 802.1X Port Authentication (`EAPOL`) & MPLS (`MPLS`)

### `EAPOL` Modifiers (EtherType `0x888E`)
* `VERSION <1|2|3>`: 802.1X version (`2` = 2004, `3` = 2010/2020).
* `TYPE <START|LOGOFF|KEY|EAP_PACKET>`: Always include the `TYPE` keyword before the packet type.
* `EAP_CODE <1..4>`: `1` = Request, `2` = Response, `3` = Success, `4` = Failure.
* `EAP_ID <u8>`, `EAP_METHOD <u8>` (`1` = Identity, `4` = MD5, `13` = EAP-TLS, `25` = PEAP), `IDENTITY "<str>"`.

### `MPLS` Modifiers (EtherType `0x8847`)
* `MPLS <0..1048575>` (or `LABEL <u20>`): 20-bit MPLS label value.
* `EXP <0..7>` (or `TC <0..7>`): 3-bit Traffic Class QoS marking.
* `BOS <0|1>`: Bottom-of-Stack bit (`1` default).
* `MPLS_TTL <0..255>`: MPLS shim TTL independent of the inner IP TTL (`64` default).

```frameassembly
host laptop   { ip 10.50.10.25 mac 00:24:d7:11:22:33 }
host auth_sw  { ip 10.50.10.1  mac 00:1c:73:80:21:10 }

flow dot1x_and_mpls_forwarding(supp, sw) {
    // 802.1X EAP-TLS onboarding
    supp -> sw eapol version 2 type start wait 2ms
    supp <- sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 1 eap_id 1 eap_method 1 wait 2ms
    supp -> sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 2 eap_id 1 eap_method 1 identity "host/laptop.corp" wait 2ms
    supp <- sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 3 eap_id 1 wait 5ms

    // MPLS L3VPN labeled ICMP exchange
    supp -> sw mpls 24010 exp 5 bos 1 mpls_ttl 64 icmp echo_request id 301 seq 1 payload "VRF_PING" wait 2ms
    supp <- sw mpls 24020 exp 5 bos 1 mpls_ttl 63 icmp echo_reply id 301 seq 1 payload "VRF_PONG"
}

compile {
    dot1x_and_mpls_forwarding(laptop, auth_sw)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l3_protocols.md`

# Layer 3 Network, Routing, Tunneling, VPN & FHRP Reference

FrameAssembly supports **20 Layer 3 protocols** across IPv4 (`0x0800`) and IPv6 (`0x86DD`), along with universal IP header modifiers that can be applied to any frame statement.

---

## 1. Universal IPv4 & IPv6 Modifiers

| Modifier | Syntax | Range | Effect on Wire |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TTL / Hop Limit** | `TTL <u8>` | `0..255` | IPv4 TTL or IPv6 Hop Limit (`64` default, `255` for GTSM/NDP, `1` for link-local multicast) |
| **DiffServ QoS** | `DSCP <u8>` | `0..63` | 6-bit DSCP (`46` = EF Voice, `34` = AF41 Video, `48` = CS6 Routing Control) |
| **Congestion Bits** | `ECN <u8>` | `0..3` | 2-bit Explicit Congestion Notification (`0`=Non-ECT, `1`=ECT1, `2`=ECT0, `3`=CE) |
| **IPv6 Flow Label** | `FLOWLABEL <u20>`| `0..1048575` | 20-bit IPv6 Flow Label for ECMP hashing (ignored on IPv4 statements) |
| **IPv4 Frag ID** | `IPID <u16>` | `0..65535` | 16-bit IPv4 Identification field for fragment reassembly |
| **Frag Flags** | `DF`, `MF` | Bare flags | Sets IPv4 Don't Fragment (`0x4000`) or More Fragments (`0x2000`) |
| **Frag Offset** | `FRAGOFFSET <u16>`| `0..8191` | 13-bit IPv4 fragment offset in 8-byte units |
| **Inner Protocol** | `NEXT_HEADER <u8>`| `0..255` | Overrides protected inner protocol on IPsec/ESP/AH/IPv6 headers |

---

## 2. Diagnostics & IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (`ICMP` & `NDP`)

* **`ICMP` (Emits ICMPv4 on IPv4 pairs and ICMPv6 with RFC 4443 pseudo-header checksum on IPv6 pairs):**
  * Message types: `ECHO_REQUEST`, `ECHO_REPLY`, `DEST_UNREACH`, `TIME_EXCEEDED`, `REDIRECT`.
  * Modifiers: `CODE <u8>` (e.g. `3` = Port Unreachable, `4` = Frag Needed, `13` = Admin Prohibited), `ID <u16>`, `SEQ <u32>`, `GATEWAY <ip>`.
* **`NDP` (IPv6 Neighbor Discovery — RFC 4861, default Hop Limit `255`):**
  * Message types: `ROUTER_SOLICIT`, `ROUTER_ADVERT`, `NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT`, `NEIGHBOR_ADVERT`.
  * Modifiers: `TARGET <ipv6>`, `SLLA <mac>` (Source Link-Layer Address option), `TLLA <mac>` (Target Link-Layer Address option), `ROUTER_LIFETIME <u16>`.

```frameassembly
host client_v4 { ip 192.168.10.50 }
host router_v4 { ip 192.168.10.1 }
host host_v6   { ip 2001:db8:100::50 mac 00:50:56:60:00:50 }
host router_v6 { ip 2001:db8:100::1  mac 00:50:56:60:00:01 }

flow diagnostics_and_slaac(c4, r4, h6, r6) {
    // IPv4 ping, Path MTU Discovery (Code 4), and Redirect
    c4 -> r4 icmp echo_request id 1001 seq 1 payload "IPV4_PROBE" wait 1ms
    c4 <- r4 icmp echo_reply id 1001 seq 1 payload "IPV4_PROBE" wait 1ms
    c4 <- r4 icmp dest_unreach code 4 payload "PMTUD_MTU_1400" wait 1ms
    c4 <- r4 icmp redirect code 1 gateway 192.168.10.254 wait 2ms

    // IPv6 SLAAC Router Solicitation/Advertisement and Neighbor Discovery
    h6 -> r6 ndp router_solicit slla 00:50:56:60:00:50 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    h6 <- r6 ndp router_advert slla 00:50:56:60:00:01 router_lifetime 1800 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    h6 -> r6 ndp neighbor_solicit target 2001:db8:100::1 slla 00:50:56:60:00:50 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    h6 <- r6 ndp neighbor_advert target 2001:db8:100::1 tlla 00:50:56:60:00:01 ttl 255
}

compile {
    diagnostics_and_slaac(client_v4, router_v4, host_v6, router_v6)
}
```

---

## 3. Multicast Group Management (`IGMP` & `MLD`)

| Protocol | Modifiers | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`IGMP`** | `QUERY`, `REPORT`, `LEAVE`, `V1` / `V2` / `V3` (`VERSION <1..3>`), `GROUP <ipv4>`, `MAX_RESP <u8>` | IPv4 multicast membership query, join report, and fast-leave (`MAX_RESP` in 1/10s) |
| **`MLD`** | `QUERY`, `REPORT`, `DONE`, `MULTICAST_ADDR <ipv6>`, `MAX_RESP_DELAY <u16>` | IPv6 ICMPv6 Multicast Listener Discovery (`MAX_RESP_DELAY` in ms) |

```frameassembly
host rtr_v4 { ip 10.40.1.1 }
host stb_v4 { ip 10.40.1.50 }
host rtr_v6 { ip fe80::1 }
host sub_v6 { ip fe80::50 }

flow multicast_lifecycle(r4, h4, r6, h6) {
    r4 -> h4 igmp version 3 query group 239.255.1.1 max_resp 100 ttl 1 wait 2ms
    r4 <- h4 igmp version 2 report group 239.255.1.1 ttl 1 wait 2ms
    r4 <- h4 igmp version 2 leave group 239.255.1.1 ttl 1 wait 5ms

    r6 -> h6 mld query multicast_addr ff3e::100 max_resp_delay 1000 ttl 1 wait 2ms
    r6 <- h6 mld report multicast_addr ff3e::100 ttl 1 wait 2ms
    r6 <- h6 mld done multicast_addr ff3e::100 ttl 1
}

compile {
    multicast_lifecycle(rtr_v4, stb_v4, rtr_v6, sub_v6)
}
```

---

## 4. Overlay & Underlay Tunneling (`GRE`, `VXLAN`, `GENEVE`)

| Protocol | Default Port / Proto | Modifiers & Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`GRE`** | IP Proto `47` | `GRE_KEY <u32>`, `GRE_SEQ <u32>`, `GRE_PROTO <u16>` (`0x0800` IPv4, `0x86DD` IPv6, `0x6558` TEB), `CHECKSUM` |
| **`VXLAN`** | UDP `4789` | `VNI <0..16777215>` (or `VNID`), `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>` (emits a valid inner Ethernet+IPv4+UDP frame if payload is omitted) |
| **`GENEVE`**| UDP `6081` | `VNI <0..16777215>`, `OPT_CLASS <u16>` (e.g. `0x0102` OVN/Cilium, `0x0108` AWS GWLB), `OPT_TYPE <u8>`, `PROTOCOL_TYPE <u16>` |

```frameassembly
host vtep_a { ip 10.200.0.1 }
host vtep_b { ip 10.200.0.2 }

flow fabric_overlays(a, b) {
    a -> b gre gre_key 50010 gre_seq 1 gre_proto 0x0800 checksum payload "GRE_ROUTED_PACKET" wait 1ms
    a -> b vxlan vni 10500 df payload "EVPN_VXLAN_TENANT_FRAME" wait 1ms
    a -> b geneve vni 20800 opt_class 0x0102 opt_type 1 protocol_type 0x6558 payload "CILIUM_GENEVE_FRAME"
}

compile {
    fabric_overlays(vtep_a, vtep_b)
}
```

---

## 5. Cryptographic VPNs (`IKEV2`, `IPSEC`, `ESP`, `AH`, `WIREGUARD`)

| Protocol | Default Port / Proto | Modifiers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`IKEV2`** | UDP `500` / `4500` | `SA_INIT`, `CREATE_CHILD_SA`, `INFORMATIONAL`, `EXCHANGE <mode>`, `INITIATOR_SPI <u64>`, `RESPONDER_SPI <u64>`, `MSGID <u32>`, `NEXT_PAYLOAD <u8>` |
| **`IPSEC` / `ESP`**| IP Proto `50` | `SPI <u32>`, `SEQ <u32>`, `IV "<hex>"`, `ICV "<hex>"`, `NEXT_HEADER <u8>` (`4`=IPv4, `6`=TCP, `41`=IPv6) |
| **`AH`** | IP Proto `51` | `SPI <u32>`, `SEQ <u32>`, `ICV "<hex>"`, `NEXT_HEADER <u8>` |
| **`WIREGUARD`**| UDP `51820` | `TYPE <INITIATION\|RESPONSE\|COOKIE\|DATA>` (or bare `INITIATION`, `COOKIE`, `DATA`), `SENDER <u32>`, `RECEIVER <u32>`, `COUNTER <u64>` |

```frameassembly
host branch_vpn { ip 198.51.100.10 }
host hq_vpn     { ip 203.0.113.1 }

flow ipsec_and_wireguard(branch, hq) {
    branch -> hq ikev2 sa_init initiator_spi 0xa1b2c3d4e5f60001 responder_spi 0 msgid 0 next_payload 33 wait 2ms
    branch <- hq ikev2 sa_init initiator_spi 0xa1b2c3d4e5f60001 responder_spi 0x9988776655440002 msgid 0 next_payload 33 wait 2ms
    branch -> hq esp spi 0x10002001 seq 1 iv "1122334455667788" icv "aabbccddeeff001122334455" next_header 4 payload "ESP_CIPHERTEXT" wait 1ms
    branch <- hq ah spi 0x20003002 seq 1 icv "99887766554433221100ffeeddcc" next_header 4 payload "AH_AUTHENTICATED" wait 5ms

    branch -> hq wireguard type initiation sender 0x10203040 wait 1ms
    branch <- hq wireguard type response sender 0x50607080 receiver 0x10203040 wait 1ms
    branch -> hq wireguard type data receiver 0x50607080 counter 1 payload "WG_TRANSPORT_DATA"
}

compile {
    ipsec_and_wireguard(branch_vpn, hq_vpn)
}
```

---

## 6. Dynamic Routing Protocols (`OSPF`, `BGP`, `RIP`, `PIM`)

| Protocol | Default Port / Proto | Modifiers & Syntax Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`OSPF`** | IP Proto `89` | `HELLO`, `DBD`, `LSR`, `LSU`, `LSACK`, `ROUTER_ID <ipv4>`, `AREA_ID <u32>` *(integer, e.g. `0` for Area 0.0.0.0)*, `HELLO_INTERVAL <u16>`, `DEAD_INTERVAL <u32>`, `PRIORITY <u8>` |
| **`BGP`** | TCP `179` | `OPEN`, `UPDATE`, `NOTIFICATION`, `KEEPALIVE`, `ASN <u32>`, `HOLDTIME <u16>`, `BGPID <ipv4>`, `PREFIX "<cidr>"` *(quoted CIDR string)*, `NEXTHOP <ip>` |
| **`RIP`** | UDP `520` | `REQUEST`, `RESPONSE`, `PREFIX <ip>` *(unquoted IP address)*, `NEXTHOP <ip>`, `METRIC <1..16>`, `TAG <u16>` |
| **`PIM`** | IP Proto `103` | `HELLO`, `JOIN_PRUNE`, `REGISTER`, `GROUP <ip>`, `SOURCE <ip>`, `RP <ip>`, `HOLDTIME <u16>`, `DR_PRIORITY <u32>` |

```frameassembly
host rtr1 { ip 10.0.0.1 }
host rtr2 { ip 10.0.0.2 }

flow routing_convergence(r1, r2) {
    r1 -> r2 ospf hello router_id 1.1.1.1 area_id 0 hello_interval 10 dead_interval 40 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    r1 <- r2 ospf hello router_id 2.2.2.2 area_id 0 hello_interval 10 dead_interval 40 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    r1 -> r2 bgp open asn 65001 holdtime 90 bgpid 1.1.1.1 ttl 255 wait 1ms
    r1 <- r2 bgp open asn 65002 holdtime 90 bgpid 2.2.2.2 ttl 255 wait 1ms
    r1 <- r2 bgp update asn 65002 prefix "172.16.0.0/12" nexthop 10.0.0.2 ttl 255 wait 1ms
    r1 -> r2 rip response prefix 192.168.50.0 nexthop 10.0.0.1 metric 2 tag 100 ttl 2 wait 1ms
    r1 <- r2 pim join_prune group 239.10.10.1 source 10.1.1.10 rp 10.0.0.1 ttl 1
}

compile {
    routing_convergence(rtr1, rtr2)
}
```

---

## 7. Gateway Redundancy, Fast Failover & SDN (`VRRP`, `HSRP`, `BFD`, `OPENFLOW`)

| Protocol | Default Port / Proto | Modifiers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`VRRP`** | IP Proto `112` | `VERSION <2\|3>` (default `3`), `VRID <1..255>`, `PRIORITY <0..255>`, `ADV_INT <u16>`, `VIP <ip>` |
| **`HSRP`** | UDP `1985` | `GROUP <u8>`, `PRIORITY <u8>`, `STATE <u8>` (`16` = Active, `8` = Standby), `HELLOTIME <u8>`, `HOLDTIME <u16>`, `VIP <ip>` |
| **`BFD`** | UDP `3784` | `STATE <0..3>` (`3`=Up, `2`=Init, `1`=Down, `0`=AdminDown), `DIAG <u8>`, `MY_DISC <u32>`, `YOUR_DISC <u32>`, `MIN_TX <u32>` ($\mu$s), `MIN_RX <u32>` ($\mu$s), `MULT <u8>` |
| **`OPENFLOW`**| TCP `6653` | `HELLO`, `FEATURES_REQ`, `FEATURES_REPLY`, `PACKET_IN`, `PACKET_OUT`, `FLOW_MOD`, `ECHO_REQ`, `ECHO_REPLY`, `VERSION <u8>` (`4`=v1.3), `XID <u32>`, `DPID <u64>`, `TABLE_ID <u8>`, `PRIORITY <u16>` |

```frameassembly
host gw_pri { ip 10.10.0.2 }
host gw_sec { ip 10.10.0.3 }

flow gateway_ha_and_openflow(pri, sec) {
    pri -> sec vrrp version 3 vrid 10 priority 200 adv_int 1 vip 10.10.0.1 ttl 255 wait 1ms
    pri -> sec hsrp group 10 priority 150 state 16 hellotime 3 holdtime 10 vip 10.10.0.254 ttl 1 wait 1ms
    pri -> sec bfd state 3 diag 0 my_disc 1001 your_disc 2002 min_tx 50000 min_rx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    pri <- sec openflow version 4 features_req xid 101 wait 1ms
    pri -> sec openflow version 4 features_reply xid 101 dpid 0x0000001c73aabbcc
}

compile {
    gateway_ha_and_openflow(gw_pri, gw_sec)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l4_transports.md`

# Layer 4 Transport Protocols Reference (`TCP`, `UDP`, `SCTP`)

FrameAssembly supports **TCP**, **UDP**, and **SCTP** across IPv4 and IPv6, automatically computing IPv4/IPv6 pseudo-header checksums (`TCP`/`UDP`) and hardware-valid 32-bit Castagnoli CRC32c checksums (`SCTP`).

| Protocol | Keyword | IP Proto | Checksum | Key Capabilities |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TCP** | `TCP` | `6` | RFC 1071 + IPv4/IPv6 Pseudo-Header | Automatic `SEQ`/`ACKNUM` & port tracking, all 8 flags, `MSS`, `WSCALE`, `SACK_PERM`, `TSVAL`/`TSECR` |
| **UDP** | `UDP` | `17` | RFC 1071 + IPv4/IPv6 Pseudo-Header | Unicast/multicast datagrams, bidirectional port reversal, custom payloads, fragmentation tests |
| **SCTP** | `SCTP` | `132` | 32-bit CRC32c (Castagnoli) | 4-way `INIT`/`COOKIE_ECHO` handshake, `VTAG`, multi-streaming (`STREAM`, `SSN`, `TSN`, `PPID`) |

---

## 1. Transmission Control Protocol (`TCP` — RFC 9293)

### Automatic Connection State vs. Manual Overrides
When `SEQ`, `ACKNUM`, or ports are omitted on follow-up packets in a flow, FrameAssembly maintains connection state automatically:
* **Bidirectional port swapping:** If `c -> s tcp syn srcport 52000 dstport 443` is followed by `c <- s tcp syn ack`, the reply automatically sets `srcport 443` and `dstport 52000`.
* **Sequence accounting:** `SYN` and `FIN` consume `1` sequence number (`SEQ + 1`), while data packets advance `SEQ` by the exact payload byte count—including Layer 7 TCP protocols (`HTTP`, `TLS`, `SSH`, `POSTGRES`, etc.) on the same connection.
* **Explicit overrides:** Specifying `SEQ`, `ACKNUM`, or `WIN` on any statement overrides the tracked value for that packet (useful for testing retransmissions, out-of-window drops, or zero-window stalls).

| Category | Modifier Syntax | Description & Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ports** | `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>` | Source and destination ports (default `DSTPORT 80`; never write `SPORT`/`DPORT`) |
| **Control Flags** | `SYN`, `ACK`, `FIN`, `RST`, `PSH`, `URG`, `ECE`, `CWR` | Combine any flags separated by spaces (e.g. `tcp syn ack` or `tcp rst ack`) |
| **Sequence / Ack**| `SEQ <u32>`, `ACKNUM <u32>` | 32-bit Sequence and Acknowledgment numbers (never write `ACK_NUM`) |
| **Window & Urgent**| `WIN <u16>` (or `WINDOW <u16>`), `URGENT <u16>` | Receive window size (default `65535`) and Urgent Pointer offset |
| **RFC 7323 Options**| `MSS <u16>`, `WSCALE <0..14>`, `SACK_PERM`, `TSVAL <u32>`, `TSECR <u32>` | Max Segment Size, Window Scale shift count, SACK Permitted, and Timestamps |
| **Dual-Mode L7** | `TRANSPORT TCP` | Forces dual-transport L7 protocols (`DNS`, `SIP`, `SYSLOG`, `NFS`) over TCP |

### Example A: Full TCP Handshake with Options, Data Transfer & FIN Close
```frameassembly
host app_client { ip 10.10.20.50 }
host api_server { ip 10.10.20.10 }

flow tcp_full_lifecycle(c, s) {
    c -> s tcp syn srcport 54321 dstport 443 mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm tsval 10000 tsecr 0 wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp syn ack mss 1460 wscale 7 sack_perm tsval 20000 tsecr 10000 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack win 512 tsval 10002 tsecr 20000 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp psh ack win 512 tsval 10005 tsecr 20000 payload "GET /v1/status HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.internal\r\n\r\n" wait 2ms
    c <- s tcp psh ack win 512 tsval 20005 tsecr 10005 payload "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nOK" wait 2ms
    c -> s tcp fin ack win 512 tsval 10010 tsecr 20005 wait 1ms
    c <- s tcp fin ack win 512 tsval 20010 tsecr 10010 wait 1ms
    c -> s tcp ack win 512 tsval 10012 tsecr 20010
}

compile {
    tcp_full_lifecycle(app_client, api_server)
}
```

### Example B: ECN Congestion Signaling, Urgent Pointer, Zero-Window & `RST` Abort
```frameassembly
host sender_v6   { ip 2001:db8:40::10 }
host receiver_v6 { ip 2001:db8:40::20 }

flow tcp_edge_cases(a, b) {
    a -> b tcp syn ece cwr srcport 58000 dstport 9000 ecn 2 wait 1ms
    a <- b tcp syn ack ece ecn 2 wait 1ms
    a -> b tcp psh ack ecn 3 payload "CONGESTED_BURST" wait 1ms
    a <- b tcp ack ece window 16384 ecn 2 wait 1ms
    a -> b tcp psh ack cwr window 32768 ecn 2 payload "CWND_REDUCED" wait 1ms
    a -> b tcp psh ack urg urgent 1 payload "!" wait 1ms
    a <- b tcp ack window 0 wait 5ms
    a -> b tcp rst ack window 0
}

compile {
    tcp_edge_cases(sender_v6, receiver_v6)
}
```

---

## 2. User Datagram Protocol (`UDP` — RFC 768)

Provides connectionless datagram framing with automatic port reversal across `<-` arrows and automatic multicast MAC derivation when targeting multicast IPs.
* **Modifiers:** `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>`, `TRANSPORT UDP` (for dual-transport L7 protocols), `PAYLOAD "<str>"`, `HEXPAYLOAD "<hex>"`.

```frameassembly
host worker_a   { ip 10.88.1.10 }
host worker_b   { ip 10.88.1.20 }
host feed_mcast { ip 239.192.10.1 }

flow udp_unicast_and_mcast(a, b, mcast) {
    a -> b vlan 88 pcp 3 dscp 26 udp srcport 51001 dstport 4791 payload "RDMA_WRITE_QP_101" wait 200us
    a <- b vlan 88 pcp 3 dscp 26 udp payload "RDMA_ACK_PSN_101" wait 500us
    a -> mcast dscp 34 udp srcport 30001 dstport 15500 hexpayload "01020304deadbeef"
}

compile {
    udp_unicast_and_mcast(worker_a, worker_b, feed_mcast)
}
```

---

## 3. Stream Control Transmission Protocol (`SCTP` — RFC 9260)

Used across 5G Core (`NGAP` port `38412`), 4G LTE (`S1AP` port `36412`, `Diameter` port `3868`), Telecom SS7 SIGTRAN (`M3UA` port `2905`), and WebRTC DataChannels (`5000`).

| Modifier | Syntax | Description & Common Values |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chunk Type** | `CHUNK <TYPE>` | `INIT`, `INIT_ACK`, `COOKIE_ECHO`, `COOKIE_ACK`, `DATA`, `SACK`, `HEARTBEAT`, `HEARTBEAT_ACK`, `SHUTDOWN`, `ABORT` |
| **Verification Tag**| `VTAG <u32>` | 32-bit association tag (`0` on `INIT`, peer tag thereafter) |
| **Stream & Seq** | `STREAM <u16>`, `SSN <u16>`, `TSN <u32>` (`SEQ <u32>`) | Stream ID, Stream Sequence Number, and Transmission Sequence Number |
| **Payload Proto ID**| `PPID <u32>` | `60` = 5G NGAP, `18` = S1AP, `27` = X2AP, `3` = M3UA, `46` = Diameter, `50` = WebRTC DCEP, `51` = WebRTC String |

```frameassembly
host gnb_n2 { ip 10.50.2.10 }
host amf_n2 { ip 10.50.2.1 }

flow sctp_5g_ngap_session(gnb, amf) {
    gnb -> amf dscp 46 sctp chunk init vtag 0 srcport 38412 dstport 38412 wait 1ms
    gnb <- amf dscp 46 sctp chunk init_ack vtag 3841201 wait 1ms
    gnb -> amf dscp 46 sctp chunk cookie_echo vtag 3841201 payload "STATE_COOKIE_5G" wait 1ms
    gnb <- amf dscp 46 sctp chunk cookie_ack vtag 3841201 wait 1ms
    gnb -> amf dscp 46 sctp chunk data vtag 3841201 seq 100 stream 0 ssn 0 ppid 60 payload "NGAP_NG_SETUP_REQ" wait 2ms
    gnb <- amf dscp 46 sctp chunk sack vtag 3841201 seq 100 wait 5ms
    gnb -> amf dscp 46 sctp chunk heartbeat vtag 3841201 payload "PATH_PRIMARY" wait 2ms
    gnb <- amf dscp 46 sctp chunk heartbeat_ack vtag 3841201 payload "PATH_PRIMARY" wait 2ms
    gnb -> amf dscp 46 sctp chunk shutdown vtag 3841201 seq 100
}

compile {
    sctp_5g_ngap_session(gnb_n2, amf_n2)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_snmp.md`

# Layer 7 Network Management: SNMPv1, SNMPv2c & SNMPv3 USM Reference

FrameAssembly dynamically encodes ASN.1 Basic Encoding Rules (BER) structures, SMIv1/SMIv2 variable bindings (`VARBIND`), and full RFC 3414 / 3826 / 7860 SNMPv3 User-based Security Model (USM) authentication and encryption across **SNMPv1 (`SNMP1`)**, **SNMPv2c (`SNMP2`)**, and **SNMPv3 (`SNMP3`)**.

| Protocol | Keyword | Default UDP Ports | Security Model | Supported PDU Types |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SNMPv1** | `SNMP1` | `161` (Poll), `162` (Trap) | Community (`COMMUNITY`) | `GET`, `GETNEXT`, `SET`, `RESPONSE`, `TRAP` |
| **SNMPv2c**| `SNMP2` | `161` (Poll), `162` (Trap/Inform)| Community (`COMMUNITY`) | `GET`, `GETNEXT`, `GETBULK`, `SET`, `RESPONSE`, `TRAP`, `INFORM` |
| **SNMPv3** | `SNMP3` | `161` (Poll), `162` (Trap/Inform)| USM (`noAuthNoPriv`, `authNoPriv`, `authPriv`)| `GET`, `GETNEXT`, `GETBULK`, `SET`, `RESPONSE`, `TRAP`, `INFORM`, `REPORT` |

---

## 1. Shared Modifiers & All 9 `VARBIND` Data Types

* **PDU Type:** `GET`, `GETNEXT`, `GETBULK`, `SET`, `RESPONSE`, `TRAP`, `INFORM`, `REPORT` *(write `GETNEXT` and `GETBULK` without underscores)*.
* **Correlation & Uptime:** `REQID <u32>` *(no underscore)*, `SYSUPTIME <u32>` *(in 1/100ths of a second)*, `OID <oid>`.
* **OID Formatting:** Both unquoted (`1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0`) and quoted (`"1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0"`) OIDs are accepted. Root arcs must follow standard ITU-T X.690 rules (`0..=2`, with second arc `< 40` under roots `0` and `1`).

Every SNMP statement can include zero, one, or multiple `VARBIND <oid> <TYPE> [value]` clauses:

| `VARBIND` Type | Example Syntax | Wire Tag & Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NULL` or `NULLVAL` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 null` | `0x05` ASN.1 NULL (used in `GET`/`GETNEXT`/`GETBULK` queries) |
| `STRING` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "core-rtr-01"` | `0x04` OCTET STRING (UTF-8 / ASCII text) |
| `INT` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.1 int 2` | `0x02` Signed 32-bit INTEGER (e.g. `1`=up, `2`=down) |
| `TIMETICKS` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 timeticks 8640000` | `0x43` TimeTicks in hundredths of a second |
| `IPVAL` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.20.1.1.10.0.0.1 ipval 10.0.0.1`| `0x40` IPv4 (4B) or IPv6 (16B) address |
| `OIDVAL` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 oidval 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.1` | `0x06` OBJECT IDENTIFIER value |
| `COUNTER32` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.1 counter32 4590123` | `0x41` 32-bit monotonically increasing counter |
| `GAUGE32` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 gauge32 1000000000` | `0x42` 32-bit non-wrapping gauge (speed, CPU, temp) |
| `COUNTER64` | `varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6.1 counter64 98765432100`| `0x46` 64-bit high-capacity counter (`ifHCInOctets`) |

---

## 2. SNMPv1 (`SNMP1` — RFC 1157)

SNMPv1 uses plaintext community strings (`COMMUNITY "<str>"`, default `"public"`) and a dedicated v1 `Trap-PDU` header:
* `ENTERPRISE <oid>`: Originating vendor/object OID (e.g. `1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.1`).
* `AGENTIP <ipv4>`: Originating IPv4 address inside the v1 Trap header.
* `GENTRAP <0..6>`: `0`=coldStart, `1`=warmStart, `2`=linkDown, `3`=linkUp, `4`=authenticationFailure, `5`=egpNeighborLoss, `6`=enterpriseSpecific.
* `SPECTRAP <u32>`: Vendor-specific trap code when `GENTRAP` is `6`.

```frameassembly
host nms_poller    { ip 10.100.1.10 }
host legacy_switch { ip 10.100.1.50 }

flow snmpv1_poll_and_traps(nms, sw) {
    nms -> sw snmp1 get community "public" reqid 1001 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 null wait 2ms
    nms <- sw snmp1 response community "public" reqid 1001 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 string "C2960 Software Version 15.2" wait 5ms

    // LinkDown trap (gentrap 2) and Enterprise-Specific trap (gentrap 6, spectrap 1)
    nms <- sw snmp1 trap community "public" enterprise 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.1.716 agentip 10.100.1.50 gentrap 2 spectrap 0 sysuptime 4320500 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.5 int 5 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.5 int 2 wait 2ms
    nms <- sw snmp1 trap community "public" enterprise 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.43.2 agentip 10.100.1.50 gentrap 6 spectrap 1 sysuptime 4321000 varbind 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.43.1.1.6.1.3.1 int 1
}

compile {
    snmpv1_poll_and_traps(nms_poller, legacy_switch)
}
```

---

## 3. SNMPv2c (`SNMP2` — RFC 3416)

Adds bulk table walks (`GETBULK` with `NONREPEATERS <u32>` and `MAXREPETITIONS <u32>`), 64-bit counters (`COUNTER64`), standard `TRAP` PDUs, and acknowledged `INFORM` notifications:

```frameassembly
host collector    { ip 172.16.10.10 }
host spine_router { ip 172.16.10.1 }

flow snmpv2c_bulk_trap_inform(nms, rtr) {
    nms -> rtr snmp2 getbulk community "spine_ro" reqid 2001 nonrepeaters 1 maxrepetitions 15 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 null varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6 null wait 2ms
    nms <- rtr snmp2 response community "spine_ro" reqid 2001 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 timeticks 9950000 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6.1 counter64 1844674407370955100 wait 5ms

    nms <- rtr snmp2 trap community "spine_trap" reqid 2002 sysuptime 9950050 oid 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.1 int 1 wait 2ms
    nms <- rtr snmp2 inform community "spine_inform" reqid 2003 sysuptime 9950100 oid 1.3.6.1.2.1.15.7.1 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.15.3.1.2.192.0.2.1 int 6 wait 2ms
    nms -> rtr snmp2 response community "spine_inform" reqid 2003 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.15.3.1.2.192.0.2.1 int 6
}

compile {
    snmpv2c_bulk_trap_inform(collector, spine_router)
}
```

---

## 4. SNMPv3 USM Authentication & Encryption (`SNMP3`)

FrameAssembly derives localized authentication and privacy keys (`Ku` $\to$ `Kul`) from your passphrases and `ENGINEID`, encrypts the `scopedPDU` (`DES-CBC` or `AES-128-CFB`), and computes the truncated HMAC digest over the full message. To inspect encrypted payloads in Wireshark, add the same Username, EngineID, Auth protocol/password, and Priv protocol/password under *Edit $\rightarrow$ Preferences $\rightarrow$ Protocols $\rightarrow$ SNMP $\rightarrow$ Users Table*.

| Modifier | Syntax | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Username** | `USER "<username>"` | USM username (`""` for Engine ID discovery) |
| **Engine ID** | `ENGINEID "<hex>"` | Authoritative Engine ID hex string (e.g. `"80001f888055667788"`) |
| **Engine Timeline**| `ENGINEBOOTS <u32>`, `ENGINETIME <u32>`| Reboot count and seconds since boot (for replay protection) |
| **Context Name** | `CONTEXTNAME "<str>"` | Optional VRF / VLAN MIB context inside `scopedPDU` |
| **Authentication**| `AUTH <MD5\|SHA\|SHA256\|SHA384\|SHA512> "<pass>"`| Enables `authFlag` and signs the message |
| **Encryption** | `PRIV <DES\|AES> "<pass>"` | Enables `privFlag` and encrypts `scopedPDU` (requires `AUTH`) |

> **Syntax Rule:** Keep the algorithm identifier in `AUTH` and `PRIV` **unquoted**—for example: `auth sha256 "MyAuthPass!" priv aes "MyPrivPass!"` (never put quotes around `sha256` or `aes`).

```frameassembly
host noc_mgr    { ip 10.254.0.10 }
host core_agent { ip 10.254.0.1 }

flow snmpv3_security_levels(mgr, agent) {
    // 1. Unauthenticated Engine ID discovery (noAuthNoPriv)
    mgr -> agent snmp3 get user "" engineid "" engineboots 0 enginetime 0 reqid 3001 wait 2ms
    mgr <- agent snmp3 response user "" engineid "80001f8880aabbccddeeff" engineboots 12 enginetime 86400 reqid 3001 varbind 1.3.6.1.6.3.15.1.1.4.0 int 1 wait 2ms

    // 2. Signed poll without encryption (authNoPriv - HMAC-SHA256)
    mgr -> agent snmp3 get user "auditor_ro" engineid "80001f8880aabbccddeeff" engineboots 12 enginetime 86401 auth sha256 "AuditSha256Pass!" reqid 3002 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 null wait 2ms
    mgr <- agent snmp3 response user "auditor_ro" engineid "80001f8880aabbccddeeff" engineboots 12 enginetime 86401 auth sha256 "AuditSha256Pass!" reqid 3002 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "core-rtr-01.prod" wait 2ms

    // 3. Signed & encrypted SET and TRAP (authPriv - HMAC-SHA512 + AES-128)
    mgr -> agent snmp3 set user "netadmin_rw" engineid "80001f8880aabbccddeeff" engineboots 12 enginetime 86402 contextname "vrf-prod" auth sha512 "AdminSha512Key!" priv aes "AdminAes128Key!" reqid 3003 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.4.0 string "noc@example.com" wait 2ms
    mgr <- agent snmp3 trap user "netadmin_rw" engineid "80001f8880aabbccddeeff" engineboots 12 enginetime 86405 contextname "vrf-prod" auth sha512 "AdminSha512Key!" priv aes "AdminAes128Key!" reqid 3004 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 timeticks 8640500 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6.1 counter64 9988776655443322
}

compile {
    snmpv3_security_levels(noc_mgr, core_agent)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`

# Layer 7 Infrastructure, Time, AAA, Flow Telemetry & CLI Reference

This guide covers **16 core network infrastructure, precision time, AAA authentication, logging/flow export, and remote administration protocols** across IPv4 and IPv6.

---

## 1. Naming & Address Assignment (`DNS`, `MDNS`, `DHCP`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Wire Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`DNS`** | UDP / TCP `53` | `QUERY` / `RESPONSE` *(0-arg flags)*, `TXID <u16>`, `QNAME "<domain>"`, `QTYPE "<A\|AAAA\|PTR\|MX\|TXT\|SRV\|CNAME\|SOA\|AXFR>"`, `RDATA "<val>"`, `RCODE <u8>` (`0`=NOERROR, `3`=NXDOMAIN, `5`=REFUSED), `ANS_TTL <u32>`, `TRANSPORT TCP` |
| **`MDNS`** | UDP `5353` | Same modifiers as `DNS`; automatically targets multicast `224.0.0.251` (`01:00:5e:00:00:fb`) or `ff02::fb` (`33:33:00:00:00:fb`) with default `TXID 0` |
| **`DHCP`** | UDP `68`/`67` (v4), `546`/`547` (v6) | v4 flags: `DISCOVER`, `OFFER`, `REQUEST`, `ACK`, `RELEASE`. v6 flags: `SOLICIT`, `ADVERTISE`, `REQUEST`, `REPLY`. Fields: `XID <u32>` / `TXID <u32>`, `CHADDR <mac>`, `CIADDR <ip>`, `YIADDR <ip>`, `SIADDR <ip>`, `HOSTNAME "<str>"`, `SUBNET_MASK <ip>`, `ROUTER <ip>`, `DNS_SERVER <ip>`, `LEASE_TIME <u32>` |

> **Syntax Rule:** In `DNS` and `MDNS`, `QUERY` and `RESPONSE` take no inline string—always pass the domain name with `QNAME "<domain>"`.

```frameassembly
host client_v4 { ip 192.168.20.100 mac 00:50:56:20:00:64 }
host infra_v4  { ip 192.168.20.1   mac 00:50:56:20:00:01 }
host client_v6 { ip 2001:db8:20::100 mac 00:50:56:62:00:64 }
host infra_v6  { ip 2001:db8:20::1   mac 00:50:56:62:00:01 }

flow dhcp_dns_mdns_onboarding(c4, s4, c6, s6) {
    // DHCPv4 DORA lease + DNS A lookup + DNS TCP AXFR + mDNS printer discovery
    c4 -> s4 dhcp discover chaddr 00:50:56:20:00:64 hostname "eng-ws-01" wait 2ms
    c4 <- s4 dhcp offer yiaddr 192.168.20.100 siaddr 192.168.20.1 chaddr 00:50:56:20:00:64 subnet_mask 255.255.255.0 router 192.168.20.1 dns_server 192.168.20.1 lease_time 86400 wait 2ms
    c4 -> s4 dhcp request ciaddr 192.168.20.100 yiaddr 192.168.20.100 chaddr 00:50:56:20:00:64 wait 2ms
    c4 <- s4 dhcp ack yiaddr 192.168.20.100 chaddr 00:50:56:20:00:64 subnet_mask 255.255.255.0 router 192.168.20.1 dns_server 192.168.20.1 lease_time 86400 wait 2ms
    c4 -> s4 dns query txid 1010 qname "git.corp.example.com" qtype "A" wait 1ms
    c4 <- s4 dns response txid 1010 qname "git.corp.example.com" qtype "A" rdata "192.168.20.55" rcode 0 ans_ttl 300 wait 1ms
    c4 -> s4 transport tcp dns query txid 1011 qname "corp.example.com" qtype "AXFR" wait 2ms
    c4 -> s4 mdns query qname "_ipp._tcp.local" qtype "PTR" wait 2ms

    // DHCPv6 SARR lease + DNS AAAA lookup
    c6 -> s6 dhcp solicit chaddr 00:50:56:62:00:64 hostname "eng-ws-01-v6" wait 2ms
    c6 <- s6 dhcp advertise yiaddr 2001:db8:20::100 dns_server 2001:db8:20::1 lease_time 86400 wait 2ms
    c6 -> s6 dhcp request hostname "eng-ws-01-v6" wait 2ms
    c6 <- s6 dhcp reply yiaddr 2001:db8:20::100 dns_server 2001:db8:20::1 lease_time 86400 wait 2ms
    c6 -> s6 dns query txid 2020 qname "git.corp.example.com" qtype "AAAA" wait 1ms
    c6 <- s6 dns response txid 2020 qname "git.corp.example.com" qtype "AAAA" rdata "2001:db8:20::55" rcode 0 ans_ttl 300
}

compile {
    dhcp_dns_mdns_onboarding(client_v4, infra_v4, client_v6, infra_v6)
}
```

---

## 2. Precision Time Synchronization (`NTP` & `PTP`)

* **`NTP` (UDP 123):** `LI <0..3>`, `VN <1..4>` (`4` default), `MODE <1..7>` (`3`=Client, `4`=Server, `5`=Broadcast), `STRATUM <0..16>` (`1`=Primary GPS/Atomic, `16`=Unsynchronized), `POLL <u8>`, `PRECISION <i8>`, `REFID "<4char>"`, `TX_TIMESTAMP <u64>`.
* **`PTP` (IEEE 1588v2):** Automatically routes time-critical Event frames (`SYNC`, `DELAY_REQ`) to **UDP port `319`** and General frames (`FOLLOW_UP`, `DELAY_RESP`, `ANNOUNCE`) to **UDP port `320`**. Modifiers: `DOMAIN <u8>`, `SEQ_ID <u16>`, `CLOCK_ID "<eui64>"`, `VERSION <u8>`.

```frameassembly
host grandmaster { ip 10.158.0.1 }
host follower    { ip 10.158.0.50 }

flow clock_synchronization(gm, sub) {
    sub -> gm dscp 46 ntp li 0 vn 4 mode 3 stratum 2 poll 6 refid "INIT" tx_timestamp 0xe9b0000100000000 wait 1ms
    sub <- gm dscp 46 ntp li 0 vn 4 mode 4 stratum 1 poll 6 refid "GPS" tx_timestamp 0xe9b0000100001000 wait 2ms

    gm -> sub dscp 46 ptp announce domain 0 seq_id 500 clock_id "00:1c:73:ff:fe:00:01:01" wait 500us
    gm -> sub dscp 46 ptp sync domain 0 seq_id 501 clock_id "00:1c:73:ff:fe:00:01:01" wait 100us
    gm -> sub dscp 46 ptp follow_up domain 0 seq_id 501 clock_id "00:1c:73:ff:fe:00:01:01" wait 200us
    sub -> gm dscp 46 ptp delay_req domain 0 seq_id 501 clock_id "00:1c:73:ff:fe:00:01:50" wait 200us
    gm -> sub dscp 46 ptp delay_resp domain 0 seq_id 501 clock_id "00:1c:73:ff:fe:00:01:01"
}

compile {
    clock_synchronization(grandmaster, follower)
}
```

---

## 3. AAA Access Security (`RADIUS` & `TACACS`)

* **`RADIUS`:** Automatically routes Authentication packets (`ACCESS_REQUEST`, `ACCESS_ACCEPT`, `ACCESS_REJECT`, `ACCESS_CHALLENGE`) to **UDP port `1812`** and Accounting packets (`ACCOUNTING_REQUEST`, `ACCOUNTING_RESPONSE`) to **UDP port `1813`**. Supports `ID <u8>`, `USER "<str>"`, `NAS_IP <ip>`, `FRAMED_IP <ip>` (automatically emitting IPv4 Attributes `4`/`8` or IPv6 Attributes `95`/`168`), and `SERVICE_TYPE <u32>`.
* **`TACACS` (TCP 49):** `AUTHEN`, `AUTHOR`, `ACCT` (or `TYPE <AUTHEN|AUTHOR|ACCT>`), `SEQ <u8>`, `FLAGS <u8>`, `SESSION_ID <u32>`, `USER "<str>"`, `PAYLOAD "<str>"`.

```frameassembly
host nas_switch { ip 10.60.1.10 }
host aaa_server { ip 10.60.1.200 }

flow radius_and_tacacs_audit(nas, aaa) {
    nas -> aaa radius access_request id 10 user "alice@corp.local" nas_ip 10.60.1.10 service_type 2 wait 2ms
    nas <- aaa radius access_accept id 10 user "alice@corp.local" framed_ip 10.60.20.55 wait 2ms
    nas -> aaa radius accounting_request id 11 user "alice@corp.local" nas_ip 10.60.1.10 framed_ip 10.60.20.55 wait 2ms
    nas <- aaa radius accounting_response id 11 wait 5ms

    nas -> aaa tacacs author session_id 900102 user "netadmin" payload "cmd=configure;cmd-arg=terminal" wait 2ms
    nas <- aaa tacacs author session_id 900102 user "netadmin" payload "AUTHOR_STATUS_PASS_ADD"
}

compile {
    radius_and_tacacs_audit(nas_switch, aaa_server)
}
```

---

## 4. Logging & Flow Telemetry (`SYSLOG`, `NETFLOW`, `IPFIX`, `SFLOW`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`SYSLOG`** | UDP / TCP `514` | `FACILITY <0..23>`, `SEVERITY <0..7>` (`0`=Emerg .. `7`=Debug), `PRI <0..191>` (`FACILITY * 8 + SEVERITY` if omitted), `HOSTNAME "<str>"`, `APP "<str>"`, `PROCID "<str>"`, `MSG "<text>"`, `TRANSPORT TCP` |
| **`NETFLOW`**| UDP `2055` | NetFlow v5 record: `SRCIP <ip>`, `DSTIP <ip>`, `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>`, `PROTO <u8>`, `PACKETS <u32>`, `OCTETS <u32>` |
| **`IPFIX`** | UDP / TCP `4739` | Dual-stack v10 flow record: `DOMAIN_ID <u32>`, `SRCIP <ip>`, `DSTIP <ip>`, `SRCPORT <u16>`, `DSTPORT <u16>`, `PROTO <u8>`, `PACKETS <u32>`, `OCTETS <u32>` |
| **`SFLOW`** | UDP `6343` | sFlow v5 Flow Sample: `AGENT_IP <ip>`, `SUB_AGENT_ID <u32>`, `SEQ <u32>`, `UPTIME <u32>`, `SAMPLES <u32>` |

```frameassembly
host core_exporter { ip 10.250.10.1 }
host collector     { ip 10.250.10.100 }

flow observability_export(rtr, col) {
    rtr -> col syslog facility 16 severity 4 hostname "core-rtr-01" app "bgpd" procid "1842" msg "Neighbor 198.51.100.1 Up" wait 1ms
    rtr -> col netflow srcip 198.51.100.25 dstip 203.0.113.80 srcport 51200 dstport 443 proto 6 packets 15400 octets 21560000 wait 1ms
    rtr -> col ipfix domain_id 4001 srcip 198.51.100.25 dstip 203.0.113.80 srcport 51200 dstport 443 proto 6 packets 15400 octets 21560000 wait 1ms
    rtr -> col sflow agent_ip 10.250.10.1 sub_agent_id 1 uptime 86400000 samples 8
}

compile {
    observability_export(core_exporter, collector)
}
```

---

## 5. File Transfer, Remote CLI & Registry (`TFTP`, `FTP`, `SSH`, `TELNET`, `WHOIS`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Syntax Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`TFTP`** | UDP `69` | `RRQ`, `WRQ`, `DATA`, `ACK`, `FILENAME "<str>"`, `MODE "<octet\|netascii>"`, `BLOCK <u16>`, `ERRCODE <u16>`, `ERRMSG "<str>"` |
| **`FTP`** | TCP `21` | `CMD "<USER\|PASS\|EPSV\|RETR\|STOR\|QUIT>"`, `ARG "<str>"`, `CODE <u16>` (`220`, `230`, `226`), `REPLY "<str>"` |
| **`SSH`** | TCP `22` | `BANNER "<str>"` (e.g. `"SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.8p1"`), `KEXINIT`, `NEWKEYS`, `MSG_CODE <u8>` |
| **`TELNET`** | TCP `23` | `WILL <u8>`, `WONT <u8>`, `DO <u8>`, `DONT <u8>`, `OPTION <u8>` *(pass option code integer directly, e.g. `DO 1 WILL 3`)*, `PAYLOAD "<str>"` |
| **`WHOIS`** | TCP `43` | `QUERY` / `RESPONSE` *(0-arg flags)*, `DOMAIN "<domain_or_asn>"`, `REGISTRAR "<str>"` |

```frameassembly
host bastion { ip 10.70.1.50 }
host server  { ip 10.70.1.10 }

flow remote_cli_and_transfers(adm, srv) {
    adm -> srv ssh banner "SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.8p1" wait 1ms
    adm <- srv ssh banner "SSH-2.0-Cisco-2.0" wait 1ms
    adm -> srv ssh kexinit payload "curve25519-sha256" wait 1ms
    adm <- srv ssh newkeys wait 2ms

    adm <- srv telnet do 24 will 1 option 3 payload "Username: " wait 1ms
    adm -> srv telnet will 24 do 3 payload "admin\r\n" wait 2ms

    adm -> srv tftp rrq filename "nos-image.bin" mode "octet" wait 1ms
    adm <- srv tftp data block 1 payload "FIRMWARE_BLOCK_0001" wait 1ms
    adm -> srv tftp ack block 1 wait 2ms

    adm <- srv ftp code 220 reply "vsFTPd Ready" wait 1ms
    adm -> srv ftp cmd "USER" arg "backup_ops" wait 1ms
    adm <- srv ftp code 230 reply "Login successful" wait 2ms

    adm -> srv whois query domain "AS65001" registrar "whois.arin.net" wait 1ms
    adm <- srv whois response domain "AS65001" registrar "whois.arin.net"
}

compile {
    remote_cli_and_transfers(bastion, server)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_web_and_cloud.md`

# Layer 7 Web, Cloud, TLS/QUIC, VoIP Media & IoT Messaging Reference

This guide covers **14 web, microservice, encrypted transport, real-time VoIP/streaming, and IoT messaging protocols** across IPv4 and IPv6. *(For `SSH`, `TELNET`, `TFTP`, `FTP`, and `WHOIS`, see [`l7_infra_and_telemetry.md`](l7_infra_and_telemetry.md).)*

---

## 1. Web, API & Microservice Protocols (`HTTP`, `HTTP2`, `GRPC`, `WEBSOCKET`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Wire Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`HTTP`** | TCP `80` | `GET` / `POST` / `PUT` / `DELETE` / `HEAD` / `OPTIONS` / `PATCH` (or `METHOD "<verb>"`), `URI "<path>"`, `HOST_HDR "<host>"` *(never write `HOST` inside `HTTP`)*, `USER_AGENT "<ua>"`, `CONTENT_TYPE "<mime>"`, `HEADER "<Key>" "<Val>"`, `STATUS <u16>`, `REASON "<str>"`, `BODY "<str>"` (auto-adds `Content-Length`) |
| **`HTTP2`** | TCP `443` | `PREFACE` (24B `"PRI * HTTP/2.0..."`), `SETTINGS`, `HEADERS`, `DATA`, `WINDOW_UPDATE`, `PING`, `GOAWAY`, `STREAM_ID <u32>` (`0` control, odd `1, 3, 5` requests) |
| **`GRPC`** | TCP `50051` | 5-byte length-prefixed framing: `SERVICE "<pkg.Svc>"`, `METHOD "<Rpc>"`, `GRPC_STATUS <0..16>` (`0`=OK, `14`=UNAVAILABLE), `PAYLOAD "<str>"` |
| **`WEBSOCKET`**| TCP `80` | `OPCODE "<TEXT\|BINARY\|CLOSE\|PING\|PONG>"` (or bare `TEXT`, `BINARY`, `CLOSE`, `PING`, `PONG`), `FIN_BIT <0\|1>`, `MASK_KEY <u32>` (auto-XORs payload bytes), `PAYLOAD "<str>"` |

```frameassembly
host ingress_gw { ip 10.120.1.10 }
host mesh_pod   { ip 10.120.1.50 }

flow web_and_service_mesh(gw, pod) {
    gw -> pod http method "POST" uri "/v1/checkout" host_hdr "api.shop.example.com" user_agent "Envoy/1.31" content_type "application/json" header "X-Request-Id" "req-99" body "{\"cart_id\":42}" wait 1ms
    gw <- pod http status 201 reason "Created" content_type "application/json" body "{\"order_id\":8801}" wait 2ms

    gw -> pod http2 preface settings stream_id 0 wait 1ms
    gw <- pod http2 settings window_update stream_id 0 wait 1ms
    gw -> pod http2 headers stream_id 1 payload ":method GET :path /v2/catalog" wait 1ms
    gw <- pod http2 goaway stream_id 0 wait 2ms

    gw -> pod grpc service "payment.v1.Ledger" method "Authorize" payload "PROTOBUF_REQ" wait 1ms
    gw <- pod grpc service "payment.v1.Ledger" method "Authorize" grpc_status 0 payload "PROTOBUF_OK" wait 2ms

    gw -> pod websocket opcode "TEXT" fin_bit 1 mask_key 0x37fa213d payload "{\"sub\":\" alerts\"}" wait 1ms
    gw <- pod websocket opcode "TEXT" fin_bit 1 payload "{\"status\":\"subscribed\"}"
}

compile {
    web_and_service_mesh(ingress_gw, mesh_pod)
}
```

---

## 2. Cryptographic & Next-Gen Web Transport (`TLS` & `QUIC`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Syntax Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`TLS`** | TCP `443` | `CLIENT_HELLO`, `SERVER_HELLO`, `CERTIFICATE`, `FINISHED`, `APP_DATA`, `ALERT`, `RECORD_VERSION <u16>` (`0x0301`=1.0, `0x0303`=1.2), `HANDSHAKE_VERSION <u16>`, `SNI "<hostname>"`, `CIPHERSUITE <u16>` (`4865`=AES_128_GCM, `4866`=AES_256_GCM, `4867`=CHACHA20), `ALPN "<h2\|http/1.1>"` |
| **`QUIC`** | UDP `443` | `INITIAL`, `ZERO_RTT`, `HANDSHAKE`, `RETRY`, `SHORT`, `VERSION <u32>` (`1` default), `DCID <u64>`, `SCID <u64>` *(64-bit integer/hex literals, never quoted strings)*, `PKT_NUM <u32>`, `TOKEN "<str>"` |

```frameassembly
host client_v6   { ip 2001:db8:443::50 }
host cdn_edge_v6 { ip 2001:db8:443::1 }

flow tls13_and_quic_v1(c, s) {
    // TLS 1.3 handshake with SNI + ALPN h2, encrypted AppData, and close_notify Alert
    c -> s tls client_hello record_version 0x0301 handshake_version 0x0303 sni "edge.cdn.example.com" ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls server_hello record_version 0x0303 handshake_version 0x0303 ciphersuite 4866 alpn "h2" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls certificate record_version 0x0303 payload "X509_CERT_CHAIN" wait 1ms
    c <- s tls finished record_version 0x0303 payload "SERVER_VERIFY_DATA" wait 1ms
    c -> s tls finished record_version 0x0303 payload "CLIENT_VERIFY_DATA" wait 1ms
    c -> s tls app_data record_version 0x0303 payload "ENCRYPTED_H2_GET" wait 1ms
    c -> s tls alert record_version 0x0303 payload "CLOSE_NOTIFY" wait 5ms

    // QUIC v1 Initial -> Retry -> 0-RTT -> Handshake -> 1-RTT Short Header
    c -> s quic initial dcid 0x8394c8f03e515708 scid 0x1122334455667788 pkt_num 1 payload "QUIC_CLIENT_HELLO" wait 1ms
    c <- s quic retry dcid 0x1122334455667788 scid 0x9988776655443322 payload "retry_token_v1" wait 1ms
    c -> s quic zero_rtt dcid 0x9988776655443322 scid 0x1122334455667788 pkt_num 2 payload "HTTP3_EARLY_GET" wait 1ms
    c <- s quic handshake dcid 0x1122334455667788 scid 0x9988776655443322 pkt_num 1 payload "QUIC_SERVER_FINISHED" wait 1ms
    c <- s quic short dcid 0x1122334455667788 pkt_num 2 payload "HTTP3_200_OK"
}

compile {
    tls13_and_quic_v1(client_v6, cdn_edge_v6)
}
```

---

## 3. Real-Time VoIP, NAT Traversal & Media (`STUN`, `SIP`, `RTP`, `RTSP`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Syntax Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`STUN`** | UDP `3478` | `BINDING_REQUEST`, `BINDING_RESPONSE`, `BINDING_ERROR`, `XOR_MAPPED_ADDR <ip>` *(takes IPv4/IPv6 address only, never a port)*, `SOFTWARE "<str>"`, `TXID <u32>` |
| **`SIP`** | UDP / TCP `5060` | `INVITE`, `BYE`, `CANCEL`, `METHOD "<ACK\|REGISTER\|OPTIONS>"`, `URI "<sip_uri>"`, `FROM "<uri>"`, `TO "<uri>"`, `CALL_ID "<id>"`, `CSEQ <u32>`, `VIA "<str>"`, `CONTACT "<str>"`, `CONTENT_TYPE "<str>"`, `STATUS <u16>`, `REASON "<str>"`, `BODY "<sdp>"`, `TRANSPORT TCP` |
| **`RTP`** | UDP `5004` | `PT <0..127>` (`0`=PCMU, `96`=Opus/H.264), `SEQ <u16>`, `TIMESTAMP <u32>`, `SSRC <u32>`, `MARKER <0\|1>` *(write `RTP ...` directly, never `UDP ... RTP ...`)* |
| **`RTSP`** | TCP `554` | `OPTIONS`, `DESCRIBE`, `SETUP`, `PLAY`, `TEARDOWN` (or `METHOD "<verb>"`), `URI "<rtsp_url>"`, `CSEQ <u32>`, `TRANSPORT_HDR "<str>"`, `SESSION "<id>"`, `STATUS <u16>` |

```frameassembly
host media_client { ip 10.80.1.50 }
host sbc_server   { ip 10.80.1.10 }

flow voip_and_rtsp_session(c, s) {
    c -> s stun binding_request software "WebRTC-Client/1.0" wait 1ms
    c <- s stun binding_response xor_mapped_addr 203.0.113.50 software "Coturn-4.6" wait 2ms

    c -> s dscp 24 sip invite uri "sip:bob@example.com" from "sip:alice@example.com" to "sip:bob@example.com" call_id "call-99@10.80.1.50" cseq 1 via "SIP/2.0/UDP 10.80.1.50:5060" contact "sip:alice@10.80.1.50" content_type "application/sdp" body "v=0\r\nm=audio 16384 RTP/AVP 0\r\n" wait 2ms
    c <- s dscp 24 sip status 200 reason "OK" call_id "call-99@10.80.1.50" cseq 1 wait 2ms
    c -> s dscp 24 sip method "ACK" uri "sip:bob@example.com" call_id "call-99@10.80.1.50" cseq 1 wait 1ms
    c -> s dscp 46 rtp pt 0 seq 1001 timestamp 160 ssrc 0x11223344 marker 1 payload "G711_20MS_FRAME" wait 20ms
    c -> s dscp 24 sip bye uri "sip:bob@example.com" call_id "call-99@10.80.1.50" cseq 2 wait 2ms

    c -> s rtsp method "SETUP" uri "rtsp://10.80.1.10:554/cam01/track1" cseq 1 transport_hdr "RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port=5004-5005" wait 1ms
    c <- s rtsp status 200 cseq 1 session "sess-7788" wait 1ms
    c -> s rtsp method "PLAY" uri "rtsp://10.80.1.10:554/cam01" cseq 2 session "sess-7788"
}

compile {
    voip_and_rtsp_session(media_client, sbc_server)
}
```

---

## 4. IoT Messaging, Queues & UPnP Discovery (`MQTT`, `COAP`, `AMQP`, `SSDP`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`MQTT`** | TCP `1883` | `CONNECT`, `CONNACK`, `PUBLISH`, `PUBACK`, `SUBSCRIBE`, `SUBACK`, `PINGREQ`, `PINGRESP`, `DISCONNECT`, `CLIENT_ID "<id>"`, `TOPIC "<topic>"`, `QOS <0..2>`, `RETAIN`, `PKT_ID <u16>`, `RETURN_CODE <u8>` |
| **`COAP`** | UDP `5683` | `CON`, `NON`, `ACK`, `RST`, `CODE "<0.01\|0.02\|2.04\|2.05>"`, `MSGID <u16>`, `TOKEN <u32>`, `URI_PATH "<path>"`, `CONTENT_FORMAT <u16>` (`50`=`application/json`) |
| **`AMQP`** | TCP `5672` | `PROTOCOL_HEADER`, `CONNECTION_START`, `CHANNEL_OPEN`, `BASIC_PUBLISH`, `BASIC_DELIVER`, `HEARTBEAT`, `CHANNEL <u16>`, `EXCHANGE "<str>"`, `ROUTING_KEY "<str>"` |
| **`SSDP`** | UDP `1900` | `MSEARCH`, `NOTIFY`, `HOST_HDR "239.255.255.250:1900"`, `MAN "\"ssdp:discover\""`, `MX <u8>`, `ST "<target>"`, `NT "<type>"`, `NTS "<ssdp:alive\|ssdp:byebye>"`, `USN "<uuid>"`, `LOCATION "<url>"` |

```frameassembly
host iot_gw { ip 192.168.140.10 }
host broker { ip 192.168.140.1 }

flow iot_messaging_pipeline(edge, brk) {
    edge -> brk mqtt connect client_id "gw-floor2" wait 1ms
    edge <- brk mqtt connack return_code 0 wait 1ms
    edge -> brk mqtt publish pkt_id 10 topic "plant/floor2/temp" qos 1 retain payload "{\"temp_c\":23.8}" wait 1ms
    edge <- brk mqtt puback pkt_id 10 wait 2ms

    edge -> brk coap con code "0.02" msgid 401 token 0x99aabb uri_path "sensors/pressure" content_format 50 payload "{\"kpa\":101.3}" wait 1ms
    edge <- brk coap ack code "2.04" msgid 401 token 0x99aabb wait 2ms

    edge -> brk amqp protocol_header wait 1ms
    edge -> brk amqp basic_publish channel 1 exchange "telemetry" routing_key "alerts" payload "{\"ok\":true}" wait 2ms

    edge -> brk ssdp msearch host_hdr "239.255.255.250:1900" man "\"ssdp:discover\"" mx 3 st "upnp:rootdevice"
}

compile {
    iot_messaging_pipeline(iot_gw, broker)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_mail_auth_storage_db.md`

# Layer 7 Mail, Directory Auth, Storage, Caches & Databases Reference

This guide covers **11 enterprise email, Active Directory authentication, network file storage, key-value caching, and SQL database wire protocols** across IPv4 and IPv6. *(For `MQTT`, `COAP`, and `AMQP`, see [`l7_web_and_cloud.md`](l7_web_and_cloud.md).)*

---

## 1. Electronic Mail Suite (`SMTP`, `IMAP`, `POP3`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Syntax Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`SMTP`** | TCP `25` / `587` | `EHLO "<domain>"`, `HELO "<domain>"`, `MAIL_FROM` + `PARAM "<addr>"`, `RCPT_TO` + `PARAM "<addr>"` *(`MAIL_FROM` and `RCPT_TO` are 0-arg flags; pass the email address via `PARAM`)*, `QUIT`, `CODE <u16>`, `REPLY "<text>"`, `BODY "<mime_msg>"` |
| **`IMAP`** | TCP `143` / `993` | `TAG "<A001>"`, `CMD "<LOGIN\|SELECT\|FETCH\|LOGOUT>"`, `ARG "<args>"`, `STATUS "<OK\|NO\|BAD>"`, `RESPONSE "<str>"` (or `PAYLOAD "<line>"`) |
| **`POP3`** | TCP `110` / `995` | `CMD "<USER\|PASS\|STAT\|LIST\|RETR\|QUIT>"`, `ARG "<arg>"`, `OK`, `ERR`, `RESPONSE "<str>"` (or `PAYLOAD "<line>"`) |

```frameassembly
host mail_client { ip 10.30.1.50 }
host mail_server { ip 10.30.1.10 }

flow mail_submission_and_retrieval(mua, mta) {
    mua <- mta smtp code 220 reply "mx01.corp.example.com ESMTP Postfix" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp ehlo "ws01.corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "PIPELINING STARTTLS" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp mail_from param "alice@corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "2.1.0 Ok" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp rcpt_to param "bob@corp.example.com" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "2.1.5 Ok" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp body "Subject: Maintenance Window\r\n\r\nCore switch upgrade at 22:00." wait 2ms
    mua <- mta smtp code 250 reply "2.0.0 Queued" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta smtp quit wait 2ms

    mua -> mta imap tag "A001" cmd "LOGIN" arg "bob@corp.example.com SecretPass!" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta imap tag "A001" payload "A001 OK LOGIN completed" wait 1ms
    mua -> mta pop3 cmd "STAT" wait 1ms
    mua <- mta pop3 ok payload "4 18420"
}

compile {
    mail_submission_and_retrieval(mail_client, mail_server)
}
```

---

## 2. Enterprise Identity & Directory (`KERBEROS` & `LDAP`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Wire Encoding |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`KERBEROS`**| UDP / TCP `88` | ASN.1 DER Kerberos v5: `AS_REQ`, `AS_REP`, `TGS_REQ`, `TGS_REP`, `KRB_ERROR`, `REALM "<REALM>"`, `CNAME "<principal>"`, `SNAME "<service>"`, `ETYPE <u32>` (`18`=AES256, `17`=AES128, `23`=RC4) |
| **`LDAP`** | TCP `389` / `636`| ASN.1 BER LDAPv3: `BIND_REQ`, `BIND_RES`, `SEARCH_REQ` (encodes all 8 mandatory RFC 4511 fields), `SEARCH_ENTRY`, `SEARCH_DONE`, `UNBIND_REQ`, `MSGID <u32>`, `BASE_DN "<dn>"` *(never write `DN`)*, `FILTER "<filter>"`, `RESULT_CODE <u32>` (`0`=success, `49`=invalidCredentials) |

```frameassembly
host ad_workstation { ip 10.45.1.100 }
host domain_ctrl    { ip 10.45.1.10 }

flow active_directory_logon(ws, dc) {
    ws -> dc kerberos as_req realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "krbtgt/CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws <- dc kerberos as_rep realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "krbtgt/CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc kerberos tgs_req realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "ldap/dc01.corp.example.com" etype 18 wait 1ms
    ws <- dc kerberos tgs_rep realm "CORP.EXAMPLE.COM" cname "jdoe" sname "ldap/dc01.corp.example.com" etype 18 wait 2ms

    ws -> dc ldap bind_req msgid 1 base_dn "cn=jdoe,ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap bind_res msgid 1 result_code 0 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc ldap search_req msgid 2 base_dn "ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" filter "(&(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName=jdoe))" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap search_entry msgid 2 base_dn "cn=jdoe,ou=Users,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" payload "memberOf: cn=NetOps,ou=Groups,dc=corp,dc=example,dc=com" wait 1ms
    ws <- dc ldap search_done msgid 2 result_code 0 wait 1ms
    ws -> dc ldap unbind_req msgid 3
}

compile {
    active_directory_logon(ad_workstation, domain_ctrl)
}
```

---

## 3. Network File Storage (`SMB` & `NFS`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers & Wire Encoding |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`SMB`** | TCP `445` | 4B NetBIOS + 64B `\xfeSMB` SMB2/3 header + UTF-16LE paths: `COMMAND "<NEGOTIATE\|SESSION_SETUP\|TREE_CONNECT\|CREATE\|READ\|WRITE\|CLOSE\|TREE_DISCONNECT\|LOGOFF>"`, `STATUS <u32>` (`0`=SUCCESS, `0xC0000022`=ACCESS_DENIED), `SESSION_ID <u64>`, `TREE_ID <u32>`, `MSGID <u64>`, `SHARE "<\\\\srv\\share>"`, `FILENAME "<file>"` |
| **`NFS`** | TCP / UDP `2049` | ONC-RPC v2 + 4B XDR padding: `VERS <3\|4>` (`4` default), `PROC "<NULL\|COMPOUND\|LOOKUP\|READ\|WRITE>"`, `TAG "<tag>"`, `PATH "</export/path>"` |

```frameassembly
host compute_node { ip 10.90.1.25 }
host nas_filer    { ip 10.90.1.10 }

flow nas_file_operations(node, filer) {
    node -> filer smb command "NEGOTIATE" msgid 0 wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "NEGOTIATE" status 0 msgid 0 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "SESSION_SETUP" session_id 0x100001 msgid 1 wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "SESSION_SETUP" status 0 session_id 0x100001 msgid 1 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "TREE_CONNECT" session_id 0x100001 msgid 2 share "\\\\nas01.corp\\vmstore" wait 1ms
    node <- filer smb command "TREE_CONNECT" status 0 session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 2 wait 1ms
    node -> filer smb command "CREATE" session_id 0x100001 tree_id 10 msgid 3 filename "disk0.vhdx" wait 2ms

    node -> filer nfs vers 4 proc "COMPOUND" tag "open_read" path "/exports/hpc/checkpoint.dat" wait 1ms
    node <- filer nfs vers 4 proc "COMPOUND" tag "open_read" path "/exports/hpc/checkpoint.dat" payload "NFS4_DATA_4096B"
}

compile {
    nas_file_operations(compute_node, nas_filer)
}
```

## 4. In-Memory Caches & SQL Databases (`REDIS`, `MEMCACHED`, `MYSQL`, `POSTGRES`)

| Protocol | Default Port | Modifiers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`REDIS`** | TCP `6379` | RESP2/3 arrays & replies: `CMD "<PING\|GET\|SET\|HSET\|EVAL>"`, `ARGS "<space_sep_args>"`, `REPLY_TYPE "<SIMPLE\|BULK\|INTEGER\|ARRAY\|ERROR>"`, `VALUE "<val>"` |
| **`MEMCACHED`**| TCP / UDP `11211`| Text (`set`/`get`/`STORED`) or Binary (`0x80` via `OPCODE`): `CMD "<cmd>"`, `KEY "<key>"`, `EXPTIME <u32>`, `OPCODE <u8>`, `OPAQUE <u32>`, `CAS <u64>`, `PAYLOAD "<val>"` |
| **`MYSQL`** | TCP `3306` | MySQL v10 3B-LE length framing: `GREETING`, `SERVER_VERSION "<ver>"`, `LOGIN`, `USER "<user>"`, `DB "<schema>"`, `SQL "<query>"`, `OK`, `ERR`, `ERRCODE <u16>`, `EOF` |
| **`POSTGRES`** | TCP `5432` | PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol: `STARTUP`, `USER "<role>"`, `DB "<dbname>"`, `AUTH_OK`, `SQL "<query>"`, `COMMAND_COMPLETE`, `READY_FOR_QUERY`, `ERROR_RESPONSE` |

```frameassembly
host app_worker   { ip 10.110.1.50 }
host data_cluster { ip 10.110.1.10 }

flow cache_and_database_tier(app, db) {
    app -> db redis cmd "SET" args "session:4201 active EX 300" wait 1ms
    app <- db redis reply_type "SIMPLE" payload "+OK\r\n" wait 1ms
    app -> db memcached cmd "set" key "ratelimit:198.51.100.9" exptime 60 opaque 701 cas 1001 payload "14" wait 1ms
    app <- db memcached cmd "STORED" key "ratelimit:198.51.100.9" opaque 701 cas 1002 wait 2ms

    app <- db mysql greeting server_version "8.4.2-Enterprise" wait 1ms
    app -> db mysql login user "orders_svc" db "commerce" wait 1ms
    app <- db mysql ok wait 1ms
    app -> db mysql sql "INSERT INTO orders (id, total_cents) VALUES (9001, 14999);" wait 1ms
    app <- db mysql err errcode 1062 payload "Duplicate entry '9001' for key 'PRIMARY'" wait 2ms

    app -> db postgres startup user "ledger_svc" db "ledger" wait 1ms
    app <- db postgres auth_ok ready_for_query wait 1ms
    app -> db postgres sql "BEGIN; UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 14999 WHERE id = 42; COMMIT;" wait 1ms
    app <- db postgres command_complete ready_for_query payload "COMMIT"
}

compile {
    cache_and_database_tier(app_worker, data_cluster)
}
```
