# Documentation Bundle: `docs/l7_industrial_ot.md`

# Layer 7 Industrial Control Systems (ICS), SCADA & OT Reference

FrameAssembly implements native wire builders for **6 industrial, building-automation, electrical substation, and factory PLC protocols**, enabling IEC 62443 firewall testing, Purdue Level 1–3.5 zone verification, and OT IDS rule validation without physical controllers.

| Protocol | Keyword | Default Port | Standard | Supported Operations & Modifiers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Modbus TCP** | `MODBUS` | TCP `502` | Modbus v1.1b3 | `FUNC "<name>"`, `TXID <u16>`, `PROTO_ID <u16>`, `UNITID <u8>`, `ADDR <u16>`, `COUNT <u16>`, `VALUE <u16>`, `IS_RESPONSE` |
| **BACnet/IP** | `BACNET` | UDP `47808` | ANSI/ASHRAE 135 | `WHO_IS`, `I_AM`, `READ_PROPERTY`, `WRITE_PROPERTY`, `INVOKE_ID <u8>`, `OBJECT_TYPE <u16>`, `OBJECT_INSTANCE <u32>`, `PROPERTY_ID <u32>`, `VALUE <u32>` |
| **DNP3** | `DNP3` | TCP `20000` | IEEE 1815-2012 | `FUNC "<name>"`, `SRC <u16>`, `DST <u16>`, `SEQ <u8>`, `GROUP <u8>`, `VARIATION <u8>`, `CRC <u16>` |
| **Siemens S7comm**| `S7COMM` | TCP `102` | RFC 1006 / ISO 8073| `ROSCTR "<JOB\|ACK\|ACK_DATA\|USERDATA>"`, `FUNC "<SETUP_COMM\|READ_VAR\|WRITE_VAR\|PLC_CONTROL>"`, `PDU_REF <u16>`, `AREA <u8>`, `DB_NUM <u16>`, `OFFSET <u32>`, `COUNT <u16>` |
| **EtherNet/IP** | `ETHERNETIP`| TCP `44818` | ODVA CIP | `CMD "<name>"`, `SESSION_HANDLE <u32>`, `STATUS <u32>`, `CONTEXT <u64>`, `CIP_SERVICE <u8>`, `CIP_CLASS <u16>`, `CIP_INSTANCE <u16>`, `CIP_ATTR <u16>` |
| **OPC UA Binary**| `OPCUA` | TCP `4840` | IEC 62541 | `MSG_TYPE "<HEL\|ACK\|ERR\|OPN\|CLO\|MSG>"`, `CHUNK_TYPE "<F\|C\|A>"`, `SECURE_CHANNEL_ID <u32>`, `TOKEN_ID <u32>`, `SEQ_NUM <u32>`, `REQID <u32>`, `ENDPOINT_URL "<url>"`, `NODE_ID "<str>"` |

---

## 1. Modbus TCP (`MODBUS` — TCP Port 502)

Encapsulates Modbus function codes inside a 7-byte MBAP header (`TXID`, `PROTO_ID 0x0000`, computed `Length`, and `UNITID`).
* **`FUNC` values:** `"READ_COILS"` (`0x01`), `"READ_DISCRETE_INPUTS"` (`0x02`), `"READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS"` (`0x03` default), `"READ_INPUT_REGISTERS"` (`0x04`), `"WRITE_SINGLE_COIL"` (`0x05`), `"WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER"` (`0x06`), `"WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS"` (`0x10`).
* **Directionality:** Omit `IS_RESPONSE` for HMI Master requests; add `IS_RESPONSE` for PLC Slave replies.

```frameassembly
host scada_hmi   { ip 192.168.100.10 }
host turbine_plc { ip 192.168.100.50 }

flow modbus_polling_cycle(hmi, plc) {
    hmi -> plc modbus func "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS" txid 101 unitid 1 addr 40001 count 4 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc modbus func "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS" txid 101 unitid 1 count 4 is_response wait 5ms
    hmi -> plc modbus func "WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER" txid 102 unitid 1 addr 40010 value 1500 wait 2ms
    hmi <- plc modbus func "WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER" txid 102 unitid 1 addr 40010 value 1500 is_response
}

compile {
    modbus_polling_cycle(scada_hmi, turbine_plc)
}
```

---

## 2. BACnet/IP (`BACNET` — UDP Port 47808)

Encodes BVLC (`0x81`), NPDU (`0x01`), and APDU layers for building management and HVAC controllers:
* **Services:** `WHO_IS` (broadcast BVLC `0x0B`), `I_AM`, `READ_PROPERTY` (default), `WRITE_PROPERTY`.
* **Object & Property IDs:** `OBJECT_TYPE <u16>` (`0`=Analog Input, `1`=Analog Output, `2`=Analog Value, `3`=Binary Input, `4`=Binary Output, `8`=Device), `OBJECT_INSTANCE <u32>`, `PROPERTY_ID <u32>` (`85`=Present Value, `77`=Object Name, `111`=Status Flags), `VALUE <u32>`, `INVOKE_ID <u8>`.

```frameassembly
host bms_server  { ip 10.120.1.10 }
host chiller_ahu { ip 10.120.1.50 }

flow bacnet_hvac_control(bms, ahu) {
    bms -> ahu bacnet who_is wait 2ms
    bms <- ahu bacnet i_am object_type 8 object_instance 1010 wait 5ms
    bms -> ahu bacnet read_property invoke_id 10 object_type 0 object_instance 1 property_id 85 wait 2ms
    bms <- ahu bacnet read_property invoke_id 10 object_type 0 object_instance 1 property_id 85 value 68 wait 5ms
    bms -> ahu bacnet write_property invoke_id 11 object_type 2 object_instance 2 property_id 85 value 72
}

compile {
    bacnet_hvac_control(bms_server, chiller_ahu)
}
```

---

## 3. Distributed Network Protocol v3 (`DNP3` — TCP Port 20000)

Serializes IEEE 1815 `0x0564` Data Link headers, Transport headers, Application Object headers (`GROUP`, `VARIATION`), and automatic little-endian IEEE 1815 CRC-16 checksums across both the 8-byte header and every 16-byte data block (with optional `CRC <u16>` override for dissector fuzz/negative testing).
* **`FUNC` values:** `"CONFIRM"`, `"READ"`, `"WRITE"`, `"SELECT"`, `"OPERATE"`, `"DIRECT_OPERATE"`, `"RESPONSE"`, `"UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE"`.

```frameassembly
host dms_master     { ip 10.200.1.1 }
host substation_rtu { ip 10.200.1.50 }

flow dnp3_breaker_control(master, rtu) {
    // Class 0 integrity poll (Group 60 Variation 1)
    master -> rtu dnp3 func "READ" src 1 dst 50 seq 1 group 60 variation 1 wait 3ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 50 dst 1 seq 1 group 30 variation 1 wait 5ms

    // CROB Relay Select-Before-Operate sequence (Group 12 Variation 1)
    master -> rtu dnp3 func "SELECT" src 1 dst 50 seq 2 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 50 dst 1 seq 2 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master -> rtu dnp3 func "OPERATE" src 1 dst 50 seq 3 group 12 variation 1 wait 2ms
    master <- rtu dnp3 func "RESPONSE" src 50 dst 1 seq 3 group 12 variation 1
}

compile {
    dnp3_breaker_control(dms_master, substation_rtu)
}
```

---

## 4. Factory PLCs: Siemens S7 (`S7COMM`), EtherNet/IP (`ETHERNETIP`) & OPC UA (`OPCUA`)

* **`S7COMM` (TCP 102):** TPKT + ISO COTP + `0x32` S7 PDU (10-byte header on `"JOB"`/`"USERDATA"`, 12-byte header with 2-byte error status on `"ACK"`/`"ACK_DATA"`). Modifiers: `ROSCTR "<JOB|ACK|ACK_DATA|USERDATA>"`, `FUNC "<SETUP_COMM|READ_VAR|WRITE_VAR|PLC_CONTROL>"`, `PDU_REF <u16>`, `AREA <u8>` (`0x84`=DB, `0x83`=Merker, `0x81`=Inputs, `0x82`=Outputs), `DB_NUM <u16>`, `OFFSET <u32>`, `COUNT <u16>`.
* **`ETHERNETIP` (TCP 44818):** 24-byte little-endian encapsulation header + Common Packet Format (CPF) + logical EPATH (`Class`/`Instance`/`Attribute`). Modifiers: `CMD "<NOP|LIST_SERVICES|LIST_IDENTITY|LIST_INTERFACES|REGISTER_SESSION|UNREGISTER_SESSION|SEND_RR_DATA|SEND_UNIT_DATA>"`, `SESSION_HANDLE <u32>`, `STATUS <u32>`, `CONTEXT <u64>`, `CIP_SERVICE <u8>` (`0x0e`=Get_Attribute_Single, `0x10`=Set_Attribute_Single), `CIP_CLASS <u16>`, `CIP_INSTANCE <u16>`, `CIP_ATTR <u16>`.
* **`OPCUA` (TCP 4840):** IEC 62541 binary chunks: `MSG_TYPE "<HEL|ACK|ERR|OPN|CLO|MSG>"`, `CHUNK_TYPE "<F|C|A>"`, `SECURE_CHANNEL_ID <u32>`, `TOKEN_ID <u32>`, `SEQ_NUM <u32>`, `REQID <u32>`, `ENDPOINT_URL "<url>"`, `NODE_ID "<str>"`.

```frameassembly
host eng_station { ip 10.80.10.5 }
host cell_plc    { ip 10.80.10.20 }

flow multi_vendor_factory_cell(eng, plc) {
    // 1. Siemens S7comm Setup & DB1 Read/Write
    eng -> plc s7comm rosctr "JOB" func "SETUP_COMM" pdu_ref 100 wait 2ms
    eng <- plc s7comm rosctr "ACK_DATA" func "SETUP_COMM" pdu_ref 100 wait 2ms
    eng -> plc s7comm rosctr "JOB" func "READ_VAR" pdu_ref 101 area 0x84 db_num 1 offset 0 count 8 wait 2ms
    eng <- plc s7comm rosctr "ACK_DATA" func "READ_VAR" pdu_ref 101 count 8 wait 5ms

    // 2. ODVA EtherNet/IP Session Registration & CIP Assembly Read
    eng -> plc ethernetip cmd "REGISTER_SESSION" session_handle 1001 wait 2ms
    eng <- plc ethernetip cmd "REGISTER_SESSION" session_handle 1001 status 0 wait 2ms
    eng -> plc ethernetip cmd "SEND_RR_DATA" session_handle 1001 cip_service 0x0e cip_class 0x04 cip_instance 100 cip_attr 3 wait 5ms

    // 3. OPC UA Binary Hello, OpenSecureChannel, Read Node, and Close
    eng -> plc opcua msg_type "HEL" chunk_type "F" endpoint_url "opc.tcp://10.80.10.20:4840/plc" wait 2ms
    eng <- plc opcua msg_type "ACK" chunk_type "F" wait 2ms
    eng -> plc opcua msg_type "OPN" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 seq_num 1 reqid 1 wait 2ms
    eng -> plc opcua msg_type "MSG" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 2 reqid 2 node_id "ns=2;s=Cell01.SpindleRPM" wait 2ms
    eng -> plc opcua msg_type "CLO" chunk_type "F" secure_channel_id 10 token_id 1 seq_num 3 reqid 3
}

compile {
    multi_vendor_factory_cell(eng_station, cell_plc)
}
```

---

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/topologies_and_dual_stack.md`

# Multi-Protocol Network Topologies & Dual-Stack Scenarios

FrameAssembly can model complete multi-tier network architectures in a single `.fasm` file by combining three features:
1. **Multi-host `flow` signatures:** Pass 3 to 8+ hosts into a single flow (`flow onboarding(laptop, sw, radius, nms)`) to capture client-to-server, east-west, and out-of-band management traffic in chronological order.
2. **Dual-stack IPv4 / IPv6 flow reuse:** Run the same `flow` inside `compile` first with IPv4 `host` definitions and then with IPv6 `host` definitions—automatically switching between IPv4 (`0x0800`) and IPv6 (`0x86DD`) framing and checksums.
3. **Microsecond-to-second `wait` steps & `loop` bursts:** Synthesize realistic protocol timers, RTP media bursts, and telemetry exports.

*(Browse **104 additional full-stack `.fasm` topologies** in [`examples/topologies/`](../examples/topologies/).)*

---

## 1. EVPN-VXLAN Leaf-Spine Data Center Fabric (`LLDP` + `BFD` + `BGP` + `VXLAN` + `IPFIX`)

Brings up a Spine-Leaf underlay via LLDP neighbor discovery, 50ms BFD liveness, and eBGP peering, transmits a 4-packet VXLAN East-West burst, and exports an IPFIX flow record to a fabric collector:

```frameassembly
host spine_01  { ip 10.255.0.1    mac 00:1c:73:00:00:01 }
host leaf_01   { ip 10.255.0.11   mac 00:1c:73:00:01:01 }
host leaf_02   { ip 10.255.0.12   mac 00:1c:73:00:01:02 }
host collector { ip 10.255.100.50 mac 00:1c:73:00:99:50 }

flow underlay_bringup(spine, leaf) {
    spine -> leaf lldp chassis_id "spine-01.dc1" port_id "Ethernet1/1" ttl 120 sysname "spine-01" wait 1ms
    spine <- leaf lldp chassis_id "leaf-01.dc1" port_id "Ethernet49/1" ttl 120 sysname "leaf-01" wait 2ms

    spine <- leaf bfd state 3 my_disc 101 your_disc 1 min_tx 50000 min_rx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine -> leaf bfd state 3 my_disc 1 your_disc 101 min_tx 50000 min_rx 50000 mult 3 ttl 255 wait 2ms

    spine <- leaf bgp open asn 65101 holdtime 90 bgpid 10.255.0.11 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine -> leaf bgp open asn 65000 holdtime 90 bgpid 10.255.0.1 ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine <- leaf bgp keepalive ttl 255 wait 2ms
    spine <- leaf bgp update asn 65101 prefix "10.254.1.1/32" nexthop 10.255.0.11 ttl 255 wait 5ms
}

flow vxlan_east_west(vtep1, vtep2) {
    vtep1 -> vtep2 vxlan vni 10100 dscp 26 df payload "EAST_WEST_TENANT_RPC" wait 2ms
}

flow export_telemetry(leaf, col) {
    leaf -> col ipfix seq 1 domain_id 100 srcip 10.255.0.11 dstip 10.255.0.12 proto 17 packets 4 octets 512
}

compile {
    underlay_bringup(spine_01, leaf_01)
    loop 4 {
        vxlan_east_west(leaf_01, leaf_02)
    }
    export_telemetry(leaf_01, collector)
}
```

---

## 2. Campus Zero-Trust 802.1X NAC Onboarding (`EAPOL` + `RADIUS` + `DHCP` + `ARP` + `SNMP3`)

Models a corporate laptop authenticating on an access switch port, receiving a DHCPv4 lease, broadcasting a Gratuitous ARP check, and triggering an encrypted SNMPv3 compliance notification:

```frameassembly
host workstation { ip 10.10.50.100 mac 00:22:44:66:88:aa }
host access_sw   { ip 10.10.50.1   mac 00:11:22:33:44:01 }
host radius_srv  { ip 10.10.1.10   mac 00:11:22:33:44:10 }
host nms_srv     { ip 10.10.1.20   mac 00:11:22:33:44:20 }

flow campus_dot1x_onboarding(ws, sw, aaa, nms) {
    ws -> sw eapol version 2 type start wait 2ms
    ws <- sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 1 eap_id 1 eap_method 1 wait 2ms
    ws -> sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 2 eap_id 1 eap_method 1 identity "eng-laptop-42" wait 2ms

    sw -> aaa radius access_request id 42 user "eng-laptop-42" nas_ip 10.10.50.1 wait 5ms
    sw <- aaa radius access_accept id 42 framed_ip 10.10.50.100 wait 2ms
    ws <- sw eapol version 2 type eap_packet eap_code 3 eap_id 1 wait 5ms

    ws -> sw dhcp discover txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa wait 5ms
    ws <- sw dhcp offer txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 router 10.10.50.1 dns_server 10.10.1.53 subnet_mask 255.255.255.0 lease_time 43200 wait 5ms
    ws -> sw dhcp request txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 wait 5ms
    ws <- sw dhcp ack txid 0xabcdef01 chaddr 00:22:44:66:88:aa yiaddr 10.10.50.100 router 10.10.50.1 dns_server 10.10.1.53 subnet_mask 255.255.255.0 lease_time 43200 wait 5ms

    ws -> sw arp gratuitous sha 00:22:44:66:88:aa spa 10.10.50.100 tpa 10.10.50.100 wait 2ms
    sw -> nms snmp3 inform user "nac_auditor" engineid "80001f88801122334455" engineboots 5 enginetime 3600 auth sha256 "AuditAuthKey2026!" priv aes "AuditPrivKey2026!" reqid 500 varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 string "access-sw-floor2" varbind 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8.12 int 1
}

compile {
    campus_dot1x_onboarding(workstation, access_sw, radius_srv, nms_srv)
}
```

---

## 3. Dual-Stack Cloud Microservice Mesh (`DNS` + `TCP` + `TLS` + `GRPC` + `REDIS` + `POSTGRES`)

Runs a single 4-tier service mesh transaction across **both IPv4 and IPv6** cluster networks without duplicating flow logic:

```frameassembly
host ingress_v4 { ip 10.244.1.10 }
host coredns_v4 { ip 10.96.0.10 }
host orders_v4  { ip 10.244.2.20 }
host storage_v4 { ip 10.244.3.30 }

host ingress_v6 { ip fd00:10:244:1::10 }
host coredns_v6 { ip fd00:10:96::10 }
host orders_v6  { ip fd00:10:244:2::20 }
host storage_v6 { ip fd00:10:244:3::30 }

flow service_mesh_checkout(gw, dns, svc, db) {
    gw -> dns dns query txid 901 qname "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" qtype "A" wait 1ms
    gw <- dns dns response txid 901 qname "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" qtype "A" rdata "10.244.2.20" wait 1ms

    gw -> svc tcp syn srcport 51051 dstport 50051 wait 1ms
    gw <- svc tcp syn ack wait 1ms
    gw -> svc tcp ack wait 1ms
    gw -> svc tls client_hello sni "orders.prod.svc.cluster.local" ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    gw <- svc tls server_hello ciphersuite 4865 alpn "h2" wait 2ms
    gw -> svc grpc service "commerce.OrderService" method "CreateOrder" payload "sku=NVME-4TB&qty=2" wait 2ms

    svc -> db redis cmd "GET" args "inventory:NVME-4TB" wait 1ms
    svc <- db redis reply_type "BULK" value "42" wait 1ms
    svc -> db postgres sql "INSERT INTO orders (sku, qty) VALUES ('NVME-4TB', 2);" wait 2ms
    svc <- db postgres command_complete ready_for_query payload "INSERT 0 1" wait 2ms

    gw <- svc grpc service "commerce.OrderService" method "CreateOrder" grpc_status 0 payload "order_id=90042"
}

compile {
    service_mesh_checkout(ingress_v4, coredns_v4, orders_v4, storage_v4)
    service_mesh_checkout(ingress_v6, coredns_v6, orders_v6, storage_v6)
}
```

---

## 4. IEC 62443 Substation & Industrial DMZ Conduit (`MODBUS` + `DNP3` + `S7COMM` + `OPCUA` + `SYSLOG`)

Combines priority-tagged Level 1–2 PLC/RTU polling (`VLAN 110 PCP 6`) with OPC UA historian push and Syslog SIEM auditing across the Level 3.5 Industrial DMZ (`VLAN 120`):

```frameassembly
host substation_hmi { ip 172.22.10.5   mac 00:1b:21:22:0a:05 }
host bay_rtu        { ip 172.22.10.50  mac 00:a0:c9:22:0a:32 }
host s7_plc         { ip 172.22.10.60  mac 00:0e:8c:22:0a:3c }
host idmz_historian { ip 172.22.20.100 mac 00:50:56:22:14:64 }

flow substation_conduit_telemetry(hmi, rtu, plc, idmz) {
    hmi -> rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus unitid 1 func "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS" addr 40001 count 8 wait 1ms
    hmi <- rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 modbus unitid 1 func "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS" count 8 is_response wait 2ms
    hmi -> rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 dnp3 src 1 dst 10 func "READ" group 60 variation 1 wait 2ms
    hmi <- rtu vlan 110 pcp 6 dnp3 src 10 dst 1 func "RESPONSE" group 30 variation 1 wait 2ms
    hmi -> plc vlan 110 pcp 6 s7comm rosctr "JOB" func "READ_VAR" pdu_ref 10 area 0x84 db_num 1 offset 0 count 4 wait 2ms

    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 opcua msg_type "MSG" chunk_type "F" endpoint_url "opc.tcp://idmz:4840" node_id "ns=3;s=Feeder01.kV" wait 2ms
    hmi -> idmz vlan 120 pcp 4 syslog facility 4 severity 5 hostname "sub-hmi-01" app "scada-poller" msg "IEC62443-Conduit: Authorized poll completed"
}

compile {
    substation_conduit_telemetry(substation_hmi, bay_rtu, s7_plc, idmz_historian)
}
```

# Documentation Bundle: `docs/for_nerds.md`

# For Nerds: Compiler Pipeline, Rust Library API & Formal Grammars

This reference covers FrameAssembly's internal Rust compiler architecture, how to embed `frameassembly` inside Rust unit/integration test suites, and how to use the repository's formal context-free grammars for zero-hallucination LLM constrained decoding.

---

## 1. Six-Stage Zero-Copy Compiler Architecture

FrameAssembly (`frameassembly` v1.2.2, Rust Edition 2024) compiles `.fasm` source buffers into `.pcap` / `.pcapng` captures through a deterministic six-stage pipeline in pure userspace—requiring zero root privileges (`CAP_NET_RAW`), kernel sockets, or external C libraries (`libpcap` is not required at build or runtime):

```text
 ┌────────────────┐     ┌────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────┐
 │  .fasm Source  │ ──> │  Logos Lexer   │ ──> │  Winnow TokenSlice  │
 │  Text Buffer   │     │  (Zero-Copy)   │     │  Parser Combinators │
 └────────────────┘     └────────────────┘     └─────────────────────┘
                                                          │
                                                          ▼
 ┌────────────────┐     ┌────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────┐
 │ .pcap / PCAPNG │ <── │  4-Tuple State │ <── │  Semantic Validator │
 │ Serialization  │ <── │ & Wire Builders│ <── │ & AST Representation│
 └────────────────┘     └────────────────┘     └─────────────────────┘
```

### Stage 1: Zero-Copy Lexical Analysis (`src/lexer/mod.rs`)
* Powered by `logos 0.14`, scanning UTF-8 input buffers without allocating heap strings.
* Emits `SpannedToken<'a>` items borrowing `&'a str` slices directly from the source buffer alongside byte-offset spans (`Range<usize>`) across all 81 protocol keywords, 640+ lexer tokens, integer literals, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, IEEE 802 MACs, ASN.1 OIDs, and duration suffixes (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`).

### Stage 2: Two-Phase Token-Slice Parsing (`src/parser/`)
* Implemented with `winnow 1.0` operating over a custom `TokenSlice<'i, 'a>` stream (`Stream<'i, 'a>`).
* Decoupling lexical tokenization from syntactic combinators eliminates character-level backtracking, strips comments in $O(N)$ time, and dispatches protocol-scoped modifiers cleanly across `src/parser/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/`.

### Stage 3: Semantic Validation (`src/parser/validation.rs`)
Enforces structural invariants across `Program<'a>` before wire serialization, rendering graphical source-mapped diagnostics via `miette 7.6` on errors:
1. **Host uniqueness & scope:** Every `HOST` identifier must be unique, define a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address, and exist when referenced in `COMPILE`.
2. **Flow signature arity:** Every `FLOW` call in `COMPILE` or `LOOP` must pass the exact number of endpoint arguments declared in its parameter list.
3. **Dual-stack endpoint homogeneity:** Concrete hosts bound to `lhs -> rhs` or `lhs <- rhs` must share the same IP family (both IPv4 or both IPv6).
4. **Modifier exclusivity & positive loops:** Rejects duplicate modifiers or multiple protocols on a single frame statement and enforces `LOOP <count>` with `count >= 1`.

### Stage 4: Zero-Heap Protocol Wire Builders (`src/builders/`)
* Dedicated wire builders under `src/builders/{l2,l3,l4,l7}/` serialize RFC-compliant headers directly into pre-allocated frame buffers and populate RFC defaults for omitted optional fields.
* **Built-in Checksum & Crypto Engines:**
  * RFC 1071 16-bit one's complement checksums (IPv4, ICMPv4, TCP/UDP with IPv4/IPv6 pseudo-headers, GRE RFC 2784, IGMP, VRRPv2 RFC 3768).
  * RFC 4443 & RFC 5798 IPv6 pseudo-header checksums (ICMPv6, NDP, MLD, VRRPv3).
  * RFC 9260 32-bit Castagnoli CRC32c (`SCTP`) and IEEE 1815 reflected 16-bit CRC-16 (`DNP3`).
  * ASN.1 BER/DER (`rasn`) & SNMPv3 USM (`src/builders/l7/snmp/`): RFC 3414 1-MB password-to-key (`Ku`) expansion, `ENGINEID` key localization (`Kul`), `DES-CBC` / `AES-128-CFB` encryption, and truncated `HMAC-MD5-96`, `HMAC-SHA-96`, `HMAC-SHA-256-192`, `HMAC-SHA-384-256`, and `HMAC-SHA-512-384` authentication.

### Stage 5: Stateful 4-Tuple Engine (`src/backend/`)
* Tracks bidirectional connection state keyed by canonical 4-tuple (`Endpoint A`, `Endpoint B`, `Port A`, `Port B`, `Protocol`), reversing ports on `<-`, advancing TCP `SEQ`/`ACK` across `SYN`/`FIN` ghost bytes and L4/L7 payloads, and deriving RFC 1112 (`01:00:5e:xx:xx:xx`) and RFC 2464 (`33:33:xx:xx:xx:xx`) multicast MAC addresses.

### Stage 6: Nanosecond PCAPNG Writer (`src/pcap.rs`)
* Serializes finalized Ethernet frames with `IfTsResol(9)` nanosecond timestamps via `pcap-file 2.0`.

---

## 2. Repository `<layer>/<protocol>` Symmetry

```text
frameassembly/
├── src/
│   ├── lexer/          # Zero-copy Logos tokenizer
│   ├── ast/            # Strongly-typed AST & *Spec structs (l2/, l3/, l4/, l7/)
│   ├── parser/         # Winnow token-slice combinators & semantic validator
│   ├── builders/       # RFC wire encoders & SNMPv3 USM crypto (l2/, l3/, l4/, l7/)
│   ├── backend/        # 4-tuple state engine, loop unrolling, L7 dispatch
│   ├── packet.rs       # Ethernet/VLAN/QinQ/MPLS/IPv4/IPv6/L4 framing & checksums
│   ├── pcap.rs         # Nanosecond-precision PCAPNG serializer
│   ├── error.rs        # Miette diagnostic error types (CompilerError)
│   └── main.rs         # Clap CLI binary interface
├── docs/               # User guides, layer protocol references & internals
└── examples/           # 2,611 verified .fasm scenarios (l2/, l3/, l4/, l7/, topologies/)
```

---

## 3. Public Rust Library API

Embed `frameassembly` directly inside Rust test suites to synthesize Ethernet frames (`Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>`) in memory or write `.pcap` fixtures to disk:

```rust
use frameassembly::parser::parse_program;
use frameassembly::backend::{compile_program, generate_pcap};

let fasm = r#"
    HOST sensor { IP 192.168.10.5 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e }
    HOST plc    { IP 192.168.10.20 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5f }

    FLOW modbus_poll(c, s) {
        c -> s MODBUS TXID 1 UNITID 1 READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS ADDR 100 COUNT 4 WAIT 5ms
        c <- s MODBUS TXID 1 UNITID 1 READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS IS_RESPONSE VALUE 42 WAIT 5ms
    }

    COMPILE { modbus_poll(sensor, plc) }
"#;

let program = parse_program(fasm).expect("valid .fasm specification");
let frames = compile_program(&program).expect("wire synthesis succeeds");
assert_eq!(frames.len(), 2);
assert_eq!(frames[1].1, 5_000_000); // 5ms in nanoseconds

generate_pcap(&program, "modbus_fixture.pcap").expect("pcap written");
```

### Entry Signatures & Error Variants
* `frameassembly::lexer::lex(source: &str) -> Result<Vec<SpannedToken<'_>>, CompilerError>`
* `frameassembly::parser::parse_program(source: &str) -> Result<Program<'_>, CompilerError>` (runs `validate_semantics` automatically)
* `frameassembly::parser::validate_semantics<'a>(program: &Program<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Result<(), CompilerError>`
* `frameassembly::backend::compile_program(program: &Program<'_>) -> Result<Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)>, String>`
* `frameassembly::backend::generate_pcap(program: &Program<'_>, output_path: &str) -> Result<(), String>`
* `frameassembly::error::CompilerError::{LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, BackendError}`

---

## 4. Formal Grammars, Constrained Decoding & SFT Corpus

FrameAssembly ships synchronized formal grammars in the repository root so structured LLM inference engines can generate syntactically valid `.fasm` specifications with **0% syntax hallucination**:

| Artifact | Format | Target Frameworks & Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`grammar.ebnf`](../grammar.ebnf) | ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF | Canonical context-free grammar reference across all 81 protocols |
| [`frameassembly.gbnf`](../frameassembly.gbnf) | GGML BNF (`GBNF`) | `llama.cpp` (`--grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf`), `KoboldCpp`, `TabbyAPI` |
| [`frameassembly.lark`](../frameassembly.lark) | Lark Earley / LALR | `vLLM`, `Outlines`, `Guidance`, `XGrammar`, `SGLang`, `llguidance` |
| [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt) / [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) | Markdown Context | Concise LLM index and single-fetch RAG context bundle |

### `llama.cpp` Constrained Decoding Example
```bash
llama-cli \
  -m qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct-q8_0.gguf \
  --grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf \
  -p "Write a FrameAssembly (.fasm) program that performs a TCP 3-way handshake between 10.0.0.1 and 10.0.0.2 on port 443 and sends a TLS ClientHello with SNI 'secure.example.com'." \
  > generated.fasm && frameassembly generated.fasm -o synthesized.pcap
```

### Training Corpus Conventions (`examples/`)
Every `.fasm` file across the `2,611` scenarios in [`examples/`](../examples/) is verified by `cargo test --test corpus_verification_tests` and includes structured header comments for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and compiler-verified RLVR evaluation:
* **Line 1 (`// PROMPT:`)**: Natural-language description of the network scenario.
* **Line 2 (`// TOKENS:`)**: Exact uppercase lexer tokens exercised in the file.
* **Block Headers (`// INSTRUCTION:`)**: Precedes each `HOST`, `FLOW`, and `COMPILE` declaration.

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Polymorphic dual-stack ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 Echo Request and Echo Reply using a single reusable FLOW.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, ICMP, ECHO_REQUEST, ECHO_REPLY, ID, SEQ, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Declare IPv4 endpoints and IPv6 endpoints.
HOST client_v4 { IP 10.0.0.10 }
HOST dns_v4    { IP 8.8.8.8 }
HOST client_v6 { IP 2001:db8::10 }
HOST dns_v6    { IP 2001:4860:4860::8888 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a polymorphic ping flow that works over both IPv4 and IPv6.
FLOW dual_stack_ping(src, dst) {
    src -> dst ICMP ECHO_REQUEST ID 100 SEQ 1 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "polymorphic-ping"
    src <- dst ICMP ECHO_REPLY ID 100 SEQ 1 TTL 57 PAYLOAD "polymorphic-ping" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the flow for IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint pairs.
COMPILE {
    dual_stack_ping(client_v4, dns_v4)
    dual_stack_ping(client_v6, dns_v6)
}
```

---

# Formal ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF Grammar (`grammar.ebnf`)

```ebnf
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* FrameAssembly Formal Grammar Specification (ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF)           *)
(* Covers all 81 native protocols, L2-L7 sub-keywords, modifiers & literals. *)
(* Synchronized with src/lexer/mod.rs and src/parser/                        *)
(* Note: All keyword, protocol, modifier, and duration terminals are matched *)
(* ASCII case-insensitively by the lexer (e.g., "HOST", "host", "Host").     *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

program                 = { top_level_decl } , compile_block , { top_level_decl } ;

top_level_decl          = host_declaration | flow_declaration ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 1. Host Declarations                                                      *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
host_declaration        = "HOST" , identifier , "{" , { host_property } , "}" ;
host_property           = ( "IP" , ip_address )
                        | ( "MAC" , mac_address ) ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 2. Flow Declarations & Frame Statements                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
flow_declaration        = "FLOW" , identifier , "(" , [ param_list ] , ")" ,
                          "{" , { frame_statement } , "}" ;
param_list              = identifier , { "," , identifier } ;

frame_statement         = endpoint , direction , endpoint , { frame_field } ;
endpoint                = identifier ;
direction               = "->" | "<-" ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 3. Compilation Block & Execution Loops                                    *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
compile_block           = "COMPILE" , "{" , { run_statement } , "}" ;
run_statement           = flow_invocation | loop_block ;
loop_block              = "LOOP" , unsigned_int , "{" , { flow_invocation } , "}" ;
flow_invocation         = identifier , "(" , [ arg_list ] , ")" ;
arg_list                = identifier , { "," , identifier } ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 4. Frame Fields (Protocols, Modifiers & Protocol-Specific Attributes)     *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
frame_field             = protocol_keyword
                        | universal_modifier
                        | l2_modifier
                        | l3_modifier
                        | l4_modifier
                        | l2_protocol_field
                        | l3_protocol_field
                        | l4_protocol_field
                        | snmp_protocol_field
                        | l7_protocol_field ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 5. All 81 Native Protocol Keywords                                        *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
protocol_keyword        = l2_protocol
                        | l3_protocol
                        | l4_protocol
                        | snmp_protocol
                        | l7_infra_protocol
                        | l7_app_protocol
                        | l7_ot_protocol ;

(* Layer 2 Data-Link Protocols (8) *)
l2_protocol             = "ARP" | "VLAN" | "QINQ" | "LLDP"
                        | "STP" | "LACP" | "EAPOL" | "MPLS" ;

(* Layer 3 Network, Tunneling, Security & Routing Protocols (20) *)
l3_protocol             = "ICMP" | "NDP" | "IGMP" | "MLD"
                        | "GRE" | "VXLAN" | "GENEVE"
                        | "IPSEC" | "ESP" | "AH" | "IKEV2" | "WIREGUARD"
                        | "OSPF" | "BGP" | "RIP" | "VRRP" | "HSRP"
                        | "PIM" | "BFD" | "OPENFLOW" ;

(* Layer 4 Transport Protocols (3) *)
l4_protocol             = "TCP" | "UDP" | "SCTP" ;

(* Layer 7 SNMP Protocols (3) *)
snmp_protocol           = "SNMP1" | "SNMP2" | "SNMP3" ;

(* Layer 7 Infrastructure, Management & Telemetry Protocols (11) *)
l7_infra_protocol       = "DNS" | "MDNS" | "DHCP" | "NTP" | "PTP"
                        | "RADIUS" | "TACACS" | "SYSLOG"
                        | "NETFLOW" | "IPFIX" | "SFLOW" ;

(* Layer 7 Web, Application, Directory, Mail, Storage & Messaging Protocols (30) *)
l7_app_protocol         = "TFTP" | "FTP" | "SSH" | "TELNET"
                        | "HTTP" | "HTTP2" | "GRPC" | "WEBSOCKET"
                        | "TLS" | "QUIC" | "STUN" | "SIP" | "RTP" | "RTSP"
                        | "SMTP" | "IMAP" | "POP3"
                        | "KERBEROS" | "LDAP" | "SMB" | "NFS"
                        | "REDIS" | "MEMCACHED" | "MYSQL" | "POSTGRES"
                        | "MQTT" | "COAP" | "AMQP" | "SSDP" | "WHOIS" ;

(* Layer 7 Industrial / Operational Technology (SCADA/OT) Protocols (6) *)
l7_ot_protocol          = "MODBUS" | "BACNET" | "DNP3"
                        | "S7COMM" | "ETHERNETIP" | "OPCUA" ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6. Universal, Layer 2, Layer 3 & Layer 4 Frame Modifiers                  *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
universal_modifier      = ( "WAIT" , duration_literal )
                        | ( "PAYLOAD" , string_literal )
                        | ( "HEXPAYLOAD" , hex_string_literal ) ;

l2_modifier             = ( "SRCMAC" , mac_address )
                        | ( "DSTMAC" , mac_address )
                        | ( "ETHERTYPE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "VLAN" , [ unsigned_int ] )
                        | ( "PCP" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "DEI" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "QINQ" , [ unsigned_int ] )
                        | ( "INNER_VLAN" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MPLS" , [ unsigned_int ] )
                        | ( "LABEL" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( ( "EXP" | "TC" ) , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "BOS" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MPLS_TTL" , unsigned_int ) ;

l3_modifier             = ( "TTL" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "DSCP" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ECN" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "FLOWLABEL" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "IPID" , unsigned_int )
                        | "DF"
                        | "MF"
                        | ( "FRAGOFFSET" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "NEXT_HEADER" , unsigned_int ) ;

l4_modifier             = ( "SRCPORT" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "DSTPORT" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "TRANSPORT" , ( "TCP" | "UDP" ) )
                        | tcp_flag
                        | ( "SEQ" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ACKNUM" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( ( "WIN" | "WINDOW" ) , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "URGENT" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MSS" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "WSCALE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "SACK_PERM" | "SACKPERM" )
                        | ( "TSVAL" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "TSECR" , unsigned_int ) ;

tcp_flag                = "SYN" | "ACK" | "FIN" | "RST"
                        | "PSH" | "URG" | "ECE" | "CWR" ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 7. Layer 2 Protocol Sub-Keywords                                          *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
l2_protocol_field       = arp_field | lldp_field | stp_field
                        | lacp_field | eapol_field ;

arp_field               = "REQUEST"
                        | ( "REPLY" , [ string_literal ] )
                        | "GRATUITOUS" | "GARP"
                        | ( ( "SHA" | "SENDERMAC" ) , mac_address )
                        | ( ( "SPA" | "SENDERIP" ) , ip_address )
                        | ( ( "THA" | "TARGETMAC" ) , mac_address )
                        | ( ( "TPA" | "TARGETIP" ) , ip_address ) ;

lldp_field              = ( "CHASSIS_ID" , str_or_ident )
                        | ( "PORT_ID" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "SYSNAME" , str_or_ident )
                        | ( "SYSDESC" , str_or_ident ) ;

stp_field               = ( "ROOT_ID" , str_or_ident )
                        | ( "BRIDGE_ID" , str_or_ident )
                        | ( "COST" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MAX_AGE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "HELLO_TIME" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "FORWARD_DELAY" , unsigned_int )
                        | "RSTP"
                        | ( "FLAGS" , unsigned_int ) ;

lacp_field              = ( "ACTOR_SYS" , ( mac_address | string_literal ) )
                        | ( "ACTOR_KEY" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ACTOR_PORT" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "PARTNER_SYS" , ( mac_address | string_literal ) )
                        | ( "PARTNER_KEY" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "PARTNER_PORT" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ACTOR_STATE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "PARTNER_STATE" , unsigned_int ) ;

eapol_field             = ( "VERSION" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "TYPE" , ( unsigned_int | eapol_pkt_type | wireguard_pkt_type
                                     | openflow_pkt_type | tacacs_pkt_type | str_or_ident ) )
                        | eapol_pkt_type
                        | ( "EAP_CODE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "EAP_ID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "EAP_METHOD" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "IDENTITY" , str_or_ident ) ;

eapol_pkt_type          = "START" | "LOGOFF" | "KEY" | "EAP_PACKET" ;
wireguard_pkt_type      = "INITIATION" | "RESPONSE" | "COOKIE" | "DATA" ;
openflow_pkt_type       = "HELLO" | "FEATURES_REQ" | "FEATURES_REPLY"
                        | "PACKET_IN" | "PACKET_OUT" | "FLOW_MOD"
                        | "ECHO_REQ" | "ECHO_REQUEST" | "ECHO_REPLY" ;
tacacs_pkt_type         = "AUTHEN" | "AUTHOR" | "ACCT" ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 8. Layer 3 Protocol Sub-Keywords                                          *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
l3_protocol_field       = icmp_field | ndp_field | igmp_field | mld_field
                        | gre_field | vxlan_geneve_field | ipsec_esp_ah_field
                        | ikev2_field | wireguard_field | ospf_field
                        | bgp_field | rip_field | vrrp_field | hsrp_field
                        | pim_field | bfd_field | openflow_field ;

icmp_field              = "ECHO_REQUEST" | "ECHO_REPLY" | "DEST_UNREACH"
                        | "TIME_EXCEEDED" | "REDIRECT"
                        | ( "CODE" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "ID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "GATEWAY" , ip_address ) ;

ndp_field               = "ROUTER_SOLICIT" | "ROUTER_ADVERT"
                        | "NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT" | "NEIGHBOR_ADVERT"
                        | ( "TARGET" , ( ip_address | mac_address ) )
                        | ( "SLLA" , mac_address )
                        | ( "TLLA" , mac_address )
                        | ( "ROUTER_LIFETIME" , unsigned_int ) ;

igmp_field              = "QUERY" | "REPORT" | "LEAVE"
                        | "V1" | "V2" | "V3"
                        | ( "GROUP" , ( ip_address | unsigned_int ) )
                        | ( "MAX_RESP" , unsigned_int ) ;

mld_field               = "DONE"
                        | ( "MULTICAST_ADDR" , ip_address )
                        | ( "MAX_RESP_DELAY" , unsigned_int ) ;

gre_field               = "CHECKSUM"
                        | ( "GRE_KEY" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "GRE_SEQ" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "GRE_PROTO" , unsigned_int ) ;

vxlan_geneve_field      = ( ( "VNI" | "VNID" ) , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "OPT_CLASS" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "OPT_TYPE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "PROTOCOL_TYPE" , unsigned_int ) ;

ipsec_esp_ah_field      = ( "SPI" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "IV" , ( hex_string_literal | unsigned_int ) )
                        | ( "ICV" , ( hex_string_literal | unsigned_int ) ) ;

ikev2_field             = ( "INITIATOR_SPI" , ( unsigned_int | hex_string_literal ) )
                        | ( "RESPONDER_SPI" , ( unsigned_int | hex_string_literal ) )
                        | ( "EXCHANGE" , ( unsigned_int | ikev2_exchange_mode | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ikev2_exchange_mode
                        | ( "MSGID" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "NEXT_PAYLOAD" , unsigned_int ) ;

ikev2_exchange_mode     = "SA_INIT" | "CREATE_CHILD_SA" | "INFORMATIONAL" ;

wireguard_field         = "INITIATION"
                        | ( "COOKIE" , [ str_or_ident ] )
                        | ( "DATA" , [ str_or_ident ] )
                        | ( "SENDER" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "RECEIVER" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "COUNTER" , unsigned_int ) ;

ospf_field              = "HELLO" | "DBD" | "LSR" | "LSU" | "LSACK"
                        | ( "ROUTER_ID" , ip_address )
                        | ( "AREA_ID" , ( unsigned_int | ip_address ) )
                        | ( "HELLO_INTERVAL" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "DEAD_INTERVAL" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "PRIORITY" , unsigned_int ) ;

bgp_field               = "OPEN" | "UPDATE" | "NOTIFICATION"
                        | ( "KEEPALIVE" , [ unsigned_int ] )
                        | ( "ASN" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "HOLDTIME" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "BGPID" , ip_address )
                        | ( ( "PREFIX" | "NLRI" ) , ( ip_address | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "NEXTHOP" , ip_address ) ;

rip_field               = ( "COMMAND" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "METRIC" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "TAG" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) ) ;

vrrp_field              = ( "VRID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ADV_INT" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "VIP" , ip_address ) ;

hsrp_field              = ( "HELLOTIME" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "STATE" , unsigned_int ) ;

pim_field               = "JOIN_PRUNE" | "REGISTER"
                        | ( "SOURCE" , ip_address )
                        | ( "RP" , ip_address )
                        | ( "DR_PRIORITY" , unsigned_int ) ;

bfd_field               = ( "DIAG" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MY_DISC" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "YOUR_DISC" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MIN_TX" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MIN_RX" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "MULT" , unsigned_int ) ;

openflow_field          = "FEATURES_REQ" | "FEATURES_REPLY"
                        | "PACKET_IN" | "PACKET_OUT"
                        | "FLOW_MOD" | "ECHO_REQ"
                        | ( "XID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "DPID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "TABLE_ID" , unsigned_int ) ;

                        | "DIRECT_OPERATE" | "UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE"

                        | ( "CRC" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "SRC" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "DST" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ROSCTR" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "PDU_REF" , unsigned_int )
                        | "SETUP_COMM" | "READ_VAR" | "WRITE_VAR" | "PLC_CONTROL"
                        | ( "AREA" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "DB_NUM" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "OFFSET" , unsigned_int )
                        | "LIST_SERVICES" | "LIST_IDENTITY" | "LIST_INTERFACES"
                        | "REGISTER_SESSION" | "UNREGISTER_SESSION"
                        | "SEND_RR_DATA" | "SEND_UNIT_DATA"
                        | ( "SESSION_HANDLE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "CONTEXT" , ( unsigned_int | str_or_ident ) )
                        | ( "CIP_SERVICE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "CIP_CLASS" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "CIP_INSTANCE" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "CIP_ATTR" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "CHUNK_TYPE" , str_or_ident )
                        | ( "SECURE_CHANNEL_ID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "TOKEN_ID" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "SEQ_NUM" , unsigned_int )
                        | ( "ENDPOINT_URL" , str_or_ident )
                        | ( "NODE_ID" , str_or_ident ) ;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 12. Lexical Terminals                                                     *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
str_or_ident            = string_literal | identifier ;
identifier              = ( letter | "_" ) , { letter | digit | "_" } ;
unsigned_int            = decimal_int | hex_int ;
signed_int              = [ "-" ] , decimal_int | hex_int ;
decimal_int             = digit , { digit } ;
hex_int                 = ( "0x" | "0X" ) , hex_digit , { hex_digit } ;
duration_literal        = unsigned_int , time_unit ;
time_unit               = "ns" | "us" | "ms" | "s" | "m" ;
string_literal          = '"' , { string_char | escape_sequence } , '"' ;
string_char             = " ".."!" | "#".."[" | "]".."~" ;
hex_string_literal      = '"' , { hex_digit | ":" | " " } , '"' ;
escape_sequence         = "\" , ( "r" | "n" | "t" | "\" | '"' | "'"
                                | ( "x" , hex_digit , hex_digit )
                                | ( "u" , hex_digit , hex_digit , hex_digit , hex_digit ) ) ;
mac_address             = hex_byte , ":" , hex_byte , ":" , hex_byte , ":" ,
                          hex_byte , ":" , hex_byte , ":" , hex_byte ;
hex_byte                = hex_digit , hex_digit ;
ip_address              = ipv4_address | ipv6_address ;
ipv4_address            = decimal_int , "." , decimal_int , "." , decimal_int , "." , decimal_int ;
ipv6_address            = ( "::" , { hex_digit | ":" | "." } )
                        | ( hex_digit , [ hex_digit ] , [ hex_digit ] , [ hex_digit ] ,
                            ":" , { hex_digit | ":" | "." } ) ;
oid_literal             = [ "." ] , decimal_int , { "." , decimal_int } | string_literal ;
letter                  = "A".."Z" | "a".."z" ;
digit                   = "0".."9" ;
hex_digit               = digit | "A".."F" | "a".."f" ;
```

---

# Formal GBNF Constrained Decoding Grammar (`frameassembly.gbnf`)

```gbnf
# ============================================================================
# FrameAssembly GBNF Constrained Decoding Grammar (llama.cpp / GGML BNF)
# Usage: llama-server -m model.gguf --grammar-file frameassembly.gbnf
# Enforces 100% syntactically valid FrameAssembly (.fasm) generation across
# all 81 native protocols, L2-L4 modifiers, SNMPv1/v2c/v3 USM, and L7 specs.
# Note: The FrameAssembly compiler accepts all keywords, protocols, modifiers,
# time units, and identifiers case-insensitively; canonical uppercase tokens
# are used here for deterministic LLM constrained decoding.
# ============================================================================

root ::= ws (host-decl | flow-decl)* compile-block (host-decl | flow-decl)* ws

# Whitespace and single-line comments
ws ::= ([ \t\n\r] | "//" [^\n]* "\n")*
ws1 ::= ([ \t\n\r] | "//" [^\n]* "\n")+

# 1. Host Declarations
host-decl ::= "HOST" ws1 ident ws "{" ws host-prop* "}" ws
host-prop ::= ("IP" ws1 ip-addr | "MAC" ws1 mac-addr) ws

# 2. Flow Declarations & Statements
flow-decl ::= "FLOW" ws1 ident ws "(" ws param-list? ")" ws "{" ws frame-stmt* "}" ws
param-list ::= ident ws ("," ws ident ws)*

frame-stmt ::= ident ws direction ws ident (ws1 frame-field)* ws
direction ::= "->" | "<-"

# 3. Compile Block & Loops
compile-block ::= "COMPILE" ws "{" ws run-stmt* "}" ws
run-stmt ::= loop-block | flow-call
loop-block ::= "LOOP" ws1 uint-lit ws "{" ws flow-call* "}" ws
flow-call ::= ident ws "(" ws param-list? ")" ws

# 4. Frame Fields (Protocols, Modifiers & Protocol Attributes)
frame-field ::= protocol-kw
              | universal-mod
              | l2-mod
              | l3-mod
              | l4-mod
              | l2-proto-field
              | l3-proto-field
              | l4-proto-field
              | snmp-proto-field
              | l7-proto-field

# 5. All 81 Native Protocol Keywords
protocol-kw ::= l2-proto | l3-proto | l4-proto | snmp-proto | l7-infra-proto | l7-app-proto | l7-ot-proto

l2-proto ::= "ARP" | "VLAN" | "QINQ" | "LLDP" | "STP" | "LACP" | "EAPOL" | "MPLS"

l3-proto ::= "ICMP" | "NDP" | "IGMP" | "MLD" | "GRE" | "VXLAN" | "GENEVE"
           | "IPSEC" | "ESP" | "AH" | "IKEV2" | "WIREGUARD"
           | "OSPF" | "BGP" | "RIP" | "VRRP" | "HSRP" | "PIM" | "BFD" | "OPENFLOW"

l4-proto ::= "TCP" | "UDP" | "SCTP"

snmp-proto ::= "SNMP1" | "SNMP2" | "SNMP3"

l7-infra-proto ::= "DNS" | "MDNS" | "DHCP" | "NTP" | "PTP" | "RADIUS"
                 | "TACACS" | "SYSLOG" | "NETFLOW" | "IPFIX" | "SFLOW"

l7-app-proto ::= "TFTP" | "FTP" | "SSH" | "TELNET" | "HTTP" | "HTTP2" | "GRPC"
               | "WEBSOCKET" | "TLS" | "QUIC" | "STUN" | "SIP" | "RTP" | "RTSP"
               | "SMTP" | "IMAP" | "POP3" | "KERBEROS" | "LDAP" | "SMB" | "NFS"
               | "REDIS" | "MEMCACHED" | "MYSQL" | "POSTGRES" | "MQTT" | "COAP"
               | "AMQP" | "SSDP" | "WHOIS"

l7-ot-proto ::= "MODBUS" | "BACNET" | "DNP3" | "S7COMM" | "ETHERNETIP" | "OPCUA"

# 6. Universal & Layer 2-4 Modifiers
universal-mod ::= "WAIT" ws1 duration-lit
                | "PAYLOAD" ws1 string-lit
                | "HEXPAYLOAD" ws1 hex-string-lit

l2-mod ::= "SRCMAC" ws1 mac-addr
         | "DSTMAC" ws1 mac-addr
         | "ETHERTYPE" ws1 uint-lit
         | "VLAN" (ws1 uint-lit)?
         | "PCP" ws1 uint-lit
         | "DEI" ws1 uint-lit
         | "QINQ" (ws1 uint-lit)?
         | "INNER_VLAN" ws1 uint-lit
         | "MPLS" (ws1 uint-lit)?
         | "LABEL" ws1 uint-lit
         | ("EXP" | "TC") ws1 uint-lit
         | "BOS" ws1 uint-lit
         | "MPLS_TTL" ws1 uint-lit

l3-mod ::= "TTL" ws1 uint-lit
         | "DSCP" ws1 uint-lit
         | "ECN" ws1 uint-lit
         | "FLOWLABEL" ws1 uint-lit
         | "IPID" ws1 uint-lit
         | "DF"
         | "MF"
         | "FRAGOFFSET" ws1 uint-lit
         | "NEXT_HEADER" ws1 uint-lit

l4-mod ::= "SRCPORT" ws1 uint-lit
         | "DSTPORT" ws1 uint-lit
         | "TRANSPORT" ws1 ("TCP" | "UDP")
         | tcp-flag
         | "SEQ" ws1 uint-lit
         | "ACKNUM" ws1 uint-lit
         | ("WIN" | "WINDOW") ws1 uint-lit
         | "URGENT" ws1 uint-lit
         | "MSS" ws1 uint-lit
         | "WSCALE" ws1 uint-lit
         | "SACK_PERM" | "SACKPERM"
         | "TSVAL" ws1 uint-lit
         | "TSECR" ws1 uint-lit

tcp-flag ::= "SYN" | "ACK" | "FIN" | "RST" | "PSH" | "URG" | "ECE" | "CWR"

# 7. Layer 2 Protocol Sub-Keywords
l2-proto-field ::= "REQUEST"
                 | "REPLY" (ws1 string-lit)?

                 | "HELLO" | "FEATURES_REQ" | "FEATURES_REPLY" | "PACKET_IN" | "PACKET_OUT" | "FLOW_MOD" | "ECHO_REQ" | "ECHO_REQUEST" | "ECHO_REPLY"
                 | "AUTHEN" | "AUTHOR" | "ACCT" | str-or-ident)

                 | "EAP_CODE" ws1 uint-lit

                 | "CIP_CLASS" ws1 uint-lit
                 | "CIP_INSTANCE" ws1 uint-lit
                 | "CIP_ATTR" ws1 uint-lit
                 | "CHUNK_TYPE" ws1 str-or-ident
                 | "SECURE_CHANNEL_ID" ws1 uint-lit
                 | "TOKEN_ID" ws1 uint-lit
                 | "SEQ_NUM" ws1 uint-lit
                 | "ENDPOINT_URL" ws1 str-or-ident
                 | "NODE_ID" ws1 str-or-ident

# 12. Lexical Terminals
str-or-ident ::= string-lit | ident
ident ::= [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]*
uint-lit ::= [0-9]+ | "0" [xX] [0-9a-fA-F]+
int-lit ::= "-"? [0-9]+ | "0" [xX] [0-9a-fA-F]+
duration-lit ::= uint-lit ("ns" | "us" | "ms" | "s" | "m")
string-lit ::= "\"" ([^"\\] | "\\" (["\\/bfnrt'] | "x" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} | "u" [0-9a-fA-F]{4}))* "\""
hex-string-lit ::= "\"" [0-9a-fA-F: ]* "\""
mac-addr ::= [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2} ":" [0-9a-fA-F]{2}
ip-addr ::= ipv4-addr | ipv6-addr
ipv4-addr ::= [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+
ipv6-addr ::= "::" [0-9a-fA-F:.]* | [0-9a-fA-F]{1,4} (":" [0-9a-fA-F:.]*)+
oid-lit ::= "."? [0-9]+ ("." [0-9]+)* | string-lit
```

---

# Formal Lark Earley/LALR Constrained Decoding Grammar (`frameassembly.lark`)

```lark
// ============================================================================
// FrameAssembly Lark Grammar (Outlines / vLLM / Guidance / XGrammar / llguidance)
// Synchronized with src/lexer/mod.rs, grammar.ebnf, and frameassembly.gbnf.
// Covers all 81 native protocols, L2-L4 modifiers, SNMPv1/v2c/v3 USM, and L7.
// Note: The FrameAssembly compiler accepts all keywords, protocols, modifiers,
// time units, and identifiers case-insensitively; canonical uppercase tokens
// are used here for deterministic LLM constrained decoding.
// ============================================================================

start: top_level_decl* compile_block top_level_decl*

top_level_decl: host_decl
              | flow_decl

// 1. Host Declarations
host_decl: "HOST" IDENT "{" host_prop* "}"
host_prop: "IP" ip_addr
         | "MAC" MAC_ADDR

// 2. Flow Declarations & Statements
flow_decl: "FLOW" IDENT "(" param_list? ")" "{" frame_stmt* "}"
param_list: IDENT ("," IDENT)*

frame_stmt: IDENT direction IDENT frame_field*
direction: "->" | "<-"

// 3. Compile Block & Loops
compile_block: "COMPILE" "{" run_stmt* "}"
run_stmt: loop_block
        | flow_call
loop_block: "LOOP" UINT_LIT "{" flow_call* "}"
flow_call: IDENT "(" param_list? ")"

// 4. Frame Fields (Protocols, Modifiers & Protocol Attributes)
frame_field: protocol_kw
           | universal_mod
           | l2_mod
           | l3_mod
           | l4_mod
           | l2_proto_field
           | l3_proto_field
           | l4_proto_field
           | snmp_proto_field
           | l7_proto_field

// 5. All 81 Native Protocol Keywords
protocol_kw: l2_proto
           | l3_proto
           | l4_proto
           | snmp_proto
           | l7_infra_proto
           | l7_app_proto
           | l7_ot_proto

l2_proto: "ARP" | "VLAN" | "QINQ" | "LLDP" | "STP" | "LACP" | "EAPOL" | "MPLS"

l3_proto: "ICMP" | "NDP" | "IGMP" | "MLD" | "GRE" | "VXLAN" | "GENEVE"
        | "IPSEC" | "ESP" | "AH" | "IKEV2" | "WIREGUARD"
        | "OSPF" | "BGP" | "RIP" | "VRRP" | "HSRP" | "PIM" | "BFD" | "OPENFLOW"

l4_proto: "TCP" | "UDP" | "SCTP"

snmp_proto: "SNMP1" | "SNMP2" | "SNMP3"

l7_infra_proto: "DNS" | "MDNS" | "DHCP" | "NTP" | "PTP" | "RADIUS"

// 12. Lexical Terminals
str_or_ident: STRING_LIT | IDENT | contextual_keyword

contextual_keyword: "CNAME" | "TEXT" | "BINARY" | "PING" | "PONG" | "CLOSE"
                  | "INIT" | "INIT_ACK" | "SACK" | "HEARTBEAT" | "HEARTBEAT_ACK"
                  | "ABORT" | "SHUTDOWN" | "COOKIE_ECHO" | "COOKIE_ACK"
                  | "DATA" | "ACK" | "SYN" | "FIN" | "RST" | "PSH" | "URG"
                  | "SYNC" | "REPORT" | "TRAP" | "INFORM" | "GET" | "GETNEXT" | "GETBULK" | "SET" | "RESPONSE"
                  | "REQUEST" | "REPLY" | "QUERY" | "NOTIFY" | "HELLO" | "OPEN" | "UPDATE" | "KEEPALIVE"
                  | "CONNECT" | "CONNACK" | "PUBLISH" | "SUBSCRIBE" | "DISCONNECT"
                  | "START" | "LOGOFF" | "KEY" | "EAP_PACKET" | "AUTHEN" | "AUTHOR" | "ACCT"
                  | "OK" | "ERR" | "QUIT" | "EHLO" | "HELO" | "DB"

ip_addr: IPV4_ADDR | IPV6_ADDR
oid_lit: OID_LIT | STRING_LIT

IDENT: /[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*/
UINT_LIT: /0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+/
INT_LIT: /-?[0-9]+|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+/
DURATION_LIT: /(?:0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+)(?:ns|us|ms|s|m)/
STRING_LIT: /"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/
HEX_STRING_LIT: /"[0-9a-fA-F: ]*"/
MAC_ADDR: /[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(?::[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5}/
IPV4_ADDR: /[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/
IPV6_ADDR: /::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*|[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}(?::[0-9a-fA-F:.]*)+/
OID_LIT: /\.?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+/

COMMENT: /\/\/[^\n]*/
WS: /[ \t\r\n]+/

%ignore WS
%ignore COMMENT
```

---

# Rust AST Protocol Specifications & Syntax Mappings (`src/ast/`)

- **`src/ast/l2/arp.rs` (`ArpSpec`)**: `ARP [REQUEST | REPLY] [GRATUITOUS] [SENDERMAC <mac>] [SENDERIP <ip>] [TARGETMAC <mac>] [TARGETIP <ip>]`
- **`src/ast/l2/eapol.rs` (`EapolSpec`)**: `EAPOL [VERSION <u8>] [TYPE <EAP_PACKET | START | LOGOFF | KEY>] [EAP_CODE <u8>] [EAP_ID <u8>] [EAP_METHOD <u8>] [IDENTITY "<str>"]`
- **`src/ast/l2/lacp.rs` (`LacpSpec`)**: `LACP [ACTOR_SYS <mac>] [ACTOR_KEY <u16>] [ACTOR_PORT <u16>] [ACTOR_STATE <u8>] [PARTNER_SYS <mac>] [PARTNER_KEY <u16>] [PARTNER_PORT <u16>] [PARTNER_STATE <u8>]`
- **`src/ast/l2/lldp.rs` (`LldpSpec`)**: `LLDP [CHASSIS_ID "<str>"] [PORT_ID "<str>"] [TTL <u16>] [SYSNAME "<str>"] [SYSDESC "<str>"]`
- **`src/ast/l2/mod.rs` (`L2Modifiers`)**: `[SRCMAC <mac>] [DSTMAC <mac>] [ETHERTYPE <u16>] [VLAN <vid> [PCP <pcp>] [DEI <dei>]] [QINQ <svid> [INNER_VLAN <cvid>]] [MPLS <label> [EXP <tc>] [BOS <s_bit>] [MPLS_TTL <ttl>]]`
- **`src/ast/l2/mpls.rs` (`MplsSpec`)**: `MPLS <label> [EXP <0..7>] [BOS <0|1>] [MPLS_TTL <u8>]`

# Representative Verified `.fasm` Corpus Examples (All 81 Protocols & Topologies)


## `examples/l2/arp/arp_address_conflict_detection_probe.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 5227 IPv4 Address Conflict Detection (ACD) ARP probe with zero sender IP and subsequent announcement.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ARP, REQUEST, SENDERMAC, SENDERIP, TARGETMAC, TARGETIP, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define newly booting DHCP client probing tentative IPv4 address.
HOST acd_prober {
    IP 192.168.42.77
    MAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define local broadcast segment peer receiving ACD probes.
HOST lan_listener {
    IP 192.168.42.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:00:00:99
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define RFC 5227 ARP probe with 0.0.0.0 SPA followed by ARP announcement.
FLOW acd_probe_and_announce(prober, segment) {
    prober -> segment ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3 SENDERIP 0.0.0.0 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 192.168.42.77
    prober -> segment ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3 SENDERIP 0.0.0.0 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 192.168.42.77 WAIT 1s
    prober -> segment ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 08:00:27:a1:b2:c3 SENDERIP 192.168.42.77 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 192.168.42.77 WAIT 2s
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing IPv4 Address Conflict Detection sequence.
COMPILE {
    acd_probe_and_announce(acd_prober, lan_listener)
}
```

## `examples/l2/arp/arp_anycast_vxlan_distributed_gateway.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: EVPN-VXLAN leaf switch responding to host ARP Request with distributed anycast gateway virtual MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:01.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, VLAN, ARP, REQUEST, SENDERMAC, SENDERIP, TARGETMAC, TARGETIP, WAIT, REPLY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define tenant bare-metal server querying default gateway MAC on VLAN 100.
HOST tenant_bm_srv {
    IP 10.100.1.55
    MAC 00:25:90:10:01:37
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define EVPN-VXLAN leaf switch serving distributed anycast gateway IP 10.100.1.1.
HOST evpn_anycast_leaf {
    IP 10.100.1.1
    MAC 00:00:5e:00:01:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Exchange broadcast ARP Request and unicast ARP Reply with virtual gateway hardware address on VLAN 100.
FLOW arp_evpn_anycast_gw(srv, leaf) {
    srv -> leaf VLAN 100 ARP REQUEST SENDERMAC 00:25:90:10:01:37 SENDERIP 10.100.1.55 TARGETMAC 00:00:00:00:00:00 TARGETIP 10.100.1.1 WAIT 2ms
    srv <- leaf VLAN 100 ARP REPLY SENDERMAC 00:00:5e:00:01:01 SENDERIP 10.100.1.1 TARGETMAC 00:25:90:10:01:37 TARGETIP 10.100.1.55
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the EVPN-VXLAN distributed anycast gateway ARP resolution trace.
COMPILE {
    arp_evpn_anycast_gw(tenant_bm_srv, evpn_anycast_leaf)
}
```

## `examples/l2/eapol/eapol_5g_akaprime_sim_card_authentication.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: IEEE 802.1X EAP-AKA' (EAP_METHOD 50) authentication for a 5G fixed-wireless CPE with USIM credentials.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, EAPOL, VERSION, TYPE, EAP_PACKET, EAP_CODE, EAP_ID, EAP_METHOD, WAIT, IDENTITY, PAYLOAD, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G fixed-wireless CPE supplicant authenticating via EAP-AKA' (Method 50).
HOST cpe_usim_supp {
    IP 10.50.80.15
    MAC 00:26:bb:50:50:0f
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define carrier aggregation switch authenticator forwarding EAP-AKA' to 3GPP AUSF.
HOST carrier_pae_sw {
    IP 10.50.80.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:50:50:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Complete EAP-Identity and EAP-AKA' (Method 50) challenge/response culminating in EAP-Success (Code 3).
FLOW eapol_akaprime_auth(cpe, sw) {
    cpe <- sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 1 EAP_ID 10 EAP_METHOD 1 WAIT 2ms
    cpe -> sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 2 EAP_ID 10 EAP_METHOD 1 IDENTITY "631026000012345@wlan.mnc026.mcc310.3gppnetwork.org" WAIT 5ms
    cpe <- sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 1 EAP_ID 11 EAP_METHOD 50 PAYLOAD "AKA_PRIME_RAND_AUTN_AT_KDF" WAIT 5ms
    cpe -> sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 2 EAP_ID 11 EAP_METHOD 50 PAYLOAD "AKA_PRIME_AT_RES_AT_MAC" WAIT 5ms
    cpe <- sw EAPOL VERSION 2 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 3 EAP_ID 11 EAP_METHOD 50
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the 5G EAP-AKA' USIM port authentication trace.
COMPILE {
    eapol_akaprime_auth(cpe_usim_supp, carrier_pae_sw)
}
```

## `examples/l2/eapol/eapol_authentication_failure_reject.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: IEEE 802.1X authentication rejection emitting EAP-Failure (EAP_CODE 4) for an unauthorized contractor device.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, EAPOL, VERSION, TYPE, START, EAP_PACKET, EAP_CODE, EAP_ID, EAP_METHOD, WAIT, IDENTITY, COMPILE

    IP 10.99.0.200
    MAC b4:b5:2f:99:00:c8
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define NAC-enforced campus switch port denying access.

    IP 10.99.0.1
    MAC 00:1e:14:99:00:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define EAPOL identity check culminating in EAP-Failure (EAP_CODE 4) port block.
FLOW eapol_auth_failure_reject(cli, sw) {
    cli -> sw EAPOL VERSION 1 TYPE START
    cli <- sw EAPOL VERSION 1 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 1 EAP_ID 5 EAP_METHOD 1 WAIT 2ms
    cli -> sw EAPOL VERSION 1 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 2 EAP_ID 5 EAP_METHOD 1 IDENTITY "contractor_temp@external.org" WAIT 3ms
    cli <- sw EAPOL VERSION 1 TYPE EAP_PACKET EAP_CODE 4 EAP_ID 5 EAP_METHOD 1 WAIT 10ms
}

}
```

## `examples/l2/lacp/lacp_5g_upf_dpdk_bond_mode4_hash_distribution.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 5G UPF DPDK poll-mode driver bonding two 100GbE ports via IEEE 802.1AX LACP (state 0x3F fast active collecting/distributing).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, LACP, ACTOR_SYS, ACTOR_KEY, ACTOR_PORT, ACTOR_STATE, PARTNER_SYS, PARTNER_KEY, PARTNER_PORT, PARTNER_STATE, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G UPF DPDK bond0 primary 100GbE interface.
HOST upf_dpdk_bond0 {
    IP 100.64.10.10
    MAC 0c:42:a1:40:0a:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define leaf switch port-channel 10 member interface.
HOST leaf_po10_port {
    IP 100.64.10.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:40:0a:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Synchronize LACP fast timeout (state 63 = 0x3F) and forward GTP-U payload over the active bond.
FLOW lacp_upf_dpdk_bond(upf, leaf) {
    upf -> leaf LACP ACTOR_SYS 0c:42:a1:40:0a:0a ACTOR_KEY 10 ACTOR_PORT 1 ACTOR_STATE 63 PARTNER_SYS 00:1c:73:40:0a:01 PARTNER_KEY 10 PARTNER_PORT 101 PARTNER_STATE 63 WAIT 2ms
    upf <- leaf LACP ACTOR_SYS 00:1c:73:40:0a:01 ACTOR_KEY 10 ACTOR_PORT 101 ACTOR_STATE 63 PARTNER_SYS 0c:42:a1:40:0a:0a PARTNER_KEY 10 PARTNER_PORT 1 PARTNER_STATE 63
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the 5G UPF DPDK Mode 4 LACP synchronization trace.
COMPILE {
    lacp_upf_dpdk_bond(upf_dpdk_bond0, leaf_po10_port)
}
```

## `examples/l2/lacp/lacp_active_initiator_passive_partner.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Passive switch vs Active server LACP negotiation where only the server sets the LACP Activity bit (0x01).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, LACP, ACTOR_SYS, ACTOR_KEY, ACTOR_PORT, ACTOR_STATE, PARTNER_SYS, PARTNER_KEY, PARTNER_PORT, PARTNER_STATE, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Linux bonding server configured in LACP active mode (state 0x3D = 61).
HOST active_linux_bond {
    IP 192.168.120.10
    MAC 52:54:00:78:00:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define access switch configured in LACP passive mode (state 0x3C = 60, Activity=0).
HOST passive_access_sw {
    IP 192.168.120.1
    MAC 00:1b:21:78:00:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define Active-to-Passive LACP negotiation exchange.
FLOW lacp_active_vs_passive(srv, sw) {
    srv -> sw LACP ACTOR_SYS 52:54:00:78:00:0a ACTOR_KEY 120 ACTOR_PORT 1 ACTOR_STATE 61 PARTNER_SYS 00:1b:21:78:00:01 PARTNER_KEY 120 PARTNER_PORT 24 PARTNER_STATE 60
    srv <- sw LACP ACTOR_SYS 00:1b:21:78:00:01 ACTOR_KEY 120 ACTOR_PORT 24 ACTOR_STATE 60 PARTNER_SYS 52:54:00:78:00:0a PARTNER_KEY 120 PARTNER_PORT 1 PARTNER_STATE 61 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing Active/Passive LACP port-channel synchronization.
COMPILE {
    lacp_active_vs_passive(active_linux_bond, passive_access_sw)
}
```

```frameassembly
    MAC 00:1c:73:60:00:02
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Access switch executing UplinkFast failover to backup root port and advertising elevated path cost 3000.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, STP, ROOT_ID, BRIDGE_ID, COST, PORT_ID, MAX_AGE, HELLO_TIME, FORWARD_DELAY, FLAGS, WAIT, COMPILE

    IP 10.12.1.2
    MAC 00:1c:73:0c:01:02

    acc <- dist STP ROOT_ID "4096:00:1c:73:0c:01:01" BRIDGE_ID "8192:00:1c:73:0c:01:02" COST 4 PORT_ID 32770 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 0 WAIT 2ms
    acc -> dist STP ROOT_ID "4096:00:1c:73:0c:01:01" BRIDGE_ID "49152:00:1c:73:0c:01:0a" COST 3004 PORT_ID 32770 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 1
```

## `examples/l2/stp/stp_backbonefast_inferior_bpdu_rlq_recovery.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Distribution switch receiving an inferior BPDU after indirect root link failure and reasserting true Root Bridge identity.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, STP, ROOT_ID, BRIDGE_ID, COST, PORT_ID, MAX_AGE, HELLO_TIME, FORWARD_DELAY, FLAGS, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define distribution switch B losing its direct root link and mistakenly claiming root.
HOST dist_sw_indirect_fail {
    IP 10.15.0.2
    MAC 00:25:90:0f:00:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define peer switch C retaining valid path to Root Bridge A and correcting switch B.
HOST peer_sw_valid_path {
    IP 10.15.0.3
    MAC 00:25:90:0f:00:03
}

// INSTRUCTION: Send inferior self-rooted BPDU from switch B and immediately override with superior Root Bridge BPDU from switch C.
FLOW stp_backbonefast_recovery(sw_b, sw_c) {
    sw_b -> sw_c STP ROOT_ID "32768:00:25:90:0f:00:02" BRIDGE_ID "32768:00:25:90:0f:00:02" COST 0 PORT_ID 32769 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 0 WAIT 5ms
    sw_b <- sw_c STP ROOT_ID "4096:00:25:90:0f:00:01" BRIDGE_ID "32768:00:25:90:0f:00:03" COST 2000 PORT_ID 32770 MAX_AGE 20 HELLO_TIME 2 FORWARD_DELAY 15 FLAGS 0
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the STP BackboneFast inferior BPDU recovery sequence.
COMPILE {
    stp_backbonefast_recovery(dist_sw_indirect_fail, peer_sw_valid_path)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ah/ah_bgp_routing_session_authentication.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 4302 IPsec AH authenticating an inter-domain eBGP control plane session (Next Header 6 TCP).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, AH, SPI, SEQ, NEXT_HEADER, ICV, DSCP, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define autonomous system border router A with IPv4 and MAC address.
HOST asbr_router_a {
    IP 192.0.2.10
    MAC 00:1b:21:aa:10:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define autonomous system border router B validating AH-protected BGP packets.
HOST asbr_router_b {
    IP 192.0.2.11
    MAC 00:1b:21:aa:10:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define bidirectional AH flow protecting TCP Next Header 6 with CS6 DSCP marking.
FLOW ah_bgp_auth_flow(rtr_a, rtr_b) {
    rtr_a -> rtr_b AH SPI 40100 SEQ 1 NEXT_HEADER 6 ICV "112233445566778899aabbcc" DSCP 48 TTL 255 PAYLOAD "BGP_OPEN_AS65001" WAIT 5ms
    rtr_a <- rtr_b AH SPI 40101 SEQ 1 NEXT_HEADER 6 ICV "ccbbaa998877665544332211" DSCP 48 TTL 255 PAYLOAD "BGP_OPEN_AS65002" WAIT 5ms
    rtr_a -> rtr_b AH SPI 40100 SEQ 2 NEXT_HEADER 6 ICV "aabbccddeeff001122334455" DSCP 48 TTL 255 PAYLOAD "BGP_KEEPALIVE_ACK"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the AH-authenticated eBGP routing session flow.
COMPILE {
    ah_bgp_auth_flow(asbr_router_a, asbr_router_b)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: BFD session graceful administrative shutdown signaling State 0 (AdminDown) and Diag 7.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, BFD, STATE, DIAG, MY_DISC, YOUR_DISC, MULT, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define core router entering maintenance window.
HOST core_maint_rtr { IP 172.18.10.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define adjacent peer router receiving AdminDown notification.
HOST core_peer_rtr { IP 172.18.10.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BFD transition from Up (3) to AdminDown (0) with Diag 7.
FLOW bfd_admin_shutdown(maint, peer) {
    maint -> peer BFD STATE 3 DIAG 0 MY_DISC 4010 YOUR_DISC 4020 MULT 3
    maint -> peer BFD STATE 0 DIAG 7 MY_DISC 4010 YOUR_DISC 4020 MULT 3 WAIT 25ms
    maint <- peer BFD STATE 1 DIAG 3 MY_DISC 4020 YOUR_DISC 4010 MULT 3 WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the BFD administrative teardown flow.
COMPILE {
    bfd_admin_shutdown(core_maint_rtr, core_peer_rtr)
}
```

## `examples/l3/bfd/bfd_asymmetric_timer_negotiation.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: BFD asymmetric timer negotiation between fast hardware router and slower software peer.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, BFD, STATE, MY_DISC, YOUR_DISC, MIN_TX, MIN_RX, MULT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define hardware ASIC router capable of 3.3ms intervals.
HOST hw_asic_rtr { IP 10.77.0.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define virtualized software router requiring 250ms minimum RX interval.
HOST sw_vrouter { IP 10.77.0.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define asymmetric BFD timer advertisement and adaptation.
FLOW bfd_asymmetric_timers(hw, sw) {
    hw -> sw BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 6001 YOUR_DISC 6002 MIN_TX 3300 MIN_RX 3300 MULT 3
    hw <- sw BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 6002 YOUR_DISC 6001 MIN_TX 250000 MIN_RX 250000 MULT 5
    hw -> sw BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 6001 YOUR_DISC 6002 MIN_TX 250000 MIN_RX 3300 MULT 3
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the asymmetric BFD timer negotiation flow.
COMPILE {
    bfd_asymmetric_timers(hw_asic_rtr, sw_vrouter)
}
```

## `examples/l3/bgp/bgp4_ipv6_peering.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Border Gateway Protocol 4+ peering over IPv6 using TCP 179 with OPEN and KEEPALIVE messages.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, BGP, OPEN, ASN, HOLDTIME, BGPID, KEEPALIVE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Autonomous System 65001 BGP router.
HOST bgp_peer_a { IP 2001:db8:ffff::1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define Autonomous System 65002 BGP router.
HOST bgp_peer_b { IP 2001:db8:ffff::2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP-4+ session establishment and keepalive flow.
FLOW bgp_peer_flow(a, b) {
    a -> b BGP OPEN ASN 65001 HOLDTIME 180 BGPID 10.0.0.1

    a <- b BGP KEEPALIVE
}

}
```

## `examples/l3/bgp/bgp_add_path_ecmp_multi_nexthop.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 7911 BGP ADD-PATH Route Reflector advertising multiple ECMP next-hops for the same anycast prefix.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, BGP, UPDATE, ASN, PREFIX, NEXTHOP, DSCP, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, KEEPALIVE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP Route Reflector with RFC 7911 ADD-PATH Send capability enabled.
HOST addpath_rr_server {
    IP 10.79.11.1
    MAC 00:1c:73:79:11:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define ingress WAN border router receiving multiple ECMP paths for 10.200.200.1/32.
HOST addpath_edge_client {
    IP 10.79.11.10
    MAC 00:1c:73:79:11:0a
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define sequential BGP UPDATE messages advertising distinct NEXTHOPs for the same anycast /32 prefix.
FLOW bgp_add_path_ecmp_flow(rr, client) {
    rr -> client BGP UPDATE ASN 65000 PREFIX "10.200.200.1/32" NEXTHOP 10.1.1.1 DSCP 48 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "PATH_ID_1_LEAF_A" WAIT 3ms
    rr -> client BGP UPDATE ASN 65000 PREFIX "10.200.200.1/32" NEXTHOP 10.1.1.2 DSCP 48 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "PATH_ID_2_LEAF_B" WAIT 3ms
    rr -> client BGP UPDATE ASN 65000 PREFIX "10.200.200.1/32" NEXTHOP 10.1.1.3 DSCP 48 TTL 64 PAYLOAD "PATH_ID_3_LEAF_C" WAIT 3ms
    rr <- client BGP KEEPALIVE DSCP 48 TTL 64
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the RFC 7911 BGP ADD-PATH ECMP advertisement flow.
COMPILE {
    bgp_add_path_ecmp_flow(addpath_rr_server, addpath_edge_client)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: RFC 4303 Section 3.4.3 IPsec ESP anti-replay 64-packet sliding window verification under out-of-order delivery.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ESP, SPI, SEQ, IV, ICV, NEXT_HEADER, DF, TTL, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

    MAC 00:22:bd:50:99:02
}

FLOW esp_anti_replay_window_test(tx, rx) {
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 100 IV "0000000000000064" ICV "010101010202020203030303" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_100_IN_ORDER" WAIT 2ms
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 103 IV "0000000000000067" ICV "040404040505050506060606" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_103_ADVANCE_TOP" WAIT 2ms
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 101 IV "0000000000000065" ICV "070707070808080809090909" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_101_WINDOW_HIT" WAIT 2ms
    tx -> rx ESP SPI 99001 SEQ 102 IV "0000000000000066" ICV "0a0a0a0a0b0b0b0b0c0c0c0c" NEXT_HEADER 4 DF TTL 64 PAYLOAD "ESP_PKT_SEQ_102_WINDOW_FILL"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the ESP anti-replay sliding window out-of-order test flow.
COMPILE {
    esp_anti_replay_window_test(multipath_esp_tx, multipath_esp_rx)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ikev2/ikev2_cloud_vpc_redundant_tunnel_bringup.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Enterprise edge router establishing primary IKEv2 SA_INIT and AUTH tunnel with a cloud VPC VPN gateway.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DSCP, IKEV2, SA_INIT, INITIATOR_SPI, RESPONDER_SPI, MSGID, FLAGS, NEXT_PAYLOAD, WAIT, EXCHANGE, AUTH, COMPILE

HOST onprem_vpn_edge {
    IP 198.51.100.45
    MAC 00:1c:73:c6:64:2d
}

HOST cloud_vpc_vgw {
    IP 203.0.113.200
    MAC 00:1c:73:cb:71:c8
}

// INSTRUCTION: Complete four-message IKE_SA_INIT and IKE_AUTH negotiation between on-premises edge and cloud VGW.
FLOW ikev2_cloud_vpc_setup(edge, vgw) {
    edge -> vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 SA_INIT INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 0 MSGID 0 FLAGS 8 NEXT_PAYLOAD 33 WAIT 10ms
    edge <- vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 SA_INIT INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 92003002 MSGID 0 FLAGS 32 NEXT_PAYLOAD 33 WAIT 10ms
    edge -> vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 EXCHANGE AUTH INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 92003002 MSGID 1 FLAGS 8 NEXT_PAYLOAD 46 WAIT 10ms
    edge <- vgw DSCP 48 IKEV2 EXCHANGE AUTH INITIATOR_SPI 91002001 RESPONDER_SPI 92003002 MSGID 1 FLAGS 32 NEXT_PAYLOAD 46
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the cloud VPC IKEv2 SA_INIT and AUTH negotiation trace.
COMPILE {
    ikev2_cloud_vpc_setup(onprem_vpn_edge, cloud_vpc_vgw)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ipsec/ipsec_5g_n3iwf_untrusted_wifi_backhaul.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: 5G Non-3GPP InterWorking Function (N3IWF) IPsec tunnel protecting NAS and UPF user-plane traffic.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, DSCP, IPSEC, SPI, SEQ, NEXT_HEADER, IV, ICV, PAYLOAD, WAIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G User Equipment (UE) connected over untrusted WLAN access.
HOST ue_wlan_client {
    IP 192.0.2.115
    MAC 00:26:bb:02:00:73
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define 5G core N3IWF security gateway terminating untrusted non-3GPP IPsec tunnels.
HOST core_n3iwf_gw {
    IP 198.51.100.250
    MAC 00:26:bb:64:00:fa
}

// INSTRUCTION: Exchange bidirectional IPsec ESP packets carrying encapsulated inner IPv4 user-plane payloads.
FLOW ipsec_n3iwf_userplane(ue, n3iwf) {
    ue -> n3iwf DSCP 46 IPSEC SPI 700101 SEQ 10 NEXT_HEADER 4 IV "a1a2a3a4a5a6a7a8" ICV "b1b2b3b4b5b6b7b8b9babbbc" PAYLOAD "5g_ul_pdu_session_gre_encap" WAIT 5ms
    ue <- n3iwf DSCP 46 IPSEC SPI 700202 SEQ 10 NEXT_HEADER 4 IV "c1c2c3c4c5c6c7c8" ICV "d1d2d3d4d5d6d7d8d9dadbdc" PAYLOAD "5g_dl_pdu_session_gre_encap"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the 5G N3IWF IPsec tunnel user-plane exchange.
COMPILE {
    ipsec_n3iwf_userplane(ue_wlan_client, core_n3iwf_gw)
}
```

## `examples/l3/mld/mld_all_routers_multicast_leave.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Capture multiple IPv6 hosts reporting multicast group membership and one host sending MLD Done to all-routers multicast
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, MLD, REPORT, MULTICAST_ADDR, MAX_RESP_DELAY, SRCMAC, DSTMAC, TTL, WAIT, DONE, QUERY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the first cluster node participating in an IPv6 multicast group
HOST cluster_node_1 {
    IP fe80::10:1
    MAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the second cluster node participating in the same IPv6 multicast group
HOST cluster_node_2 {
    IP fe80::10:2
    MAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:02
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the IPv6 multicast router on the cluster network
HOST cluster_mrouter {
    IP fe80::10:fe
    MAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:fe
}

// INSTRUCTION: Both nodes report membership, node 1 leaves to 33:33:00:00:00:02, and node 2 re-confirms
FLOW mld_cluster_leave_sequence(n1, n2, rtr) {
    n1 -> rtr MLD REPORT MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:01 DSTMAC 33:33:c1:00:00:01 TTL 1 WAIT 10ms
    n2 -> rtr MLD REPORT MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:02 DSTMAC 33:33:c1:00:00:01 TTL 1 WAIT 30ms
    n1 -> rtr MLD DONE MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:01 DSTMAC 33:33:00:00:00:02 TTL 1 WAIT 10ms
    rtr -> n2 MLD QUERY MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 1000 TTL 1 WAIT 10ms
    n2 -> rtr MLD REPORT MULTICAST_ADDR ff05::c100:1 MAX_RESP_DELAY 0 SRCMAC 00:16:3e:c9:10:02 DSTMAC 33:33:c1:00:00:01 TTL 1
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the cluster multicast leave and re-confirmation trace
COMPILE {
    mld_cluster_leave_sequence(cluster_node_1, cluster_node_2, cluster_mrouter)
}
```

## `examples/l3/ndp/ndp_anycast_gateway_evpn_mac_mobility.fasm`

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: EVPN-VXLAN distributed anycast IPv6 gateway advertising virtual MAC via Neighbor Advertisement after VM vMotion.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, TTL, NDP, NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT, TARGET, SLLA, WAIT, NEIGHBOR_ADVERT, TLLA, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define destination leaf switch advertising distributed anycast IPv6 gateway address.
HOST evpn_leaf_anycast {
    IP 2001:db8:400::1
    MAC 00:00:5e:00:02:64
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define migrated virtual machine resolving default gateway MAC on new rack.
HOST migrated_vm_v6 {
    IP 2001:db8:400::88
    MAC 52:54:00:40:00:88
}

// INSTRUCTION: Resolve anycast gateway via Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement with Hop Limit 255.
FLOW ndp_evpn_anycast_resolve(leaf, vm) {
    vm -> leaf TTL 255 NDP NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT TARGET 2001:db8:400::1 SLLA 52:54:00:40:00:88 WAIT 5ms
    leaf -> vm TTL 255 NDP NEIGHBOR_ADVERT TARGET 2001:db8:400::1 TLLA 00:00:5e:00:02:64 WAIT 10ms
    vm -> leaf TTL 255 NDP NEIGHBOR_ADVERT TARGET 2001:db8:400::88 TLLA 52:54:00:40:00:88
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the EVPN distributed anycast IPv6 gateway NDP resolution trace.
COMPILE {
    ndp_evpn_anycast_resolve(evpn_leaf_anycast, migrated_vm_v6)
}
```

```frameassembly
// PROMPT: Simulate an OpenFlow controller communicating with switches on both IANA TCP port 6653 and legacy TCP port 6633
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, OPENFLOW, FEATURES_REQ, VERSION, XID, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WAIT, FEATURES_REPLY, DPID, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define the multi-version SDN controller

    IP 10.150.10.1
    MAC 00:25:90:e8:10:01
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the modern switch listening on TCP port 6653
HOST modern_sw {
    IP 10.150.10.11
    MAC 00:25:90:e8:10:11
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define the legacy switch listening on TCP port 6633
HOST legacy_sw {
    IP 10.150.10.12
    MAC 00:25:90:e8:10:12
}

// INSTRUCTION: Poll the modern switch on port 6653 and the legacy switch on port 6633
FLOW openflow_custom_ports_poll(ctrl, sw_new, sw_old) {
    ctrl -> sw_new OPENFLOW FEATURES_REQ VERSION 4 XID 101 SRCPORT 52100 DSTPORT 6653 WAIT 10ms
    sw_new -> ctrl OPENFLOW FEATURES_REPLY VERSION 4 XID 101 DPID 1001 SRCPORT 6653 DSTPORT 52100 WAIT 15ms
    ctrl -> sw_old OPENFLOW FEATURES_REQ VERSION 1 XID 201 SRCPORT 52101 DSTPORT 6633 WAIT 10ms
    sw_old -> ctrl OPENFLOW FEATURES_REPLY VERSION 1 XID 201 DPID 2002 SRCPORT 6633 DSTPORT 52101
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile the dual-port OpenFlow discovery sequence
COMPILE {
    openflow_custom_ports_poll(multi_port_ctrl, modern_sw, legacy_sw)
}
```
